- internal/unit/split.go's Split applies §3.4.5 to §3.4.4's clusters: it takes a cluster's hunks in the order the cluster holds them, which already is ascending start order because §3.4.4 partitions one file's hunks on one side and every branch keeps the order of the partition it selects from, and it opens a new unit at the hunk whose changed lines would carry the running count past cluster.max_lines. A cluster inside the cap runs the same loop and comes back whole, so there is no branch on whether the cap binds, and the cluster at exactly the cap is not a case such a branch could be written wrong at.
- cluster.max_lines is registered in internal/config/config.go's §2.7 settings table with its default of 80, the only place the number lives. internal/unit's tests read it through config.Resolve, and TestTheMaxLinesDefaultComesFromTheSettingsTable pins both the default and that a layer above it reaches the key, which a name absent from the table could not.
- A hunk whose own changed lines exceed the cap becomes one unit and carries Cluster.Oversized, which Split sets and §3.4.4 forms no cluster carrying. It is the one place the limit does not bind because there is nothing below a hunk to split, and a unit cut at a line the diff never marked would give §3.4.6 a hunk range no hunk has.
- The flag reaching the coverage report is §10.1.1's sentence and belongs to the still-open status-coverage-report task. Reported rather than claimed: this task records the flag on the unit, and no reader of units.ndjson renders a report yet.
- TestASplittableClusterOpensAUnitAtTheHunkThatWouldNotFit covers the splittable cluster at the boundary the rule turns on. Fifty and thirty changed lines reach the cap exactly and stay together, and the single line after them is the first that would exceed it, so an implementation splitting at reaches-the-limit rather than exceeds-it leaves three units where two are right.
- TestAHunkOverTheCapAloneIsOneOversizedUnit covers the unsplittable oversized hunk with an ordinary hunk on either side of it, neither flagged, and adds a second cluster whose one hunk sits at exactly the cap and is a plain unit, which is the same boundary from the other side. go test -race, golangci-lint and scripts/deadcode.sh are all green.
Out of scope: §3.4.6's unit record and unit hash, the round-scoped id ordering, and §10.1.1's coverage report are each their own task.

tasks.title: Record unit fields with the hash
tasks.acceptance:
- Every unit records an id of the form u<n>, its file paths, its hunk ranges, its changed line count, a unit hash, and whether it was formed by symbol, by adjacency, or by fallback, per §3.4.6.
- The unit hash is the normalised hash per §1.4 of the unit's changed lines taken file by file in ascending path order and, within a file, ascending line order, joined by LF.
- A test fixes the hash for a known unit and asserts it changes when a changed line changes.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/unit/unit.go's Unit records every field §3.4.6 names: the round-scoped u<n> id, the file path, the hunk ranges, the changed line count, the unit hash, and the Formation the §3.4.4 branch that formed it put on the cluster, together with §3.4.5's oversized flag and the side the unit's lines are numbered on, which §3.4.4 makes a fact about a unit and the id ordering needs. Units numbers them u1 upwards over §3.4.5's clusters and returns §1.4 step 1's error rather than hashing bytes it could not decode.
- Path is singular, and that is a claim about §3.4.4 rather than a shortening of §3.4.6. §3.4.6 writes "its file paths" and §6.2.1 writes "path is one of that unit's file paths", but every branch of §3.4.4 says "same file" before anything else, so the set both sentences range over always holds one element; a []string would advertise a shape no diff produces and give every reader a loop, an ordering rule and an empty case for a second path that never arrives. The plural survives where it is real: the hash's "file by file in ascending path order" is that rule for a set of one, and §6.2.1's membership test is an equality.
- The hunk ranges are head-side, from git.Hunk.HeadRange, because §6.2.1 evaluates containment entirely in head coordinates against the head-side range of one of a unit's hunks and, for a hunk that adds no lines, its head-side insertion point. A record keeping merge-base numbers would look right on a one-sided fixture and put every §6.2.1 answer one file version out.
- The unit hash routes through text.NormalisedHash, the fenced entry point, and is taken over the unit's changed lines joined by LF once — the shape finding.AnchorContentHash uses, so a per-hunk pre-image cannot drift away from it. Both orderings the sentence names are the order the hunks already hold: a unit has one file, §3.4.4 partitions before it compares and every branch keeps the partition's order, and ParseHunks keeps a hunk's changed lines ascending.
- TestAUnitRecordsTheFieldsSection346Names asserts every field over the fixture giving all three formations, with the hash lifted out and its shape checked. TestTheUnitHashIsSection14sValueOverTheUnitsChangedLines pins 3040505c498fab51 as a literal and asserts the value is not d1537a8b7cf8801f, which is the equally well-formed value a site that skipped Normalise would produce; it then changes a line in the last hunk and asserts the hash moves, and re-indents the same code and asserts it does not. internal/cli/record.go's placeholder roundUnit is gone: it now embeds unit.Unit beside state.Stamp, and the closed record-command task's tests needed no change.
Out of scope: the total id ordering with its side tiebreak, the single-path pinning test, §6.2.1's containment predicate, and writing units.ndjson from cr brief are each their own task.

tasks.title: Order unit ids with side tiebreak
tasks.acceptance:
- Unit ids are round-scoped, assigned in ascending order of first file path then first changed line, and are not carried across rounds, per §3.4.6.
- Round 8 finding non-total-ordering: the id ordering is the one comparison that ranges over both sides at once, so it carries a side tiebreak — first file path ascending, then side with LEFT before RIGHT matching §8.3.3's convention, then first changed line ascending. Without it a file holding both a RIGHT-sided and a LEFT-sided unit yields two units whose first changed line is the same number in two coordinate spaces, the ordering is not total, and §2.1.1's reproducibility fails.
- Round 8 finding vacuous-multi-file-unit: since every branch of §3.4.4 clusters within one file, a unit carries exactly one file path. The implementation pins this — §3.4.6's per-file hash ordering and §6.2.1's path-membership test are written against a single-path unit and a test asserts no constructible diff yields two.
- A test builds a file with a delete-only hunk and an add-only hunk at the same line number and asserts a stable, total id assignment across repeated runs.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/unit/unit.go's Units numbers the units u1 upwards in §3.4.6's assignment order, computed by order and compareClusters. The ids are round-scoped by construction: they are derived from the round's own clusters and read from nowhere, so carrying one across rounds is something this package cannot do rather than something it refrains from doing, and internal/cli's roundUnitIDs already filters units.ndjson by the round on the §2.3.3 stamp.
- Round 8's non-total-ordering is fixed as the finding words it: ascending first file path, then side with LEFT before RIGHT, then ascending first changed line. The side sits between the two keys §3.4.6 names because this is the one comparison in §3.4 ranging over both sides at once; everywhere else §3.4.4's partition has already fixed which file version a number is read in. LEFT before RIGHT is taken from §8.3.3 rather than invented, so cr sorts by side in one direction wherever it sorts by side.
- Without it two units of one file can tie on a number that means two different lines, and the winner is whichever clustering happened to hand over first, which §2.1.1 does not allow because that is not a property of the inputs. Measured, not argued: deleting the side comparison and re-running TestUnitIdsOrderLeftBeforeRightAtTheSameLineNumber turns the side sequence LEFT LEFT RIGHT RIGHT into RIGHT LEFT RIGHT LEFT, and the comparison is stable-sorted so a pair no key separates still keeps the order the diff fixed.
- Round 8's vacuous-multi-file-unit is pinned by the type: Unit.Path is one string, because every branch of §3.4.4 says same file before it says anything else. §3.4.6's per-file hash ordering is that rule for a set of one and §6.2.1's path-membership test is an equality, and a []string would advertise a shape no diff produces while giving every reader a loop, an ordering rule and an empty case for a second path that never arrives.
- The no-two-paths assertion is more than a spot check in two ways. Structurally, sided.cluster is the only place a Cluster is built and it takes the path from the partition rather than from the hunks, so a unit spanning two files is not a value the package can construct. Empirically, TestNoDiffPutsTwoFilesInOneUnit enumerates a closed space rather than a fixture: two files, each with two positions, each holding an addition, a removal or nothing, which is all eighty-one combinations and so every arrangement of files and sides the clustering can be handed, and every one is checked for hunks of a foreign file, for the id order, and for equality with a second run.
- TestUnitIdsOrderLeftBeforeRightAtTheSameLineNumber builds the file the finding describes. A twelve-line removal pulls the head numbers eleven behind the base, so a later addition lands on head 53 while an earlier deletion removed merge-base 53, and the fixture asserts the collision before asserting the order; the leading addition puts the RIGHT clusters ahead of the LEFT ones on the way in, so an ordering leaning on the order it was handed would keep them there. The whole unit list is asserted to be identical on a second run.
- gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 645, Lived 13, Not covered 41, Timed out 6, efficacy 98.02 percent, up from 624 and 97.96. internal/unit alone is Killed 37, Lived 0, Not covered 0. The run first surfaced two new survivors, both the "is a unit open?" boundaries in split.go, and both were real: a cluster that is only an oversized hunk has nothing open on either side of it, and a split closing a unit it never opened would emit a hunkless unit there and nowhere else. TestAHunkOverTheCapAloneIsOneOversizedUnit gained that cluster and both are killed. The thirteen remaining Lived and the forty-one Not covered are the pre-existing set, unchanged.
Out of scope: §6.2.1's containment predicate, unit-to-claim mapping, §10.1.1's coverage report, and writing units.ndjson from cr brief are each their own task.

tasks.title: Ingest every existing review thread
tasks.acceptance:
- All existing review threads on the PR are ingested, including resolved ones, with author, body, anchor, resolution state, and replies, per §3.5.1.
- Threads are stored in threads.ndjson per §2.3.
- A test ingests a PR carrying resolved and unresolved threads and asserts both survive.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Every existing review thread on the pull request is ingested with author, body, anchor, resolution state and replies (§3.5.1): internal/gh/threads.go asks GitHub's GraphQL API for reviewThreads, the only place isResolved exists at all — REST's pull request review comments carry no resolution, so a resolved thread could only be guessed at — and walks both connections, following further pages of threads by cursor and a long thread's further comments by node id, so nothing is silently truncated; a thread keeps its opening comment as its author and body, the rest as replies, and its anchor normalised into path, side, start_line and line in git.Side terms §3.5.3 can compare against a hunk, with the original pair kept for an outdated thread whose current line GitHub reports null.
- Threads are stored in threads.ndjson per §2.3: gh.WriteThreads names that file once and writes it through internal/state's WriteRecords, the writer for the files §2.3.3 does not stamp with head and round, under the §2.3.1 lock, and TestThreadsAreStoredInThreadsNdjson round-trips the ingest and pins the empty reply list as [] rather than null per §12.3.
- A test ingests a pull request carrying resolved and unresolved threads and asserts both survive: TestIngestionKeepsResolvedAndUnresolvedThreadsAlike replays the recorded payload of cli/cli#11451 — one resolved bot thread, one unresolved human thread with a reply — and asserts both threads, their ids, authors, bodies, anchors, replies and resolution states; every test in internal/gh runs offline, from fixtures under testdata captured once by hand from public pull requests and replayed through the injectable Runner seam, with a shell stub named gh on PATH for the three tests that exercise the real invocation, its allowlisted environment and its failure shape.

tasks.title: Tag threads as human or bot
tasks.acceptance:
- Each thread is tagged with an author type of human or bot, per §3.5.2.
- cr never assigns a class to an ingested thread, per §3.5.3.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Every ingested thread carries §3.5.2's tag: internal/gh/threads.go adds the AuthorType type with AuthorHuman and AuthorBot, a Thread.AuthorType field serialised as author_type, and authorType(), which Client.thread() applies to every thread it builds, including one whose opening comment is missing. The rule is GitHub's own answer and nothing added to it, so only __typename Bot becomes bot while a User, an Organization, a Mannequin, and an author the API answers null for all become human. That leaves dependabot[bot] posting as a User tagged human, deliberately: reading a [bot] suffix or carrying a login allowlist would be cr deciding whose comment counts, which §2.1 leaves to the agent, and it fails in the expensive direction, because a human wrongly tagged bot loses §3.5.3's attachment and the §3.5.4 suppression built on it, so cr repeats a concern a colleague already raised. TestEveryIngestedThreadIsTaggedHumanOrBot pins the Bot and User threads of the recorded fixture and TestOnlyGitHubsOwnBotTypeIsTaggedBot pins all four judgement cases.
- cr assigns no class to an ingested thread, and the negative is mechanically held rather than merely true today: TestNoIngestedThreadCarriesAClass walks gh.Thread reflectively against threadFields, the exact §3.5.1 plus §3.5.2 field surface with no class among them, and also marshals a Thread and asserts the wire carries no class key, so both a struct field added years from now and a hand-written marshaller fail it. The guard was verified by temporarily adding a Class string field, which failed both assertions before it was reverted. gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 254, Lived 4, efficacy 98.45 percent, the four survivors being the known commented baseline in internal/config and internal/finding, with the new authorType conditional at gh/threads.go:399 killed.

tasks.title: Attach nearby human threads to units
tasks.acceptance:
- cr attaches to every unit the ingested human threads whose anchor falls inside the unit's hunks or within threads.proximity_lines (default 10) of them, per §3.5.3.
- cr never decides suppression itself; it locates the candidate and supplies it.
- A test asserts a bot thread and a thread beyond the proximity window are both left unattached.

tasks.title: Record a finding suppressed by thread
tasks.acceptance:
- The agent decides whether an attached thread already covers a finding. When it does, the finding is recorded in state suppressed carrying suppressed_by with the thread id, and is not drafted, per §3.5.4.
- The decision arrives through the record input, never from a cr-side text match.
- A test asserts a suppressed record never reaches draft.md.

tasks.title: Offer author replies as candidate notes
tasks.acceptance:
- Author replies inside ingested threads are offered as candidate context notes per §3.6, per §3.5.5.
- They are offered, never written: recording one is cr note with source thread.
- A test asserts a reply appears as a candidate without a note file being created.

tasks.title: Append a note against an issue
tasks.acceptance:
- cr note <ISSUE-KEY> "<text>" --source <source> appends a note with an id of the form <ISSUE-KEY>#n<n>, a timestamp, the PR it came from, and the source, per §3.6.1.
- Valid sources are chat, jira, thread, meeting, and other, per §3.6.3; any other value is rejected.
- The context store holds facts that are true about the issue but absent from the tracker.
- Round 11 finding unspecified-flag-requiredness, assigned here: §3.6.1 shows --source in the synopsis but never says it is required. The implementation requires it and rejects an absent or unlisted value with exit code 2.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr note <ISSUE-KEY> "<text>" --source <source> --pr <n> appends the note §3.6.1 requires to ~/.cr/context/<ISSUE-KEY>.ndjson, carrying an id of the form <ISSUE-KEY>#n<n> allocated by internal/note/note.go's NextID as a counter over every note the store already holds, a UTC timestamp, the pull request it came from and the source, all written by internal/note/store.go's Append — TestAppendRecordsTheFieldsTheSpecNames reads all four fields back off disk, TestNextIDCountsOverTheNotesTheStoreHolds pins the n < 1 and non-canonical id boundaries the way finding.NextID does, and the built binary recorded CR-1#n1 and CR-1#n2 against a real CR_HOME.
- Valid sources are §3.6.3's chat, jira, thread, meeting and other, in the order the section names them, exported through internal/note/note.go's Sources as a copy so no caller can widen or reorder the set, and TestTheSourcesAreTheClosedSetTheSpecNames accepts each of the five and pins that order.
- Any other value is rejected by ParseSource, which internal/note/store.go's Append re-runs because Source is a string type any caller can spell, so an unlisted source cannot reach the file by a second route — TestTheSourcesAreTheClosedSetTheSpecNames refuses gossip, Chat, a trailing space and the empty value, and TestAppendRefusesWhatCannotBecomeANote proves a refused note adds nothing to the store and spends no id.
- The context store holds facts true about the issue but absent from the tracker, so it is keyed by issue and never by pull request — internal/state/context.go's LockContext takes an advisory lock named after the issue key rather than §2.3.1's per-PR lock, because §3.6.4 loads the file on every later round and every later pull request resolving to the same key and §9.3.5 exempts it from round scoping, and it publishes by rename so a lock-free reader never sees half a document, with TestNotesAccumulateAgainstTheKeyAndNotThePullRequest recording from two pull requests into one store, TestConcurrentContextWritersSerialise proving eight concurrent writers never allocate one number twice, and TestAnIssueKeyCannotReachOutOfTheContextDirectory keeping Invariant 2 by refusing a key that is not a single name.
- Round 11 finding unspecified-flag-requiredness: §3.6.1 shows --source in its synopsis and never says it is required, and cr requires it, because a note whose provenance is unknown cannot carry the §8.1.6 disclosure every record resting on it must reach the reader with.
- An absent or unlisted --source exits 2 rather than 1, because §11.2 codes 2 a usage error and a flag is part of the invocation rather than data inside a file, and exitCodeFor already returns ExitUsage for any unmapped error so InvalidSourceError needs no mapping of its own — TestNoteRefusesAnAbsentOrUnlistedSourceWithTheUsageCode asserts ExitUsage for a missing flag, an empty value and gossip, and that no store is created.

tasks.title: Store an answer as a note
tasks.acceptance:
- cr answer <pr> <record-id> "<text>" --source <source> appends a note referencing that record, so the answer to a posted question is captured against the issue key rather than lost in a thread, per §3.6.2.
- It does not change the record's state: v0.1 ends at posting per §9, and whether an answer settles a question is a judgement v0.2 makes.
- A test asserts the referenced record's state is byte-identical before and after.
tasks.closed_reason:
- `cr answer <pr> <record-id> "<text>" --source <source>` appends a note referencing that record: internal/cli/answer.go registers the command, note.Answer reads the issue key the pull request resolved to out of its §2.3 meta.json — never a second typing of it, so the answer lands where §3.6.4 loads it — and appends through the same locked critical section `cr note` uses, with the record id on the note as `record`; a pull request cr never briefed refuses with §11.2's code 3, and one that resolved to no issue key under §3.2's fallback refuses with code 1 naming `cr brief --issue`, because §2.2 keys the store by issue and a note filed under no key is a note no round reads.
- It does not change the record's state, and the way that is kept is structural rather than merely untrue today: the answer path never takes the exclusive per-PR lock every write to §2.3's files is a method on, and never opens findings at all — the record id is checked only for the spelling §6.1 gives it, deliberately not resolved, because reading the current round's records would tie the answer to a round §9.3.5 exempts this store from and refuse a true answer arriving after the next round opened. TestAnswerHasNoRouteToARecordsState reads internal/cli/answer.go and every non-test file of internal/note and fails on any mention of the lock constructor, the three writers that are methods on it, or the two record files.
- A test asserts the referenced record's state is byte-identical before and after: TestAnAnswerLeavesTheAnsweredRecordByteIdentical writes a posted question into findings.ndjson, runs the command through the root, compares the whole file byte for byte, and then asserts the answer really was recorded so the comparison is about a run that happened rather than one that refused early.

tasks.title: Print accumulated notes with provenance
tasks.acceptance:
- cr context <ISSUE-KEY> prints the accumulated notes with provenance, per §3.6.5.
- Notes for the issue key are loaded automatically on every subsequent round and every subsequent PR that resolves to the same key, per §3.6.4.
- A test asserts a note recorded against PR 1 loads for PR 2 sharing the issue key.
tasks.closed_reason:
- `cr context <ISSUE-KEY>` prints every note the issue's store holds with its provenance per §3.6.5: internal/cli/context.go emits the whole stored record — the id §3.3.2 cites and §3.6.6 retracts by, the text, the source §8.1.6 discloses, the pull request the fact came from, the timestamp, and §3.6.2's answered record — through internal/cli/output.go's shared writer, so a pipe gets the notes as JSON and a terminal gets a line of provenance plus a line of text for each, and TestContextPrintsEveryFieldTheStoreHolds compares the printed document against note.Load's own read of the store rather than against a list written in the test, TestATerminalContextNamesEachNotesProvenance pins §12.1's other shape, and TestContextOnAKeyNobodyRecordedAgainstIsNoNotes fixes §12.3's empty [] for a key nobody recorded against.
- Notes for the issue key load on every subsequent round and every subsequent pull request resolving to the same key because the store is keyed by the issue and by nothing else: internal/note/store.go's Load takes an issue key with no pull request and no round, internal/state/context.go's ReadContextRecords reads context/<ISSUE-KEY>.ndjson lock-free per §2.3.2 while §9.3.5 exempts the store from round scoping, TestContextIsAddressedByTheIssueKeyAlone fences that surface by asserting the command declares no flag of its own so a later --pr, --round or --since fails whatever it is called, and TestReadingTheContextStoreCreatesNothing plus TestTheContextStoreIsReadWhileAWriterHoldsTheLock prove the read neither blocks behind a writer nor writes inside ~/.cr — the round half of §3.6.4 has no round machinery to drive yet and is left to notes-auto-loaded.
- TestANoteRecordedAgainstOnePullRequestLoadsForAnother briefs pull requests 1 and 2 under CR-7, records the fact from #1 alone, and reads it back twice from #2's side: `cr answer 2` allocates CR-7#n2, which §3.6.1's counter over the notes the store already holds could only produce having loaded #1's note, and `cr context CR-7` then prints both with #1's pull request still on its note, which is the other half of the claim because the PR field is provenance and is never read as a scope.

tasks.title: Retract a note within the round
tasks.acceptance:
- A note is unverified hearsay and stays revocable. cr note --remove <note-id> retracts one, and any coverage cell or record citing a retracted note is reported as needing re-evaluation in the next round rather than silently retained, per §3.6.6.
- Round 9 finding retracted-provenance-still-posts: retraction takes effect in the round it happens, not only in the next one. On cr note --remove, every current-round record or cell citing that note is re-evaluated immediately — the record is forced to kind: question or blocked from drafting, so a reviewer who retracts a note precisely because they learned it was wrong cannot still have cr draft and cr post --confirm send the assertion built on it. Because v0.1 ends at posting, the next round may never arrive for this pull request.
- Round 9 finding retracted-provenance-still-posts: a record resting on a retracted note no longer has provenance to disclose, so it no longer qualifies for the assertion register and §8.1.6's provenance region is not emitted for a dangling note id.
- The retraction is reported by cr status and in the round summary, in addition to the next-round report §3.6.6 already requires. The record itself is retained so the decision stays auditable.
- A test retracts a note mid-round and asserts the dependent record is a question, is reported, and cannot be posted as a finding.
- Found by context-command, assigned here: a corrupt context NDJSON exits 2 rather than §11.2's 3, shared by cr note, cr answer and cr context because no typed error exists to map. This task touches the same store, so it adds that error and its exitCodeFor branch; a file cr read and could not parse is a file failure, not a malformed invocation.
tasks.closed_reason:
- A note stays unverified hearsay and stays revocable: internal/note/note.go gives Note a `retracted_at` that is nil while the note stands, and §3.6.6's revocation is a mark on the note rather than a deletion of it, so a note nobody has withdrawn and a note that was withdrawn are two states of one record instead of a line and its absence.
- `cr note --remove <note-id>` retracts one and takes no issue key, because note.SplitID reads the store out of §3.6.1's id, and note.Retract marks the note in place with a UTC timestamp under state.ContextLock. Marking and not deleting is the decision this task turned on: §3.6.1 numbers a note by counting the store, so a removed line would hand the retracted note's number to the next one while §3.3.2's claims and §8.1.6's provenance still cite it by id. The cost is that a note retracted precisely because it was wrong keeps its text on disk and keeps printing from `cr context`, under its retraction, which is what lets a later round name the cells and records that rested on it rather than silently retaining them. TestRetractMarksTheNoteAndKeepsItInTheStore reads the marking, the untouched sibling, the retained text and the spent id back off disk, and TestNextIDNeverReusesARetractedNotesNumber pins §3.6.1's counter against a store a retraction has changed.
- The round-9 finding retracted-provenance-still-posts is answered structurally rather than by a check somebody has to remember to run in the right round. internal/note/note.go's StandingOf is derived from the store every time it is asked and is never stamped onto a citing record, and §9.3.5 exempts the store from round scoping, so there is no snapshot for a retraction to arrive too late for and no next round for the consequence to wait in.
- The re-evaluation is therefore immediate rather than scheduled: `cr draft`, `cr post`, `cr status` and the round summary each read note.StandingOf at the moment they run, so a record whose note was retracted after it was recorded reads as retracted the first time any of them looks. TestRetractingANoteMidRoundStopsTheRecordRestingOnIt in internal/cli/note_test.go records a note, establishes that a citation of it stands and may assert, retracts it mid-round through the command, and asserts the same citation no longer stands against the same store.
- That is what makes it correct for v0.1 ending at posting: a consequence held over to the next round is a consequence that never lands, since `cr brief` may never open another round for this pull request, and nothing in this implementation waits for one.
- The register and the provenance region turn on one fact rather than two, which is the second half of the round-9 finding. note.Standing.Stands is a single predicate documented in internal/note/note.go as what §6.3's assertion register and §8.1.6's provenance region both read, and it answers false for a retracted note and for a dangling note id alike, since a record citing either has equally little provenance to disclose. TestAStandingIsWhatACitationOfANoteMayStillDo pins all three standings and the predicate for each, including an id belonging to another issue key.
- The retraction is reported on every surface v0.1 has a reader for today: `cr note --remove` emits the whole note plus a machine-readable `standing` field through internal/cli/note.go's retractResult, its terminal shape names the consequence in words rather than leaving it to be inferred from a timestamp, and internal/cli/context.go renders the retraction into §3.6.5's provenance line so a reader never weighs withdrawn hearsay as though it stood. TestATerminalRetractionSaysWhatNeedsReevaluation and TestContextNamesARetractionInTheProvenance cover both surfaces.
- Retention is what keeps the decision auditable, and it is enforced at the store: note.Retract rewrites the file with the same records in the same order and one field added, so the withdrawn text, its source, its pull request and its number all survive, and TestRetractMarksTheNoteAndKeepsItInTheStore asserts the store still holds both notes afterwards while TestRetractingTwiceKeepsTheFirstDecision asserts a second run keeps the first retraction's moment rather than restamping it.
- The mid-round test is TestRetractingANoteMidRoundStopsTheRecordRestingOnIt, and its doc comment says exactly how far it reaches. It asserts the decision every consequence reads, since there is no record, draft, post, coverage cell, `cr status` or round summary in the tree to drive, and a draft written here to give the test something to fail against would have tested itself. The unreached halves are named below against the tasks that own them.
- Found by context-command and fixed here: a §3.6 store cr found and could not parse exited 2, a malformed invocation, when nothing about the invocation was wrong and no retyping of it could help. It now exits §11.2's 3 through `cr note`, `cr answer` and `cr context` alike, which TestACorruptContextStoreExitsWithTheFileCode in internal/cli/exit_test.go proves through all three commands rather than through one.
- The error and its branch are state.ContextStoreError in internal/state/context.go and the `errors.As` arm in internal/cli/exit.go. The type wraps both ways the store can fail as a file, unreadable and unparseable, and adds no second message, since the wrapped error already names the path and the one-based line the user has to open. The same commit maps note.UnknownNoteError onto ExitValidation beside note.NoIssueKeyError, since an id spelled §3.6.1's way that names no note is a retraction that failed rather than a command line that can be retyped.
- A file cr read and could not parse is a file failure and not a malformed invocation, and the two are kept apart rather than merged: TestACorruptContextStoreExitsWithTheFileCode asserts the corrupt store gets §11.2's 3 and names the file and line, while TestRetractRefusesAnIdThatNamesNoNote and TestTheTwoRowsOfTheNoteCommandDoNotMix assert that a malformed note id, a positional given to the retraction, and an append flag given with it all stay §11.2's 2.
Out of scope: forcing a dependent record to kind question belongs to argued-forcing, and blocking it from drafting to draft-render-command. Neither command exists in the tree, so the forcing is present here only as the decision those two will read.
Out of scope: withholding §8.1.6's provenance region for a retracted or dangling note id belongs to provenance-region. The rule is implemented as note.Standing.Stands and has no caller outside tests yet.
Out of scope: reporting the retraction in `cr status` belongs to status-findings-report and status-coverage-report, and in the round summary to round-summary-writers. It is met here on the two surfaces that exist.
Out of scope: re-evaluating coverage cells citing a retracted note belongs to cells-record-command and cell-record-consistency, and re-evaluating records to record-command.
Out of scope: note.Standing.Stands has only test callers today. When argued-forcing and provenance-region close, it must stop being test-only, per CLAUDE.md's phase-boundary rule 1.
Out of scope: gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 452, Lived 8, efficacy 98.26 percent, with the same eight commented-equivalent survivors and the same three known TIMED OUT as the baseline of Killed 436, Lived 8, 98.20 percent. One new survivor appeared and was closed rather than classified: CONDITIONALS_BOUNDARY on SplitID's `at < 1` lived because no test used a one-character issue key, which commit 200456d pins.

tasks.title: Create per-PR state on first brief
tasks.acceptance:
- Round 8 finding state-file-without-mandated-writer: cr brief creates meta.json with the round index starting at 1 and the recorded head set to the current head, and persists units.ndjson and threads.ndjson for the current round. §3.7's permission to persist derived inputs becomes an obligation, because §4.5.6 and §4.1.6 reject unknown unit ids, §9.3.1 and §9.3.3 read meta.json, and §3.5.3 attaches ingested threads — all treating these files as authoritative.
- Every other command that reads them fails with exit code 4 and a hint naming cr brief when they are absent, rather than recomputing units on the fly.
- A test runs cr review, cr cells record, and cr map record against a PR that was never briefed and asserts all three exit 4 with the hint.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/brief's Run assembles §3.7's payload and persist writes meta.json with round 1 and the recorded head set to the current head (gh's headRefOid, never a local ref), units.ndjson stamped per §2.3.3, and threads.ndjson, under one hold of the §2.3.1 lock; TestAFirstBriefOpensRoundOneAndRecordsTheDerivedInputs asserts all three off disk rather than off the returned payload.
- The persistence is an obligation and not a permission: EnsurePR materialises the whole §2.3 table before the three writes, so §4.1.6's and §4.5.6's unit ids, §9.3.1's and §9.3.3's recorded head, and §3.5.3's ingested threads all have an authoritative file, and the same test asserts every file of state.PRFiles() exists afterwards.
- state.Layout.Briefed is the single door onto §2.3's per-round files: it refuses an absent meta.json and one carrying round 0 alike with state.NotBriefedError, whose message names `cr brief <pr> --repo <owner>/<repo>` per §12.4, internal/cli/exit.go maps it onto §11.2's code 4, and cr claims record and cr record now read the round through it instead of ReadMeta.
- TestACommandReadingPerPRStateBeforeABriefExitsFourNamingBrief runs every registered per-round-state reader against a never-briefed pull request and asserts exit 4 plus the hint; cr review, cr cells record and cr map record are not registered in v0.1 yet, so TestTheCommandsSection37ObligesAreGuardedOrNamedAsAbsent pins all three as absent and fails the moment one is built without an invocation in briefRuns, where the first test then runs it.

tasks.title: Print the six-part orientation payload
tasks.acceptance:
- cr brief assembles and prints, without judgement, all six items of §3.7: PR identity, head SHA, merge base, and the resolved profile with the layer that selected it; the issue key and the source it resolved from, with the issue text or the reason no key was found; the claims of §3.3 and whether the issue text has drifted; the units of §3.4 with file paths, hunk ranges, and unit hashes; the ingested threads of §3.5 and the notes of §3.6; the active, disabled, and unavailable axes with their reasons per §4.5.
- A test asserts all six sections appear in both the text and JSON renderings.
- Carried from the claims chain: six intent functions are test-only on deadcode ./... waiting for this task — ClaimFields, ClaimSources, Unavailable.Disclosure, Intent.Unavailability, Resolve, ResolveKey — plus DetectDrift and ClaimDrift.Drifted. If any is still listed after this closes, the wiring did not happen.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/cli/brief.go's briefResult.Text prints §3.7.1 as one block: the pull request as owner/repo#n with its round, the head SHA, the merge base git.DiffAgainstMergeBase actually diffed against, and the resolved profile with brief.ProfileReport.SelectionLayer naming which of §2.4.1's two mechanisms chose it.

- §3.7.3 prints the claims of §3.3 recorded for the round and intent.DetectDrift's §3.3.3 comparison, one line saying whether the issue text moved and one line per claim saying whether its span still occurs.
- §3.7.4 prints every unit of §3.4 with its id, file path, side, hunk ranges, unit hash, and the §3.4.4 branch that formed it, flagging §3.4.5's oversized exception where it applies.
- §3.7.5 prints the ingested threads of §3.5 with anchor, author and author type and no class of cr's own, and the notes of §3.6 for the issue key with their provenance.
- §3.7.6 prints the active axes and then §4.5.4's disclosures whole, taken from activation.Activation.Disclosures and profile.MissingProfile rather than composed at the call site, and says in words when every axis ran.
- TestTheBriefPrintsAllSixItemsOfSection37 emits one payload carrying all six items through the shared writer in both ModeJSON and ModeText, decoding the document and looking each item up by key on one side and searching for the rendered values on the other; TestARoundWithNothingDisabledSaysSoInBothRenderings covers the empty-disclosure case the first payload cannot.
- Six of the eight named functions came off deadcode ./... — Resolve and ResolveKey through intent.Resolve, Intent.Unavailability and Unavailable.Disclosure through activation.Activate and the printed disclosures, and DetectDrift with ClaimDrift.Drifted through the §3.3.3 comparison; the whole list fell from 201 entries to 107.

tasks.title: Keep brief free of judgement artefacts
tasks.acceptance:
- cr brief is read-only with respect to judgement: it performs no network write and creates no finding, coverage cell, probe, or thread, per §3.7.
- It may compute and persist the derived inputs of §3.3 through §3.6 because those are facts about the PR rather than opinions about it, and §4.6 needs the same unit set.
- A test asserts findings.ndjson, coverage.ndjson, and probes.ndjson are untouched by a brief.

tasks.title: Make brief idempotent at unchanged head
tasks.acceptance:
- At an unchanged head cr brief is idempotent, per §3.7 and §9.3.3.
- When the head has moved it opens a new round per §9.3.3, which is the one case where it changes state.
- A test runs brief twice at one head and asserts the state directory is byte-identical.

tasks.title: Store the claim-to-unit mapping
tasks.acceptance:
- The claim-to-unit mapping is the agent's judgement. cr map record <pr> <file.ndjson> replaces mapping.ndjson for the current round with one {claim, unit} pair per line, rejecting an unknown claim or unit id with exit code 1, per §4.1.6.
- Every rule in §4.1 through §4.4 that speaks of the claims a unit is mapped to reads this file.
- Every unit is mapped to zero or more claims, per §4.1.1.
- Replacement is scoped to the current round; earlier rounds stay intact per §9.3.5.
tasks.closed_reason:

- Earlier rounds stay intact per §9.3.5: briefedForMapping seeds a round-1 pair beside the round-2 claims and units, and both recordings assert that pair survives byte for byte.

tasks.title: Raise an unmapped unit as question
tasks.acceptance:
- A unit mapped to zero claims raises an unmapped-unit item, per §4.1.2.
- An unmapped unit defaults to a question, never a finding, because the most common cause is intent that never reached the tracker, per §4.1.4.
- A test asserts an unmapped unit's record arrives as kind: question even before §6.3's forcing runs.
tasks.closed_reason:
- A unit mapped to zero claims raises an unmapped-unit item: mapping.Unmapped in internal/mapping/join.go derives the units of one round that mapping.ndjson's pairs of that same round map to no claim, reading the pairs and nothing else so §4.1.6 stays the only join, and review.Unmapped in internal/review/unmapped.go raises one UnmappedUnit item per such unit, in the order the units are given; TestAUnitMappedToZeroClaimsOfItsRoundIsUnmapped and TestAUnitMappedToZeroClaimsRaisesAnUnmappedUnitItem assert it, including that a pair from an earlier round does not map this round's unit of the same id.

tasks.acceptance:
- cr attaches the issue key's notes to every unmapped unit, per §4.1.5.
- The agent decides whether a note explains the unit; when it does, the item is not raised and the coverage cell cites the note id.
- cr never decides this by matching text.
- A test asserts a recorded note suppresses the matching unmapped-unit question only when the agent says so, and that the resulting cell carries note_id.

tasks.title: Write unimplemented claims to gaps file
tasks.acceptance:
- A claim mapped to zero units raises an unimplemented-claim entry. It has no code location by construction, so it cannot be a coverage cell — §4.5.5 requires every cell to name a unit — and is instead written to intent-gaps.ndjson carrying claim, round, head, and set_aside_note when §10.2.3 applies, per §4.1.3.
- It is reported by cr status per §10.1.2 and blocks completeness per §10.2.3.
- A test asserts the entry carries all four fields with head and round stamped by cr.

tasks.title: Keep intent gaps out of findings
tasks.acceptance:
- An unimplemented-claim entry never becomes a record in findings.ndjson, and is never drafted or posted: v0.1 has no unanchored comment channel per §1.6.1, per §4.1.3.
- The reviewer raises it with the author out of band and may record the answer as a note per §3.6.
- A test asserts a gap entry reaches cr status and reaches neither draft.md nor the posted payload.

tasks.title: Derive gaps preserving set-aside stamps
tasks.acceptance:
- On each successful cr map record, cr derives intent-gaps.ndjson mechanically as the claims of the current round mapped to zero units, per §4.1.7.
- Round 9 finding derived-state-clobbers-decision: because §4.1.6 permits re-recording the mapping, re-derivation preserves set_aside_note for any claim that is still unmapped, and drops the stamp — reporting that it did — for a claim that has since become mapped. A literal re-derivation would silently discard every set-aside decision the reviewer made and re-block §10.2.3 with no report.

- A test sets a claim aside, re-records the mapping unchanged, and asserts the stamp survives; then maps that claim to a unit, re-records, and asserts the stamp is dropped with a report.
- Round 12 finding derived-file-erases-recorded-decision, re-reported: a literal mechanical re-derivation discards every set_aside_note the reviewer recorded and silently re-imposes §10.2.3's completeness block. The carry-forward rule above is what prevents it.

tasks.title: Set an unimplemented claim aside
tasks.acceptance:
- cr claims set-aside <pr> <claim-id> --note <note-id> stamps set_aside_note on that gap entry after checking the note exists for the PR's issue key, per §4.1.8.
- Judging a claim out of scope is the agent's call, never cr's; cr only validates the note reference.
- A test asserts a set-aside naming a nonexistent note is rejected with exit code 1.

tasks.title: Evaluate units against their mapped claims
tasks.acceptance:
- Each unit is evaluated against the claims it is mapped to, per §4.2.1.
- A correctness finding cites the claim id it violates, per §4.2.2.
- A unit mapped to zero claims is still evaluated for internal defects, per §4.2.3.
- A test asserts a zero-claim unit still produces a prompt on the correctness axis.

tasks.title: Build a head symbol index
tasks.acceptance:
- cr builds a symbol index for the head from the profile's symbols.lang, per §4.3.1.
- For every function, method, or class added by the diff, cr attaches candidate pre-existing symbols drawn from the head symbol index minus every symbol the diff itself declares on a changed line.
- A test asserts a symbol the diff declares never appears as its own candidate.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr builds a symbol index for the head from the profile's symbols.lang per §4.3.1: internal/symbol/head.go's Head lists the head's blobs with git.BlobsAtRevision, keeps the files match.globs owns, reads each with git.BlobLines, and hands them to Build, which scans them with the rule set languages holds for that lang and reports false when cr ships no scanner for it, so a head cr cannot index comes back as no index rather than as an empty one.
- For every function, method, or class added by the diff, cr attaches candidate pre-existing symbols drawn from the head symbol index minus every symbol the diff itself declares on a changed line: internal/reinvention/attach.go's Attach intersects the index with the diff's RIGHT-side changed lines, partitions the index into the symbols the diff declared and the pool of everything else, and gives each added symbol its own copy of that pool.
- A test asserts a symbol the diff declares never appears as its own candidate: TestASymbolTheDiffDeclaresIsNeverItsOwnCandidate in internal/reinvention/attach_test.go builds a head declaring three symbols, marks two of them as added by the diff, and asserts each attachment's candidate list holds neither its own name nor the other added symbol's, leaving only the pre-existing one.
- Dogfooded against this repository's own head over cmd and internal: 2106 symbols across 325 files in 4.6 seconds, 1549 functions, 311 methods, 246 classes, and git status --porcelain stayed clean, which is invariant 2 read from outside.

tasks.title: Mark reinvention unavailable without an index
tasks.acceptance:
- When no symbol index can be built, the reinvention half of the convention axis is marked unavailable per §4.5 rather than skipped silently, per §4.3.1.
- The unavailability appears in the coverage report with its reason and survives --quiet per §11.1.
- A test runs the convention axis under the generic profile and asserts the reinvention half is reported unavailable while the rest of the axis still runs.
tasks.closed_reason:
- When no symbol index can be built, the reinvention half of the convention axis is marked unavailable per §4.5 rather than skipped silently, per §4.3.1: internal/reinvention/unavailable.go declares Unavailable with the lens and the reason, and Attach returns it beside the attachments rather than in a second report a caller has to remember to ask for, so the two halves of §4.3.1's one sentence cannot come apart. The lens is profile.ReinventionLens, half of the convention axis and never the axis itself, because §4.3.5 leaves the rest of that axis to the rule corpus of §2.6.
- The unavailability appears in the coverage report with its reason and survives --quiet per §11.1: Unavailable.Disclosure satisfies finding.HonestyDisclosure, which is the shape the writer holding §11.1's exemption consumes, and its text is derived from the two fields so what is printed and what a caller reads as data cannot drift apart. Three states each get their own reason naming what would make the lens run, which are a profile declaring no symbols.lang, a symbols.lang cr has no scanner for, and an index that was asked for and did not arrive.
- A test runs the convention axis under the generic profile and asserts the reinvention half is reported unavailable while the rest of the axis still runs: TestUnderTheGenericProfileTheReinventionHalfIsOutAndTheAxisRuns in internal/reinvention/unavailable_test.go parses the generic profile from the bytes cr ships, asserts activation.Activate keeps the convention axis active, and asserts Attach returns no attachment and exactly one entry whose lens is convention slash reinvention and whose reason names symbols.lang.
- Dogfooded against this repository's own head: with a go profile the diff's 83 added declarations each carried the pre-existing pool, and with symbols.lang cleared the same call attached nothing and printed the disclosure line naming the lens, the section, and the field to set.

tasks.title: Rank candidates by comparison name similarity
tasks.acceptance:
- Candidate ranking works on the comparison name: the symbol name case-folded to lowercase with every _ and - removed, per §4.3.2.
- Similarity is 1 - levenshtein(a, b) / max(len(a), len(b)) over comparison names, counted in Unicode code points, defined as 1.0 when both names are empty.
- A candidate qualifies only when its similarity is at least reinvention.min_similarity (default 0.6) and its declared parameter count equals that of the added symbol. The declared parameter count of a function or method is the number of parameters in its signature; for a class it is the parameter count of its constructor, or zero when it declares none.
- Qualifying candidates are ordered by similarity descending, then path ascending, then line ascending, and cr attaches at most reinvention.max_candidates (default 5).
- Semantic equivalence is the agent's judgement, not cr's; a test asserts cr emits candidates and no verdict.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Candidate ranking works on the comparison name, the symbol name case-folded to lowercase with every underscore and hyphen removed, per §4.3.2: internal/reinvention/rank.go's comparisonName lowercases the name and maps both characters away, and TestTheComparisonNameFoldsCaseAndDropsUnderscoresAndHyphens folds five spellings of one idea to formatmoney while keeping digits and non-ASCII letters.
- Similarity is 1 - levenshtein(a, b) / max(len(a), len(b)) over comparison names, counted in Unicode code points, defined as 1.0 when both names are empty: similarity converts both names to runes before the one-row levenshtein and returns 1 for two empty names, and TestSimilarityIsOneMinusTheNormalisedEditDistance pins kitten against sitting, the empty pair, and değer against deger at 1 - 1/5 rather than the byte figure.
- A candidate qualifies only when its similarity is at least reinvention.min_similarity (default 0.6) and its declared parameter count equals that of the added symbol: rank checks the count as an equality and the score with a greater-or-equal, both keys sit in internal/config's settings table with defaults 0.6 and 5, and TestACandidateQualifiesOnBothTheThresholdAndTheParameterCount rejects the same name at another arity and another name at the same arity and admits a candidate exactly on the threshold.
- The declared parameter count of a function or method is the number of parameters in its signature: internal/symbol's countParams counts the non-empty parameters at the list's own depth, which TestTheParameterCountIgnoresCommasThatAreNotSeparators pins through nested types, quoted defaults, and a trailing comma, and rank compares that count for equality.
- For a class it is the parameter count of its constructor, or zero when it declares none: internal/symbol copies the constructor's count onto the class as it scans, and TestAClassQualifiesOnItsConstructorsParameterCount follows it end to end, offering an added PHP class the existing class whose constructor matches and not the closer-named one that declares no constructor.
- Qualifying candidates are ordered by similarity descending, then path ascending, then line ascending, and cr attaches at most reinvention.max_candidates (default 5): byRank is that three-key comparison and rank cuts after sorting, TestCandidatesAreOrderedBySimilarityThenPathThenLineAndCut asserts the order across a three-way tie, the cut at three, and the same result from the pool reversed, and dogfooded on this repository's head the default ranking attached one to five candidates to 23 of 107 added declarations instead of a 2095-symbol pool.
- Semantic equivalence is the agent's judgement, not cr's: rank uses the similarity only to order and drops it before returning, so what leaves the package is a list of declarations and nothing that says whether any of them is a reinvention.
- A test asserts cr emits candidates and no verdict: TestCrEmitsCandidatesAndNoVerdict asserts the candidate was emitted, that an attachment serialises as exactly added and candidates, and that a candidate serialises as exactly path, line, name, kind, and params, with no score and no verdict.

tasks.title: Default reinvention items to question kind
tasks.acceptance:
- A reinvention item cites the candidate symbol as path:line, per §4.3.3.
- Reinvention items default to kind: question, because the tool cannot know whether the existing symbol was rejected for a reason, per §4.3.4.
- A test asserts the default holds before §6.3's forcing is applied.

tasks.title: Attach mechanical rule hits to units
tasks.acceptance:
- Project conventions beyond reinvention come from the rule corpus of §2.6, never from hard-coded logic and never from prose buried inside role instructions, per §4.3.5.
- A mechanical rule hit is attached to the unit that contains it, so the agent judges an already-located candidate instead of searching for one, per §4.3.6.
- A test asserts a hit outside every unit's hunks is not attached to an unrelated unit.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Project conventions beyond reinvention come from the rule corpus of §2.6, never from hard-coded logic and never from prose buried inside role instructions. TestAnInstallationWithNoRuleFilesEnforcesNoConvention resolves a tree holding no rule file in either §2.2 directory and no rules array in the profile, and asserts the corpus, the matchers, the hits and the injections are all empty: there is no built-in layer for Resolve to add and nothing embedded in the binary, so every rule cr evaluates was written into a file the project owns. Reinvention is the one convention cr computes for itself, and §4.3.1 gives it machinery outside the corpus. The role half was closed by rule-without-detect-injection, whose TestTheRolePackageCannotReadARule refuses an internal/rule import anywhere under internal/role and whose TestNoBuiltinRoleCarriesARuleAsProse holds the shipped roles to §2.5's table.
- A mechanical rule hit is attached to the unit that contains it, so the agent judges an already-located candidate instead of searching for one. internal/rule/attach.go's Attach answers for every unit of the round with the hits inside it, deciding containment through unit.Contains — §6.2.1's own predicate rather than a second reading of what a hunk range means, so a hit cannot be attached against one reading and graded against another. Only a RIGHT-side unit can hold one, because §2.6.1.1 evaluates the added and modified RIGHT-side lines and never the removed ones while §6.2.1 compares no side at all; TestAHitIsNeverAttachedToALeftUnit exercises exactly that overlap, with a deletion whose head-side insertion point falls inside a RIGHT unit's range. Every unit is answered for, carrying §12.3's empty array when no rule matched, because §4.6.1 emits one prompt per role and unit and a unit left out would reach its role indistinguishable from a unit cr checked and found clean.
- A test asserts a hit outside every unit's hunks is not attached to an unrelated unit. TestAHitOutsideEveryUnitIsAttachedToNone covers three ways of being outside: a line in the gap between one unit's two hunks, a line past the last hunk of the file, and a line in a file the round did not change. The gap case is the one with teeth, since an implementation reading only a unit's first and last range would pass every single-hunk fixture and fail there. An unattached hit is not lost: §2.6.1.6 appends every hit to rule-stats.ndjson whatever becomes of it here, and §2.6.1.1 evaluates over the round's own hunks so the case does not arise from a diff at all. What must not happen is the other direction, because §2.6.1.5 has the role confirm a hit before it reaches a draft, and a misplaced hit asks the role to confirm a match about lines it was never in.

tasks.title: Attach changed test files per unit
tasks.acceptance:
- cr attaches to every unit the test files changed or added by the PR and the symbols they reference, per §4.4.1.
- The agent classifies the unit as covered, partially covered, or uncovered, and the classification is recorded in the coverage cell together with the test paths it rested on.
- cr performs no coverage classification of its own, per §2.1.3.
- Round 12 finding missing-unavailability-path, assigned here: §4.4.1's 'the symbols they reference' needs a symbol index the shipped generic profile cannot provide, and §4.4 states no unavailability path the way §4.3.1 does. The implementation marks that half unavailable with its reason through §4.5.4 rather than failing or silently skipping.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/testadequacy/attach.go's Attach builds one round's §4.4.1 attachment out of the diff's hunks, taking the test files from the profile's tests.globs through the new profile.IsTestFile and the symbols they reference from the References interface, and PerUnit hands that same attachment to every unit of §3.4 so 'to every unit' is produced rather than remembered. profile.IsTestFile reads tests.globs as a real glob, with ** standing for any run of path segments, because the shipped laravel-pest glob tests/**/*Test.php read through path.Match alone would select one directory depth and silently withhold the rest of a suite.
- internal/testadequacy/coverage.go carries §4.5.5's coverage value, which is §4.4.1's classification (covered, partially-covered, or uncovered) together with the test paths it rested on, and it round-trips through NDJSON so the cell that stores it and the round that reads it back see one value. The cell itself and the file it is written to belong to coverage-cell-schema and cells-record-command.
- Coverage's two fields are unexported and no exported function takes a Classification, so UnmarshalJSON reading the agent's own line is the only way a classification comes into existence, which is §2.1.3 made structural the way state.Stamp's unexported setStamp is. A value outside §4.4.1's three, the empty string included, is refused rather than defaulted, and nothing in cr derives a classification from an Attachment.
- The symbol half of §4.4.1 needs an index no shipped profile can yet provide, and §4.4 states no unavailability path the way §4.3.1 does. testadequacy.References is its own interface because unit.SymbolIndex answers where a symbol is declared rather than what a file names, and nothing implements it until symbol-index-build.
- Attach marks that half unavailable through §4.5.4 rather than failing the run or returning an empty list cr never established: testadequacy.SymbolLens spells the lens the way profile.ReinventionLens spells §4.3.1's, Unavailable implements finding.HonestyDisclosure so the report survives --quiet per §11.1, both ways the index can be missing are named, and References answers with a bool so a file it cannot read is reported by name instead of collapsing into the same silence. The file half needs no such path: §2.4 makes tests.globs required whenever tests.cmd is present and §4.5.2 disables the test axis when tests.cmd is absent, so generic, which declares neither, never reaches §4.4 at all.

tasks.title: Define role activeness without circularity
tasks.acceptance:
- Round 8 finding circular-definition: a role is active when its axis is active and its profiles list is empty or names the resolved profile. §4.6.4's skip report is the reporting obligation for the negative case, not an input to the definition — otherwise activeness is defined in terms of an output of the command that consumes it, and §4.5.6 and §10.2.2 need the active set independently of whether cr review has run.
- The command that computes and stores meta.json's active-role list is named, and it is the only writer of that field.
- A test computes the active set with cr review never having been invoked and asserts cr cells record and cr status agree with it.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Activation.ActiveRoles in internal/activation/roles.go is the definition: a role is active when its axis is in the round's active set and its profiles list is empty or names the resolved profile, with TestRoleActivenessRestsOnTheAxisAndTheProfileAlone covering both halves of the profiles clause and both kinds of inactive axis.
- §4.6.4 is not an input: the function takes an Activation and a corpus and nothing else, its doc comment records why treating the skip report as a third clause would define activeness in terms of an output of cr review, and TestTheActiveRoleSetIsStoredWithoutAnyFanOut computes and stores the set in a round where no fan-out has run or exists.

- TestTheActiveRoleSetIsStoredWithoutAnyFanOut runs a whole round with cr review never invoked and asserts meta.json's stored list equals the definition applied directly to the same profile and intent; the cr cells record and cr status halves land in cells-record-command and status-coverage-report, which read this stored field rather than deriving a set of their own.

tasks.title: Report every lens that never ran
tasks.acceptance:
- Every lens that did not run appears in the coverage report with its reason: a disabled axis, an unavailable axis, the unavailable reinvention half of §4.3.1, and a role skipped per §4.6.4, per §4.5.4.
- cr never reports a round as complete without stating all of them — a skipped role shrinks the cells §10.2.2 demands, so silence about it would let a complete verdict cover a lens that never looked.
- A test disables one axis, makes another unavailable, skips one role, and asserts all four reasons appear together with the completeness verdict.

tasks.title: Define the coverage cell fields
tasks.acceptance:
- Every cell carries the unit id and role id it sits at, one of pass, finding, question, or na, the head it was filled against, the unit hash of §3.4.6 it was filled for, and a reason when it is na, per §4.5.5.
- It also carries note_id when a note explained an unmapped unit per §4.1.5, and coverage with test_paths when the role is on the test axis per §4.4.1.
- A test asserts an na cell without a reason is rejected.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/coverage/cell.go declares Cell with unit, role, result closed at pass/finding/question/na, the embedded state.Stamp §2.3.3 fills with the head it was filled against, unit_hash for §10.2.2's comparison, and reason; TestACellNamesItsUnitItsRoleAndOneOfTheFourVerdicts and TestACellCarriesEveryFieldSection455Names assert the whole row rather than a field at a time.

tasks.title: Store cells replacing named unit rows
tasks.acceptance:
- Cells are the agent's judgement and reach cr the same way findings do, through cr cells record <pr> <file.ndjson>, which replaces the current round's cell for each (unit, role) the file names and leaves every other cell untouched, per §4.5.6.
- cr rejects with exit code 1 a cell naming an unknown unit id or an inactive role.
- cr never invents a cell for a unit no role reported on — an unfilled cell is a coverage gap per §10.1.1, not something for cr to complete.
- A test records two of four cells and asserts the other two stay unfilled.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr cells record <pr> <file.ndjson> is internal/cli/cells.go, and it writes through the new state.ReplaceStampedKeys, which keys coverage.ndjson by (unit, role) and replaces only the current round's lines at the keys the file names; TestASecondRecordingReplacesOnlyTheCellsItNames records two cells, re-answers one, and asserts the untouched one keeps its first verdict, while TestReplaceStampedKeysRewritesTheNamedKeysAndNoOthers holds the same-unit, same-role, and other-round neighbours in place.

- TestRecordingTwoOfFourCellsLeavesTheOtherTwoUnfilled briefs two units and two active roles, records two cells at different units and different roles, and asserts coverage.ndjson holds exactly those two — the other two stay a §10.1.1 coverage gap.

tasks.title: Compute cell head from owned state
tasks.acceptance:
- Round 8 finding agent-asserted-computed-field: head and the unit hash are computed on the cell. cr cells record stamps both from the current head and from units.ndjson for the named unit id, and rejects with exit code 1 a cell arriving carrying either — the same treatment §6.1.4 gives grade.
- Without this, §10.2.2's completeness check rests on a guard whose input is the very thing being guarded: an agent echoing the current hash makes a stale cell indistinguishable from a fresh one, and P6's coverage is proven reduces to coverage asserted.
- A test records a cell, re-clusters at a changed unit, and asserts the old cell fails §10.2.2's hash comparison automatically.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Both computed fields of a cell are now cr's, and both are refused when an agent writes them. cr cells record already stamped head from the round through state.WriteStamped and unit_hash from units.ndjson through stampUnitHashes, so the values were cr's, but a supplied unit_hash was overwritten in silence rather than rejected. internal/coverage/cell.go's cellChecker.computed closes that: cellComputed names the fields §4.5.5 has cr write onto a cell, presence of the key is the whole test whatever value sits under it, and the refusal goes out as the same state.ReservedFieldError that already carries §2.3.3's head and round, which internal/cli/exit.go maps onto ExitValidation. head keeps its existing guard inside state.DecodeStamped, which owns the pair for all eight files of §2.3.3, so the two halves of the rejection have one wording and one exit code between them.
- The check runs before anything the line says. A cell that supplies unit_hash and names an unknown unit as well is refused for the field it may not carry, because the two faults have different repairs and telling an agent to correct a value it has to drop sends it round the loop a second time. TestASuppliedUnitHashIsRefusedBeforeTheLineIsRead pins that ordering and the one-based line number state.DecodeStamped counts.
- The rejection is what keeps §10.2.2 from resting on its own input. §10.2.2's second condition asks whether every cell was filled for that unit's current unit hash, so the hash is the guard's input and the thing being guarded at once. An agent free to write it could echo the current value onto a verdict reached against older code, a stale cell would then be indistinguishable from a fresh one, and P6's coverage is proven would reduce to coverage asserted. Overwriting a supplied value silently closes the same hole but accepts a file whose author believed they were recording something, which §12.4 asks cr to say out loud instead.
- TestARecordedCellGoesStaleWhenItsUnitIsReclustered is the criterion's test end to end. It clusters one unit through unit.Units, writes it to units.ndjson, records a cell through cr cells record, re-clusters the same unit at a changed line under an unchanged head, and asserts the stored cell still carries the hash it was filled for and no longer matches what units.ndjson holds, which is §10.2.2's comparison failing on its own. The agent's file is byte for byte identical in both recordings and cannot name a hash at all, so nothing chose the staleness. The last assertion is the other half: the same line handed in again picks up the new hash, so cr derives the value at record time rather than carrying a cell forward. The head is asserted unmoved in the same test, because §9.3.1's head comparison alone would have called that round complete.
- Both fixture hashes are §3.4.6's own value, taken over the unit's changed lines by the internal/unit that cr brief runs, rather than two literals written into the test. A test naming two hash strings would prove that two strings are unequal, not that changed code gives a changed unit hash.
- TestACellMayNotSupplyTheFieldsCrComputes covers the decoder over a correct hash, a wrong one, an empty one, a null one and a supplied head, all refused alike, because what is wrong is the authorship rather than the number. TestACellSupplyingAFieldCrComputesExitsOne drives unit_hash and head through the command and asserts §11.2's code 1 and a round left exactly as the refused file found it.
- Reported rather than claimed: no existing test was edited. The new tests live in internal/coverage/computed_test.go and internal/cli/cellcomputed_test.go, beside the closed cells-record-command tests they reuse fixtures from, so that task's assertions stand untouched. Both new tests were watched failing with the guard removed before it was restored.
- Gate: go test -race ./... ok, golangci-lint 0 issues, scripts/deadcode.sh clean, gofmt -l internal empty, no eighth //nolint added. deadcode ./... holds at 92 entries and lists nothing from internal/coverage or internal/cli/cells.go. Mutation with gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 5 --workers 4 ./internal over 17 minutes 17 seconds gives Killed 1341, Lived 23, Not covered 135, Timed out 12, efficacy 98.31 per cent, which is a healthy run rather than the false hundred a --test-cpu run reports. No survivor sits in internal/coverage or internal/cli/cells.go, so this task introduced none, and the dry run beforehand reported every mutant of the changed code RUNNABLE apart from the tagless switch case expressions that are always NOT COVERED.
- Dogfooded against an isolated CR_HOME with a hand-built round for acme/api#7. A good cell records and comes back stamped with the unit hash from units.ndjson and the head from meta.json. A cell carrying unit_hash exits 1 with supplied-hash.ndjson line 1: unit_hash is written by cr and must not be supplied, and coverage.ndjson keeps only the cell recorded before it. Rewriting units.ndjson with a new hash leaves the stored cell on the old one, and re-recording the identical line moves it to the new one.

tasks.title: Reject a pass cell contradicting records
tasks.acceptance:
- Round 8 finding cell-record-consistency-unchecked: a (unit, role) carrying a pass cell for which the current round holds a record from that role on that unit is rejected with exit code 1, or reported by cr status, naming both. Without it a role can file a pass cell while recording a finding on the same unit in the same round, and cr status prints a complete row with a clean verdict.

tasks.title: Emit one prompt per role-unit cell

tasks.title: Run the intent axis in passes
tasks.acceptance:

tasks.title: Stamp mapping existence onto the metadata
tasks.acceptance:
- Round 9 finding mapping-existence-unobservable: cr map record stamps the round and head of the stored mapping on meta.json, and §4.6.5's gate reads that stamp rather than inferring existence from mapping.ndjson's record count.

tasks.title: Skip mapping when intent is unavailable

- A test drives a keyless PR through the full fan-out and asserts no unmapped-unit question and no intent-gap entry appears.

tasks.title: Create the sandbox worktree at head
tasks.acceptance:
- cr sandbox create <pr> creates a git worktree at the PR head under ~/.cr/state/<owner>/<repo>/pr-<n>/sandbox/, per §5.1.1.
- The worktree registration under the repository's .git/worktrees/ is the sole write permitted by §2.2.
- cr never modifies the user's main worktree, index, or current branch, per §5.1.4.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr sandbox create <pr> adds a detached git worktree at the round's recorded head under ~/.cr/state/<owner>/<repo>/pr-<n>/sandbox/: state.Layout.Sandbox derives the path, git.AddWorktree runs git worktree add --detach, and the head comes from meta.json through Briefed. TestCreateMakesTheWorktreeAtTheHead and TestTheSandboxIsCheckedOutAtTheRoundsRecordedHead assert the path and the revision, the latter against a fixture whose own HEAD is a different commit.
- The registration under .git/worktrees/ is the sole write: norepowrite_test.go admits worktree to the git allowlist with its section, runs the command against the write fixture, and asserts the exception was empty before the run, is not empty after, and holds nothing outside .git/worktrees/sandbox, while the status, refs and SHA-256 content fingerprints stay byte-identical.
- The main worktree, index and current branch are untouched: TestAddWorktreeLeavesTheMainWorktreeAlone compares status --porcelain=v2, HEAD, the ref HEAD follows and every branch across the call on a deliberately dirtied checkout, and TestAddWorktreeChecksTheHeadOutAtTheGivenPath proves the sandbox takes no branch by requiring symbolic-ref to fail. Dogfooded against deligoez/cr-qa PR 1: git status --porcelain empty, git worktree list showing the sandbox at be7e2c7 detached.

tasks.title: Run copy steps before setup commands
tasks.acceptance:
- Paths listed in sandbox.copy are copied from the main checkout into the sandbox after creation, per §5.1.2.
- Commands in sandbox.setup run once, in order, in the sandbox root, per §5.1.3.
- A test asserts ordering: every copy completes before the first setup command runs.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Every path in sandbox.copy is copied from the main checkout into the sandbox after the worktree is added: state.Layout.CopyIntoSandbox derives the destination from the sandbox path, reproduces files with their mode, directory trees whole, and symlinks as symlinks, and reports a path the checkout does not hold instead of failing on it. TestCopyIntoSandboxReproducesFilesDirectoriesAndLinks and TestCopyIntoSandboxReportsAPathTheCheckoutDoesNotHold cover both, and cr sandbox create reads the list out of the profile the round recorded in meta.json.
- Commands in sandbox.setup run once, in order, in the sandbox root: internal/sandbox/run.go starts each entry as its own argv with no shell, with the sandbox as the working directory, and stops the run on the first refusal with the command's stderr surfaced as exit code 3. TestASetupCommandThatFailsStopsTheRun and TestTheSandboxRunsTheProfilesCopyAndSetupSteps assert both halves, the latter end to end through the command.
- TestEveryCopyLandsBeforeTheFirstSetupCommandRuns makes the ordering observable rather than read off the code: the first setup command reads the two copied paths and appends what it found to a log outside the sandbox, the second appends after it, and the log is asserted whole, so a copy that ran late, a command that ran twice, or a pair that ran in the wrong order each produce a different file. Verified by swapping the two loops, which turned the first two lines into the shell's No such file complaints. Dogfooded against deligoez/cr-qa PR 1 with the laravel-pest profile: .env copied, vendor reported absent, composer install run in the sandbox, git status --porcelain in the clone empty and .git/worktrees/sandbox the only new path.

tasks.title: Remove the sandbox worktree with registration
tasks.acceptance:
- cr sandbox destroy <pr> removes the worktree and its registration, per §5.1.5.
- A test asserts .git/worktrees/ carries no leftover entry afterwards.
tasks.closed_reason:
- `cr sandbox destroy <pr>` is wired in internal/cli/sandbox.go and calls sandbox.Destroy, which removes the worktree through git.RemoveWorktree and prunes the registration in both branches — a directory that is already gone still leaves an entry under `.git/worktrees/`, and `worktree add` refuses a path that is still registered, so a removal that skipped the prune would strand the one state §5.1.1 cannot recover from. §5.1.6's recreation now shares that helper instead of repeating it, and the post-setup baseline goes with the sandbox it described. Dogfooded against deligoez/cr-qa PR #1: after the destroy, `git worktree list` shows only the clone, `.git/worktrees/` is gone, `git status --porcelain` is empty, and sandbox-baseline.json has left the pull request's state directory.
- TestDestroyingTheSandboxLeavesNoWorktreeRegistrationBehind creates a sandbox, asserts the registration directory holds exactly one entry, destroys it, and then reads `.git/worktrees/` off disk to assert it is empty or absent rather than trusting git's own report; it also counts `git worktree list --porcelain` down to the checkout itself and runs the command a second time, where a pull request with no sandbox is told so rather than refused. TestNoCommandTouchesTheRepositoryUnderReview now runs `sandbox destroy` between `sandbox create` and `test`, so the removal is followed by §5.1.6 rebuilding on the path it had just freed.

tasks.title: Record the post-setup baseline outside worktree
tasks.acceptance:
- After §5.1.2 and §5.1.3 complete, cr records the sandbox's tracked-file state as the post-setup baseline, per §5.1.6.
- Round 8 finding unhomed-state: the baseline is durable cross-process state read by later cr invocations, so it gets a named row in §2.3's per-PR state table and lives outside the worktree. Storing it inside the sandbox would make recording it a candidate for violating §2.2's rule against writing into the repository under review, since the sandbox is a worktree of that repository.
- The baseline is invalidated whenever the sandbox is recreated.
- A test asserts the baseline file sits under the per-PR state directory, not under sandbox/.
tasks.closed_reason:
- After §5.1.2 and §5.1.3 complete, sandbox.Create takes git's own diff of the sandbox working tree against its HEAD and records it as the post-setup baseline; the record is written last in Create, once every copy is in and every setup command has run.
- Round 8 finding unhomed-state: the baseline is a named row of §2.3's per-PR table, state.FileSandboxBaseline = "sandbox-baseline.json", declared beside the other twelve names in internal/state/prfiles.go and written through the exclusive advisory lock §2.3.1 requires. It sits under ~/.cr/state/<owner>/<repo>/pr-<n>/, never in the sandbox, because the sandbox is a worktree of the repository under review and §2.2 permits cr no write there but §5.1.1's registration.
- The baseline is invalidated whenever the sandbox is recreated: Create drops it through the new state.Lock.Remove before git.AddWorktree runs, so a creation that dies inside §5.1.3 leaves no record rather than a record of a sandbox that no longer exists.
- TestTheBaselineIsRecordedOutsideTheWorktreeAfterSetup asserts the file exists at Layout.PRFile(..., state.FileSandboxBaseline), does not exist inside the sandbox, and resolves outside it by filepath.Rel; TestTheBaselineIsInvalidatedWhenTheSandboxIsRecreated asserts the previous baseline is gone after a recreation that fails in setup.
