- The state is kept whole rather than digested: §1.4 defines cr's one hash and internal/text fences the ingredient, and that hash normalises before digesting, so a mutation changing only whitespace would hash to the baseline's value and pass §5.1.6's check. git.TrackedState reads it with --binary, so a changed binary is not summarised away either.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... && golangci-lint run (0 issues) && ./scripts/deadcode.sh.

tasks.title: Verify sandbox head with cleanliness check
tasks.acceptance:
- Before every probe or test run, cr verifies that the sandbox HEAD equals the PR head and that the sandbox is clean, per §5.1.6.
- Clean means that no tracked file differs from the post-setup baseline, and that no leftover probe artefact exists — no file under any path matching tests.probe_path_template with its <probe-id> position replaced by *, which the template contains exactly once.
- Other untracked files are ignored, because sandbox.copy and sandbox.setup create them by design.
- A sandbox failing any of these checks is recreated, and the recreation is reported — a disclosure that survives --quiet per §11.1.
- A test covers a moved head, a dirtied tracked file, a leftover artefact, and a benign untracked file.
- Round 12 finding artefact-glob-not-scoped-to-untracked, assigned here: the leftover-artefact glob is evaluated over untracked files only. A tests.probe_path_template that also matches tracked test files must not make every sandbox permanently unclean and the mandated recreation unbounded.
tasks.closed_reason:
- sandbox.Ensure verifies, before a probe or test run, that the sandbox exists, that git.Head of the sandbox equals the round's head, and that it is clean; the test-run caller is wired in test-command, which depends on this task.
- Clean means the tracked-file deviation from HEAD equals the recorded post-setup baseline byte for byte, not that the sandbox matches HEAD: §5.1.3's setup modifies tracked files by design, and a baseline taken at another head is itself a reason to recreate. The leftover-artefact scan takes tests.probe_path_template with its <probe-id> replaced by * — profile.LeftoverGlob already produces it — matches it against the sandbox, and keeps only the matches git.TrackedAmong reports as untracked.
- Every other untracked file is ignored: only paths under the glob are ever looked at, and the sentinel file the tests drop into the sandbox survives a clean check.
- A sandbox failing any check is removed with git.RemoveWorktree and rebuilt by Create, and Ensure returns a sandbox.Recreated naming the path and the reason. Recreated implements finding.HonestyDisclosure, which is the shape §11.1's exemption consumes. It is returned rather than printed because internal/cli still has no disclosure-printing writer — that writer is the open quiet-honesty-exemptions task — so nothing suppresses it today and adopting it there is a call site rather than a rewrite.
- Round 12 finding artefact-glob-not-scoped-to-untracked: the scan is scoped to untracked files by asking git which of the glob's matches are tracked. TestOnlyAnUntrackedFileUnderTheGlobIsALeftoverArtefact uses a glob that matches a tracked fixture file and asserts the sandbox stays clean, then adds an untracked match beside it and asserts only that one is named.
- TestAnUncleanSandboxIsRecreatedAndTheRecreationIsReported covers a missing sandbox, a moved head, a dirtied tracked file, a leftover artefact and a missing baseline; each asserts the reason, the disclosure text, that an untracked sentinel is gone so the recreation was performed and not merely reported, and that a second Ensure reports nothing, so the mandated recreation converges.
- git.RemoveWorktree and git.PruneWorktrees are added here because recreation needs removal; wiring them to `cr sandbox destroy` remains that task's work. gitReads gains rev-parse and ls-files, both reads.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... && golangci-lint run (0 issues) && ./scripts/deadcode.sh.

tasks.title: Override probe result on unclean sandbox
tasks.acceptance:
- A probe whose post-run cleanliness check fails is recorded with result error, does not grade any finding, and forces recreation before the next run, per §5.1.7.
- Round 9 finding probe-result-override: the cleanliness check runs before the probe record is written and overrides the ladder outcome. Without the stated order, §5.3.4 and §5.4.3's totality claims collide with §5.5.1's immutability — it would be undecidable whether error is the only value ever persisted or whether an immutable record must be amended.
- A test forces an unclean post-run state and asserts exactly one record is written, carrying error, and that the next invocation recreates the sandbox.
- §5.1.7 also states that such a probe establishes nothing in either direction, so §5.3.7's suppression is not applied from it. §5.4.5's severity ceiling still binds, because error is a value it already names.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/probe/outcome.go's Decide takes §5.3.4's or §5.4.3's ladder outcome together with what §5.1.6's post-run check found and returns ResultError whenever the check found anything, while internal/sandbox's ForceRecreation drops the post-setup baseline so §5.1.6 reads the sandbox as one to recreate before the next run, and Outcome.Voided is the single fact the record value, the refusal to grade and the forced recreation all follow from.
- Round 9's probe-result-override is made structural by Outcome, whose fields are unexported and whose only constructor is Decide, so no probe result can be reached that the cleanliness check has not already had its say about, and the check therefore always runs before the record is written.
- Exactly one value is ever persisted, so §5.3.4's and §5.4.3's totality claims never collide with §5.5.1's immutability, because there is no already-written record left for an override to have to amend.
- TestAProbeWhoseSandboxFailedItsCheckIsRecordedErrorAndForcesRecreation leaves a real probe artefact in a real sandbox worktree, drives Unclean into Decide with a ladder outcome of no-test-failed, asserts one value was recorded and that it is error, then calls ForceRecreation and asserts the next Ensure recreates the sandbox naming the missing baseline as its reason and that both the artefact and the sentinel are gone.
- ResultError replaces the ladder value rather than sitting beside it, so §5.3.7's suppression cannot be read from a voided probe at all, because the failed it keys on is not the value that reached the record, and TestAnUncleanSandboxOverridesEveryLadderOutcome drives every value both ladders can produce through the override to show that no-test-failed and failed alike are discarded.
- §5.4.5 needs no special case for a voided gap probe, since error is a result it already names among those that may not support a probed grade and whose severity is capped at medium, so the ceiling binds through the ordinary handling of a value the section was already written for.

tasks.title: Run the profile test command
tasks.acceptance:
- cr test <pr> [--filter <expr>] runs the profile's test command inside the sandbox, per §5.2.1.
- tests.filter_flag narrows the run to a subset when --filter is given.
- A test asserts the command runs with the sandbox as its working directory, never the main checkout.
tasks.closed_reason:
- `cr test <pr> [--filter <expr>]` runs the profile's test command inside the sandbox per §5.2.1: it reads the round's profile from meta.json, verifies the sandbox through sandbox.Ensure (§5.1.6) and rebuilds it when the check fails, then starts the argv with sandbox.Run, whose cmd.Dir is the state-derived sandbox path. The runner's output goes to standard error as it is produced, because §12.1 keeps stdout for the command's own document; the exit status is reported as a value rather than interpreted, since a failing suite is an ordinary outcome and §5.3.4's ladder is built on reading one.
- tests.filter_flag narrows the run: Profile.TestArgv appends the flag and the expression as two argv elements, there being no shell to quote for, and refuses a --filter against a profile that sets no flag rather than silently running the whole suite.
- TestTheTestCommandRunsInTheSandboxAndNeverTheCheckout has the runner record its own working directory and asserts it equals the sandbox and differs from the repository under review; TestTheTestCommandRunsTheProfileRunnerInTheSandbox asserts the same end to end through the command, together with the argv the filter produced and §5.1.6's recreation notice in the payload's honesty field.
- The recreation disclosure reaches the reader as `honesty` on the payload, the same shape `cr brief` uses, so §11.1's exemption holds today by there being nothing that suppresses it; quiet-honesty-exemptions still owns the writer that will consume finding.HonestyDisclosure directly.
- Out of scope and left open: §5.2.4's run record and its output tail, §5.2.2's baseline-per-head rule, §5.2.3's timeout, §5.2.5's passed predicate, count_pattern/failed_pattern extraction, §5.3/§5.4's probes, and `cr sandbox destroy` — which now only needs to wire git.RemoveWorktree to a command.
- Dogfooded against deligoez/cr-qa PR 1: `cr test` ran ./vendor/bin/pest in the sandbox (4 passed), `--filter cancelled` narrowed it to 1, an unreverted edit to src/Order.php and a leftover tests/Feature/cr_probe_p1Test.php each triggered a reported recreation, and the clone's `git status --porcelain` stayed empty with `.git/worktrees/sandbox` the only added path across a remove-and-re-add cycle.
- gremlins: Killed 894, Lived 14, Not covered 80, Timed out 4, efficacy 98.46%. Two survivors appeared in this work and one was a real gap — the fallback in `differing` and the error check in git.RemoveWorktree, both now covered; the remaining one is the documented equivalent capacity hint. deadcode ./... 89, down one, with nothing of this work listed.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... && golangci-lint run (0 issues) && ./scripts/deadcode.sh.

tasks.title: Define the test run record
tasks.acceptance:
- Every run is stored as a run record in runs.ndjson carrying id of the form r<n>, head, filter when one was given, exit_code, duration_ms, tests_run and tests_failed when derivable, output_tail, and passed, per §5.2.4.
- This id space is what a probe's baseline field references.
- output_tail is the last tests.output_tail_bytes of output.
- §5.2.4's field list also carries probe, set when the run was performed on mutated or probe-injected code. It is stamped by cr; no agent submits a run record.
- Round 12 finding unstorable-value, assigned here: §5.2.3 requires a timed-out run to be 'recorded as timeout' but the field list has no slot for it. The implementation adds timed_out to the run record and records the kill through it, so a killed run stays distinguishable from a runner that exited non-zero.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/run/run.go holds §5.2.4's run record and `cr test` stores one for every run: recordRun in internal/cli/test.go allocates run.NextID's `r<n>` under the §2.3.1 lock and appends through state.AppendStamped, so the line in runs.ndjson carries id, head, round, filter when one was given, exit_code, duration_ms, tests_run and tests_failed when derivable, output_tail and passed. TestARunRecordCarriesExactlyTheFieldsSection524Names pins the wire shape and TestTheTestCommandStoresARunRecordForEveryRun asserts the stored line end to end, including that a second run is added rather than written over the first.
- The id space is the one a probe's `baseline` references: NextID allocates above every id runs.ndjson already holds rather than at the record count, because §5.5.3 keeps probe records from earlier heads on disk and reusing an id would silently repoint a stored probe at a different measurement. TestNextIDAllocatesAboveEveryRunTheFileHolds covers an empty file, a gap left by an earlier round, records out of order, and spellings cr never wrote.
- output_tail is the last `tests.output_tail_bytes` of output: run.Tail is an io.Writer teed off the same merged stream the reader watches, so what is stored is what was shown, and it holds the bound across however many writes the runner makes. TestTheOutputTailKeepsTheLastBytesOfEverythingWritten covers a write larger than the whole budget and several writes over it together, and TestTheOutputTailDoesNotEndAHalfRuneAtTheFrontOfTheOutput drops a rune the byte cut split rather than letting json.Marshal substitute U+FFFD for it.
- `probe` is a field of the record, absent for a run on untouched code and carrying the probe id for a run on mutated or probe-injected code, which is the fence §5.2.6 reads when it admits only a run carrying no `probe` as a baseline.
- It is stamped by cr: `probe` is set by the caller that performed the probe run and by nothing else, and head and round reach the record only through the embedded state.Stamp, which state.WriteStamped writes on the way out.
- No agent submits a run record, so there is no Required or Optional row of the §6.1 kind here. checkRecordFields is the fence in the idiom internal/cli/output.go uses — it holds Record's JSON tags to §5.2.4's list at package initialisation and requires head and round to be promoted from state.Stamp — and TestEveryFieldOfARunRecordIsWrittenByCR reads every row back to cr or to that stamp and to nothing else.
- Round 12's unstorable-value finding is answered by adding `timed_out` to §5.2.4's record, because §5.2.3 requires a killed run to be recorded as timeout and the section's field list has no slot for it.
- The kill is recorded through that field rather than inferred from the exit status, because the exit status of a process cr killed is the same kind of number a runner that decided to fail produces, and §5.3.4's ladder puts `timeout` and `error` on different rungs and both above every reading of the counts. TestAKilledRunIsDistinguishableFromARunnerThatExitedNonZero holds two records that agree on exit_code and disagree only there.

tasks.title: Extract counts from the last match
tasks.acceptance:
- tests.count_pattern and tests.failed_pattern each yield exactly one capture group, per §5.2.1. Corrected here after a unit found this acceptance still described the pre-repair two-group shape: a unit following the old text would reimplement the very defect the spec repair removed.
- Every match of each pattern is taken and the captures are summed, not just the last one. A count pattern that never matches leaves the counts undetermined; a failed pattern that never matches means ZERO, not undetermined, because Pest omits any status whose count is zero and prints no "failed" line at all on an all-passing run.
- A capture that does not parse as a base-10 non-negative integer leaves BOTH counts undetermined, per §5.2.1. Corrected here too: the earlier wording said "that count", which is looser than the spec.
- Counts are read from the whole captured stream, never from the retained tail. A tail-bounded sum is not an undetermined count but a wrong one: a cut through a recap line turns "2 failed, 4 passed" into four tests and no failures, which §5.2.5 would call passed and §5.3.5 would accept as a baseline.
- A test covers no match of either pattern, one match, several matches that must sum, an all-passing run whose failed pattern is absent, and an unparseable capture.
- Round 12 finding undefined-input-stream, assigned here: §5.2.1 never says which stream output_tail and count_pattern read. The implementation fixes it as the runner's merged stdout and stderr, in that order, so the value feeding probe grading is deterministic.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/run/counts.go reads §5.2.1's two counts out of one capture group per pattern: NewCounter compiles tests.count_pattern and tests.failed_pattern as internal/profile already validated them at exactly one group, and sum indexes match[1] and nothing else, so the arity the profile enforces is the arity the extractor depends on.
- The corrected acceptance is what was implemented and the pre-repair two-group shape was not: there is no second group, no positional executed-then-failed reading of one match, and no last-match-wins rule anywhere in counts.go.
- Every match of each pattern is taken and the captures are summed: sum ranges over FindAllStringSubmatch(output, -1) and adds each group, so `Tests: 2 failed, 1 passed, 3 passed` is six executed and two failed rather than the three and two a last-match reader would report.
- A count pattern that never matches leaves both counts undetermined, which Counts returns as a nil pair so §5.2.4 omits the keys entirely, and a failed pattern that never matches yields zero rather than undetermined, because sum's `matched` result is read for the count pattern and deliberately discarded for the failed one.
- The all-passing case is the reason for that asymmetry and it is asserted on real output: internal/profile/testdata/pest/all-passing.txt never contains the word failed at all, which the test now asserts as its premise, and the extractor still reports 2 executed and 0 failed from it.
- A capture that does not parse as a base-10 non-negative integer leaves both counts undetermined: strconv.ParseUint permits no sign, so `-2` fails rather than being subtracted, and a value or a sum beyond maxCount is refused rather than wrapping into a smaller number than the run produced.
- The spec is stricter than this criterion's wording and the spec was followed: §5.2.1 says a group that does not parse leaves *both* counts undetermined, so an unreadable failed capture takes the executed count with it rather than leaving a half-measured run for §5.3.4 rung 4 to read as a determined one.
- TestEveryMatchOfEachPatternIsSummedRatherThanTheLastOneWinning covers all five cases the criterion names — no match of either pattern, one match, several matches that must sum, an all-passing run whose failed pattern never matches, and an unparseable capture — plus two more matches on the failed pattern, an unparseable failed capture, and a sum too large to be a count; TestANegativeCaptureIsNotACount, TestOutputArrivingInPiecesIsCountedAsOneStream, TestAProfileWithNoCountPatternDeterminesNothingAndKeepsNothing and TestAnUncompilablePatternIsReportedAndNamesItsField cover the rest.
- Round 12's undefined-input-stream finding is answered in the implementation: Counter is an io.Writer teed off the same value sandbox.Run gives both cmd.Stdout and cmd.Stderr, so os/exec opens one pipe and one copying goroutine and the text matched is the runner's stdout and stderr merged in the order the runner wrote them.
- TestTheStoredCountsAreSummedOverTheWholeMergedStream proves that end to end through the command: the runner prints `Tests: 2 passed` to stdout and `Tests: 3 passed` to stderr and the stored record reads tests_run 5, so neither stream alone was read.
- The counts are taken from the whole captured stream and not from the retained tail, which the same test pins by setting tests.output_tail_bytes to 16: the tail stores only `ests:  3 passed` while the count is still 5. A tail-bounded sum would not be an undetermined count but a wrong one, since a cut through a recap line turns `2 failed, 4 passed` into four tests and no failures — a run §5.2.5 calls passed and §5.3.5 accepts as a baseline.
- internal/profile/builtin_test.go's sumPattern helper is gone and TestTheLaravelPestPatternsCountCapturedPestOutput now runs the shipped patterns through run.NewCounter, so the six captured Pest 4.7.8 recaps judge the production extractor rather than a copy of the arithmetic that can agree with the spec while cr does not.
- Dogfooded against deligoez/cr-qa PR 1: `cr test 1` on the all-passing suite recorded `"tests_run":4,"tests_failed":0` — the case with no failed line at all — and `cr test 1 --filter "no such test exists"` recorded neither key, leaving both undetermined per §5.2.1. `passed` is still false on both because §5.2.5's predicate is run-passed-predicate's task.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... && golangci-lint run (0 issues) && ./scripts/deadcode.sh.
Out of scope: §5.2.3's timeout, §5.2.5's passed predicate, §5.2.2's baseline-per-head rule and §5.5's baseline resolution are separate open tasks and are untouched here.

tasks.title: Kill runs exceeding the configured timeout
tasks.acceptance:
- A run exceeding tests.timeout_seconds is killed and recorded as timeout, per §5.2.3.
- The default is 900 seconds per §2.4.
- A test asserts the process group is killed, not just the parent.
tasks.closed_reason:
- sandbox.Run now takes a timeout and returns whether the run was killed for exceeding it: the runner is started rather than run to completion, cmd.Wait moves to a goroutine, and a select between it and a time.Timer decides the outcome, so a run that outlives its budget is killed and reported as a timeout instead of as an ordinary failure.
- The outcome reaches storage where §5.2.3 needs it: internal/cli/test.go passes `time.Duration(resolved.Tests.TimeoutSeconds) * time.Second` and sets Record.TimedOut, so runs.ndjson carries `"timed_out":true` beside the platform's exit code for a killed process — the slot run-record-schema opened for exactly this, because §5.3.4 rung 2 must be readable without guessing at an exit code.
- The reader is told too, which the exit code cannot do on its own: testRunResult gains `timed_out` and the text rendering prints "killed for exceeding tests.timeout_seconds", because -1 beside no explanation reads as a suite that ran and failed.
- The default is 900 seconds per §2.4 and it is the profile's number that bounds the run, not a constant in the command: profile.DefaultTimeoutSeconds is 900 and TestParseAppliesTheDocumentedDefaults already pins an omitting profile to it, while TestARunThatExceedsTheProfilesTimeoutIsRecordedAsATimeout sets tests.timeout_seconds to 1 against a runner that sleeps for two minutes — a command reaching for the 900-second default instead would hang the suite rather than fail an assertion.
- What is killed is the process group and not the parent: the child is started with SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}, so its process group id equals its own pid, and the timeout path signals the negative pid with SIGKILL, which reaches the runner and everything it started.
- TestARunOutlivingItsBudgetIsKilledWithEverythingItStarted proves the group kill in two independent ways. The runner starts a `sh -c 'while :; do sleep 0.2; done'` child that never exits on its own and inherits the output pipe, then sleeps for 120 seconds; the test reads the child's pid out of a file the runner wrote and asserts with `syscall.Kill(child, 0)` that the pid answers ESRCH within ten seconds, and separately asserts that Run returned at all inside thirty seconds.
- The test was proven to bite rather than assumed to: replacing `syscall.Kill(-group, ...)` with `syscall.Kill(group, ...)` was run and the test did not merely fail an assertion — it hung and was killed by the 25-second test deadline, with the goroutine dump showing cmd.Wait blocked in awaitGoroutines on the io.Copy from the pipe the surviving grandchild still held. That is the orphan §5.6's lock exists to prevent, seen directly.
- SIGKILL rather than SIGTERM, and a timeout of zero or less is no budget rather than an expired one; TestARunGivenNoBudgetIsNotKilled pins the second direction, since reading zero as a deadline already passed would kill every run of a caller that forgot to pass one.
- Closed-task code touched, and its claim is not weakened: TestOnlyTheStatePackageWritesToTheFilesystem banned `syscall` outside internal/state, and the process-group kill cannot be spelled without it. The guard now exempts one named file for exactly three names — SysProcAttr, Kill and SIGKILL — and gained a scan that fails on any other `syscall.X` in that same file. It was proven to bite by adding `syscall.Getpid()` to run.go and observing "internal/sandbox/run.go uses syscall.Getpid", then reverting. The sentence the guard makes is unchanged: no filesystem write can be spelled outside internal/state.
- Dogfooded against deligoez/cr-qa PR 1 with a temporary tests.cmd of `sh -c 'sleep 300 & echo $! > /tmp/cr-qa-child.pid; sleep 300'` and tests.timeout_seconds 2: run r4 recorded `"exit_code":-1,"timed_out":true,"duration_ms":2003`, the payload printed `timed_out: true`, and the pid the runner's background child wrote answered "no such process" afterwards. The profile file was restored byte-for-byte identical to internal/profile/builtin/laravel-pest.json.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... && golangci-lint run (0 issues) && ./scripts/deadcode.sh.
Out of scope: §5.2.5's passed predicate is the next task, and §5.3.4's `timeout` rung, §5.2.2's baseline-per-head rule and §5.5's baseline resolution belong to the probe and baseline tasks; nothing here reads Record.TimedOut back.

tasks.title: Decide whether a run passed
tasks.acceptance:
- A run record has passed: true when exit_code is 0, tests_run is derivable and greater than 0, and tests_failed is 0; otherwise passed: false, per §5.2.5.
- A run whose counts are underivable never passes, so it cannot serve as a baseline.
- A test covers each of the four failing conditions separately.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Record.Verdict is §5.2.5's predicate and conjoins exactly its four clauses: the exit code is 0, TestsRun is derivable, that count is greater than zero, and TestsFailed is 0. Anything else is false.
- The verdict is computed where the record is written rather than where it is built: internal/cli/test.go's appendRun sets record.Passed = record.Verdict() beside record.ID = run.NextID(stored), so both derived fields are cr's and no caller can hand runs.ndjson a `passed` its own counts do not support.
- A run whose counts are underivable never passes, because an absent count is nil in both positions and neither `*TestsRun > 0` nor `*TestsFailed == 0` can be read off nil. That is what keeps it out of §5.2.6's baseline pool, and §5.3.5 and §5.4.4 out of a `probed` grade resting on it: a baseline that passed on counts nobody could read would attribute the repository's pre-existing failures to the probe.
- TestARunPassesOnlyWhileEveryClauseOfTheVerdictHolds isolates each failing condition separately, starting from a record that passes and breaking exactly one clause per case, so a clause the predicate had quietly stopped depending on fails its own case rather than being masked by another.
- The four the criterion names are a non-zero exit code, an undetermined executed count, an executed count of zero and a non-zero failed count; two more are covered beside them, an undetermined failed count and a run killed for exceeding its budget, which reaches the verdict as the platform's exit code for a killed process.
- TestTheStoredCountsAreSummedOverTheWholeMergedStream now asserts `"passed":true` on the one shape that can satisfy the predicate end to end — exit 0, five executed, none failed — while TestTheTestCommandStoresARunRecordForEveryRun still asserts false for a run with no count pattern configured, so both branches of the verdict are pinned through the command.
- Dogfooded against deligoez/cr-qa PR 1, all four shapes with the built binary: r6 `exit_code 0, tests_run 4, tests_failed 0, passed true` on the all-passing Pest suite — the determined branch, reachable for the first time; r7 `exit_code 1, tests_run 4, tests_failed 2, passed false`, determined counts and a failure; r8 `--filter "no such test exists"`, both counts absent, `passed false`; r4 `timed_out true, exit_code -1`, `passed false`.
- Mutation testing: gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 962, Lived 19, Not covered 85, Timed out 7, efficacy 98.06%, against the 940/18/83/4 baseline. One new survivor, CONDITIONALS_BOUNDARY at run/counts.go:130:12, was a real undocumented boundary rather than an equivalent: the sum guard's `>` reads maxCount as the largest count still allowed, and `>=` would refuse a total landing exactly on it. It is now pinned by a case summing 2147483646 and 1, verified to bite by applying the mutant by hand and watching the case fail.
- The three new TIMED OUT mutants are all in the timeout path and are detections rather than survivors: negating `timeout > 0` and either mutation of `-group` make the suite hang instead of failing an assertion, which is exactly the hang the parent-only kill produced when it was tried by hand.
- The two new Not covered entries are both at run/counts.go:17:27, the `maxCount = 1<<countBits - 1` constant expression, which has no executable statement for coverage to reach; the NOT COVERED at sandbox/run.go:163:12 is a switch-case-expression artifact, since `go test -coverprofile` reports the block at 163.19 as covered.
- deadcode ./... is 89, unchanged, with nothing from this batch listed.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... && golangci-lint run (0 issues) && ./scripts/deadcode.sh.
Out of scope: §5.2.2's baseline-per-head rule and §5.2.6's baseline resolution are baseline-recording and baseline-resolution, still open; nothing reads Record.Passed back yet, and §5.3 and §5.4's probe ladders, probe-record-schema and probe-round-cap are untouched.

tasks.title: Record baselines scoped to mutation filters
tasks.acceptance:
- A baseline run with no filter is recorded once per head, so pre-existing failures are never attributed to a probe, per §5.2.2.
- Round 8 findings stale-cross-reference and unreachable-baseline-requirement, resolved by the approved specification repair: the filtered-baseline obligation is scoped to mutation probes. A gap probe's baseline is the unfiltered run per §5.5, since the probe's own test does not exist in the baseline; a filtered gap baseline would select a not-yet-created file, leaving tests_run at 0 and passed permanently false, and §5.2.6 would never resolve it.
- A test asserts a filtered gap probe records no filtered baseline, and that a filtered mutation probe records one.
- Round 12 finding baseline-contamination, assigned here: §5.1.7 voids a probe after a failed cleanliness check but nothing voids a plain cr test run, so a contaminated run can still be recorded passed: true and later resolved as a baseline. The implementation applies the same cleanliness check to a test run.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/probe/baseline.go's Required always returns the unfiltered baseline first and Missing answers "once per head" out of runs.ndjson itself rather than out of a memo beside it, because §2.3.3 already stamps head on every run record, so a moved head invalidates every baseline for free and §5.5.3's records from earlier heads can never be mistaken for this head's.
- Referenced reads the filter argument only for Mutation and ignores it for Gap, which makes the round 8 repair structural rather than checked, since no call at all can produce a filtered gap baseline.
- Required derives from Referenced, so a gap probe's baseline is §5.5's unfiltered run, and TestOnlyAFilteredMutationProbeAddsASecondBaseline pins that for a filtered gap probe and an unfiltered one alike.
- The not-yet-created test file §5.4.2 places for the probe run alone can therefore never be what a baseline selects, which is the run that would have left tests_run at 0 and passed permanently false while §5.2.6 re-performed a baseline it could never resolve.
- TestOnlyAFilteredMutationProbeAddsASecondBaseline asserts a filtered gap probe records only the unfiltered baseline while a filtered mutation probe records that one and its filtered companion, over all four combinations of kind and filter.
- run.Record.Contaminated closes round 12's baseline-contamination as a field §5.2.4's list has no slot for in the way it has none for TimedOut, read by Verdict as a fourth clause so that no path into runs.ndjson stores passed true for a run whose sandbox drifted from the head under it, and read by Spec.stands so that such a run is no candidate baseline either.
- cr test now calls sandbox.Unclean after the run as well as sandbox.Ensure before it, which is the same §5.1.6 check §5.1.7 applies to a probe, and TestATestRunItsSandboxContaminatedIsNoBaseline drives a runner that exits 0 with four tests run and none failed and then dirties a tracked file, asserting the stored record carries contaminated true and passed false while all three of §5.2.5's own clauses held.

tasks.title: Resolve a probe baseline before running
tasks.acceptance:
- cr probe run resolves its baseline per §5.5 and, when no matching run exists at the current head, performs and records it before the probe, per §5.2.6.
- When more than one matches, the most recent is used.
- A test asserts an absent baseline is created automatically and that two candidates resolve to the newer one.
- §5.2.6: only a run record carrying no probe may serve as a baseline, so a probe's own mutated or probe-injected run cannot become the next probe's baseline. A test asserts a first probe at a fresh head still obtains one, because the run §5.2.6 performs is on un-probed code.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/probe/resolve.go's Ensure performs, through the caller's Performer, every baseline Missing reports the head has no run for, and only then resolves the one §5.5's baseline column names for the kind and filter it was given, so the performing always precedes the probe as §5.2.6 requires.
- Spec.Resolve walks the stored runs backwards and stops at the first match, which is the most recent, because runs.ndjson is appended to and never rewritten under §2.3 while run.NextID allocates above every id on file, making file order, id order and chronological order the same order.
- TestAnAbsentBaselineIsPerformedBeforeTheProbe drives Ensure with nothing on file and asserts which specs were performed and in which order for both kinds, and TestTwoBaselineCandidatesResolveToTheMostRecent gives two matches that disagree about §5.2.5's verdict and asserts both the id and the verdict come from the newer one, with a performer that fails the test if §5.2.6 performs anything.
- §5.2.6's fence is made structural by the Baseline type, whose fields are unexported and whose only constructor is Spec.Resolve, which never builds one out of a record carrying a probe, so a probe's own mutated or probe-injected run cannot be handed to §5.3.5 or §5.4.4 as the record that licenses a probed grade even though it can still be read and printed like any other run.
- TestAProbesOwnRunNeverBecomesTheNextProbesBaseline asserts a probe-carrying run at the current head is passed over and a fresh baseline performed, that a first probe at a head nothing has been run at still obtains one because the run §5.2.6 performs is on un-probed code by construction, and that a performed run which is itself inadmissible leaves Ensure with an error naming the head rather than a baseline nothing stands behind.

tasks.title: Apply the mutation before running tests
tasks.acceptance:
- A mutation probe proves a test gap by breaking production code. The agent supplies a mutation as a unified diff against a sandbox file, per §5.3.1.
- cr probe run <pr> --kind mutation --patch <file> --filter <expr> applies the mutation, runs the tests, reverts the mutation, and records the result, per §5.3.2.
- A test drives the full apply-run-revert-record cycle.
tasks.closed_reason:
- A mutation probe breaks production code from an agent-supplied unified diff: internal/git/patch.go's ParsePatch reads the diff whole with every hunk body intact, and PatchedFile.Apply applies it strictly, with no offset search and no fuzz, so a hunk that does not match the sandbox file is refused rather than relocated.
- cr probe run <pr> --kind mutation --patch <file> --filter <expr> in internal/cli/probe.go applies the mutation, runs the profile's suite inside the sandbox, reverts the mutation, and records the result; the apply and the revert are one act, since state.UnderSandboxMutation in internal/state/mutate.go writes the files, calls the run, and restores them from a defer it owns, so the mutation is off disk on return, on error, and on panic. The value recorded is probe.Decide's, fed by probe.Ladder reading section 5.3.4's seven rungs off the run, so section 5.1.7's override lands before the write and exactly one value reaches probes.ndjson; section 5.2.6's baselines are performed first inside one hold of section 5.6.1's lock, and the mutated run is stored carrying the probe id, which fences a probe's own run out of every baseline resolution.
- TestAMutationProbeAppliesRunsRevertsAndRecords in internal/cli/probe_test.go drives the full apply-run-revert-record cycle against the fixture repository and asserts every step from evidence the command could not have faked: the runner's own log shows the baseline ran against the head's file and the probe against the mutated one, the sandbox holds the head's file again when the command returns, runs.ndjson holds r1 with no probe and r2 with one, and probes.ndjson holds p1 with result no-test-failed and baseline r1.
- The quality gate passes: go test -race ./..., golangci-lint run, and scripts/deadcode.sh.

tasks.title: Derive target from the mutation patch
tasks.acceptance:
- cr derives target from the patch itself — the first line the diff modifies — and rejects --target for this kind, per §5.3.2.
- The evidence chain from experiment to assertion then runs on the patch cr executed, not on a flag the agent typed.
- A test asserts --target on a mutation probe is rejected, and that the derived target matches the patch's first modified line.
- §5.3.2 derives target as the path and pre-image line of the first hunk's first removed or replaced line, or when that hunk only adds lines, its first pre-image line.
- Round 12 findings probe-target-underdetermined, probe-target-steering, undefined-derivation-branch, assigned here: the derivation must be single-valued for every unified diff. The implementation fixes 'first hunk' by ascending path then ascending pre-image start, defines the add-only branch for a zero-context hunk such as @@ -41,0 +42 @@ (which has no pre-image line of its own), and rejects a patch whose first hunk only adds lines when that would place target outside what the patch actually mutates. A table-driven test covers multi-file, multi-hunk, add-only, and -U0 patches.
- Round 12 finding unbounded-patch-target, assigned here: cr rejects a patch whose paths resolve outside the sandbox, so §5.1.4's invariant is enforced rather than assumed.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr derives target from the patch itself in internal/probe/target.go's Target, and internal/cli/probe.go rejects --target for a mutation probe before it reads anything else, naming section 5.3.2 in the refusal.
- The evidence chain runs on the patch cr executed: the record's target row is only ever Target's answer over the parsed diff, and there is no path by which a flag can set it, so the line section 6.2.2 anchors a probed finding at is the line the experiment was performed on.
- TestAMutationProbeRefusesASuppliedTarget in internal/cli/probe_test.go asserts --target exits 2 with no suite run, and TestAMutationProbeAppliesRunsRevertsAndRecords asserts probes.ndjson carries target app.go:3, which is the line the patch's only hunk replaces.
- The derivation is section 5.3.2's: the path and pre-image line of the first hunk's first removed or replaced line, counting context lines as it walks the hunk body, or the hunk's own first pre-image line when the hunk only adds.
- The round 12 findings are answered by fixing the order rather than reading the patch's own, so the derivation is single-valued for every unified diff.
- The first hunk is the lowest pre-image path and then the lowest pre-image start, so an agent cannot steer the target by rearranging its patch; the add-only branch names the hunk's own first pre-image line; and a zero-context add-only first hunk such as @@ -41,0 +42 @@ covers no pre-image line and is refused with TargetError rather than naming line 41, which the patch does not touch.
- TestTheMutationTargetIsDerivedFromThePatchAlone and TestAPatchNoTargetFollowsFromIsRefused in internal/probe/target_test.go are table-driven over multi-file, multi-hunk, add-only, -U0, file-creating and hunkless patches.
- Round 12's unbounded-patch-target finding is answered by state.Layout.InSandbox in internal/state/mutate.go, the writer's own resolution exported so internal/cli/probe.go can refuse every path the patch addresses before a suite is run; it rejects an empty, absolute or escaping path and resolves symbolic links before comparing, and TestAPatchAimedOutOfTheSandboxIsRefused asserts exit 1 with the runner log absent.
- The quality gate passes: go test -race ./..., golangci-lint run, and scripts/deadcode.sh.

tasks.title: Revert the mutation on every outcome
tasks.acceptance:
- Invariant 6: the mutation is reverted even when the run fails, times out, or cr is killed, per §5.3.3.
- On the next invocation the check of §5.1.6 detects an unclean sandbox and recreates it before running anything.
- A test covers revert after a failing run, after a timeout, and after a killed process, asserting the sandbox is clean in the first two and recreated in the third.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Invariant 6 is structural rather than remembered: state.UnderSandboxMutation in internal/state/mutate.go is the only exported way to put a mutation into a sandbox, it arranges the undo in a defer before it calls the run, and applySandboxMutation is unexported with that wrapper as its single caller, so a failing run, a run cr killed for exceeding tests.timeout_seconds, and a panic all leave the sandbox as they found it; TestOnlyTheRevertingWrapperMutatesTheSandbox in internal/cli/norevert_test.go reads the tree and asserts the single caller, the defer's position ahead of the run, and that what it calls is the undo the apply handed back, and moving the revert out of the defer makes it fail.
- Section 5.3.3's remaining case is cr ceasing to exist, which no code inside the process can answer, and section 5.1.6's check on the next invocation is what does: sandbox.Ensure compares the sandbox against its post-setup baseline before every run and rebuilds one that differs, reporting the recreation as an honesty disclosure that survives --quiet.
- TestTheMutationIsRevertedAfterAFailingRun and TestTheMutationIsRevertedAfterATimeout in internal/cli/probe_test.go drive the command end to end and assert the sandbox holds the head's own file afterwards, with results failed and timeout recorded; TestAKilledProbeLeavesASandboxTheNextRunRecreates starts the real binary, waits until the mutation is on disk, sends it SIGKILL, asserts the mutation is still there, and then asserts the next invocation names src/Order.php in its section 5.1.6 notice and hands back a rebuilt checkout; internal/state/mutate_test.go covers the panic and the partial-apply paths at the wrapper itself.
- Dogfooded against deligoez/cr-qa PR 1 from a throwaway clone: the mutation of Order::shipping's uncovered arm recorded no-test-failed at target src/Order.php:34, a mutation of the covered subtotal recorded failed, a stale patch recorded error with no run, a hanging mutation under a three-second budget recorded timeout, and a SIGKILLed probe left the file changed until the next cr test rebuilt the sandbox; after every one of them the sandbox was byte-clean and the clone's status, refs and worktree list were unchanged.
- The quality gate passes: go test -race ./..., golangci-lint run, and scripts/deadcode.sh.

tasks.title: Decide mutation result by rung ladder
tasks.acceptance:
- The result is determined by the first matching rung of §5.3.4's ladder, which is total over every run — no run matches two rungs, and none matches none: the patch did not apply cleanly gives error with no tests run; killed for exceeding tests.timeout_seconds gives timeout; the runner could not be started or exited on a signal gives error; a known executed count of zero gives no-tests-selected; an undetermined executed or failed count gives inconclusive; a failed count of zero gives no-test-failed; otherwise failed.
- A table-driven test exercises all seven rungs and asserts exactly one fires for each input.
tasks.closed_reason:
- probe.Ladder returns the first matching rung's result, and internal/probe/mutation_test.go restates the seven rungs as standalone predicates over the whole Measured value so totality is checked rather than sampled: a patch that did not apply gives error, and the CLI reaches that rung with no run record at all because no tests were run.
- A run killed for exceeding tests.timeout_seconds gives timeout, and the table drives one that also died on a signal so the rung above error is the one that answers it.
- An unstarted runner and a runner that exited on a signal both give error, driven as two separate table rows.
- A known executed count of zero gives no-tests-selected, driven both with a zero failed count beside it and with none.
- An undetermined executed or failed count gives inconclusive, driven with neither count derivable, with only the executed count, and with only a failed count of zero.
- A failed count of zero beside a known non-zero executed count gives no-test-failed, which is the one rung §5.3.5 lets prove a gap.
- Any other run gives failed, driven by twelve tests of which one caught the mutation.
- The table exercises all seven rungs and asserts exactly one fires for each input, and a cross-product sweep of 216 runs repeats that assertion over every combination the ladder reads, with the counts spanning no count, a known zero, and a known non-zero.

tasks.title: Restrict proof to no-test-failed results
tasks.acceptance:
- Only no-test-failed proves the gap, and only when the probe's baseline run record has passed: true per §5.2.5, per §5.3.5.
- timeout, error, no-tests-selected, and inconclusive never support a probed grade, so an empty selection, an unparseable runner, and a run that never finished cannot manufacture evidence.
- A result of failed disproves the gap; cr records it and the agent does not raise the finding, per §5.3.7.
- A test asserts no-test-failed against a failing baseline does not reach probed.
tasks.closed_reason:
- probe.Proves is the only route to §5.3.5's answer and returns true on one path alone: the outcome's result is no-test-failed and the resolved baseline's §5.2.5 verdict is true. Both arguments are unforgeable, since Decide is Outcome's only constructor and Spec.Resolve is Baseline's, so the passing baseline is the record the resolution chose rather than one a caller had in hand.
- timeout, error, no-tests-selected and inconclusive reach no path to a probed grade, which internal/probe/proof_test.go asserts by driving every value §5.3.4's ladder can produce against both a passing and a failing baseline, and cr probe run reports establishes: nothing for each, so an empty selection, an unparseable runner and a run that never finished cannot manufacture evidence.
- probe.Disproves is §5.3.7's other direction and answers true for the failed result alone, asking nothing of the baseline because there is no assertion on that side.
- cr records the failed result as it always did and now reports establishes: no-gap beside it, in the JSON payload and in the terminal clause, so the agent is told not to raise the finding rather than left to re-derive it.
- proof_test.go asserts no-test-failed against a baseline whose passed is false does not prove the gap, and a companion test asserts a probe §5.1.7 voided proves and disproves nothing in either direction.

tasks.title: Carry the filter into evidence region
tasks.acceptance:
- A filtered run proves the gap only for the tests it selected. cr cannot establish that a filter selects the tests which would have caught the mutation, so it does not claim it, per §5.3.6.
- The filter is carried into the §8.1.7 evidence region, and §5.3.5's guarantee is not stated more widely than the empty selection it actually catches.
- A test asserts the filter string reaches the rendered evidence region verbatim.
tasks.closed_reason:
- The scope of a filtered run is stated as the run's own and never as the suite's: cr probe run's terminal clause for a proven gap says the tests this run selected did not notice the mutation, and render.ProbeEvidence names the filter rather than describing what it covers.
- Nothing cr writes says a filter selects the tests which would have caught the mutation, and the golden assertion in internal/render/evidence_test.go is what holds that: it compares the whole region rather than the filter row, so any sentence added beside the rows breaks the test.
- render.ProbeEvidence carries the filter into §8.1.7's region beside the kind, target, result and output tail, each under §5.5's own field name, and states no guarantee at all - so §5.3.5's cannot be stated more widely than the empty selection it catches, and the row is absent for an unfiltered run rather than carrying a value cr invented.
- A table drives seven filter spellings a real runner takes, including an alternation, a quoted expression and a backtick, and asserts each reaches the rendered region byte for byte, because an author checks the comment by re-running the filter cr names.

tasks.title: Place the gap test at template
tasks.acceptance:
- A gap probe distinguishes a missing behaviour from a missing test. The agent supplies a new test file targeting the suspected edge case, per §5.4.1.
- cr probe run <pr> --kind gap --test <file> --target <path:line> --filter <expr> places the test in the sandbox at the path given by the profile's tests.probe_path_template, runs it, removes it, and records the result, per §5.4.2.
- The template is fixed per profile so §5.1.6 can recognise a leftover artefact and the runner's own discovery still finds the file.
- An existing file at that path aborts with exit code 4.
tasks.closed_reason:
- A gap probe now runs as its own kind: `cr probe run --kind gap` no longer refuses, and `internal/probe/gap.go` answers the run with §5.4.3's ladder rather than §5.3.4's, so the two kinds never share a result vocabulary.
- §5.4.1's supplied test file arrives through `--test`, is read whole, and is stored as §5.5's `input`; `gapInput` refuses `--patch` for this kind and requires both `--test` and `--target`, so an experiment cr would never carry out is named at the flag rather than after a baseline suite has run.
- §5.4.2's cycle is `runGapProbe`: `profile.ProbePath` resolves the sandbox path from `tests.probe_path_template`, `state.UnderSandboxTestFile` places the file, the suite runs, the file and any directory the placement had to create are removed, and §5.5's record is written with kind `gap`, the supplied target and the unfiltered baseline §5.2.6 resolved.
- `TestAGapProbePlacesRunsRemovesAndRecords` asserts all four steps from evidence the command could not fake: the runner printed the supplied test's content, the baseline that ran first printed that no such file was there, the sandbox holds neither the file nor its directory afterwards, and the stored record carries every §5.5 row.
- The template stays fixed per profile: the path is resolved from the profile alone and the probe id is allocated before the placement, so §5.1.6's leftover glob — the same template with `<probe-id>` replaced by `*` — recognises an artefact a killed run left behind, and the file keeps the suffix the profile's `tests.globs` imply so the runner's own discovery finds it.
- `probe.IDTakenError` closes the window that reservation opens: the id is read outside §2.3.1's lock and checked against the allocation under it, so §5.5.2's reference can never be ambiguous, and nothing is written when it refuses.
- An existing file at the probe path aborts with exit code 4: `state.FreeInSandbox` is the writer's own resolution, asked before §5.2.6 performs a baseline, and `internal/cli/exit.go` codes `state.ProbeFileExistsError` as ExitState.
- `TestAGapProbeRefusesAnExistingFileAtTheProbePath` drives that through the command with a `sandbox.setup` that occupies the path, asserting exit 4, that no suite ran, and that the occupying file is byte-for-byte untouched — which is the point, since §5.1.6's leftover scan is scoped to untracked files and cannot catch this case.
- `TestAProbePathThatIsTakenOrLeavesTheSandboxIsRefused` holds the placement inside the sandbox as invariant 2 requires: a `..` path, an absolute path, an empty path and a directory symlinked out of the tree are all refused before anything runs.
- `profile.ProbePath` is no longer test-only: `deadcode ./...` falls from 91 to 90.

tasks.title: Remove the gap test after running
tasks.acceptance:
- The removal happens even when the run fails or times out, and §5.1.6 catches the case where it did not, per §5.4.2.
- A test covers removal after a failing run and after a timeout, and asserts a skipped removal is caught by the next cleanliness check.
tasks.closed_reason:
- §5.4.2's removal is structural rather than remembered: `state.applySandboxTestFile` is unexported, `state.UnderSandboxTestFile` is its only caller, and that wrapper binds the removal the write handed back and arranges it to run on every exit before it runs anything at all — so the removal happens on the error return, on the timeout, and on the panic unwind alike, and there is no call site for a later edit to return past.
- `TestOnlyTheRevertingWrappersTouchTheSandbox` is the AST guard, now a table over both doors: for each of `applySandboxMutation`/`UnderSandboxMutation` and `applySandboxTestFile`/`UnderSandboxTestFile` it asserts the writer has exactly one caller, that the caller is the wrapper, that the wrapper arranges its undo before running anything, and that the arranged call runs the undo the write returned. It was checked to bite by moving the removal to after the run, which fails it.
- The gap probe needs its own door rather than the mutation one, because the obligations are opposites: §5.3.2 rewrites a file that must exist and restores its content, while §5.4.2 creates a file that must not exist and deletes it — one door would carry a single undo that has to decide which it is, inside the one function invariant 6 exists to leave no decision in.
- `TestAProbeTestFileIsRemovedAfterAFailingRun` covers removal after a failing run at the state boundary and asserts the run's own failure still reaches the caller, so a removal that swallowed it cannot pass.
- `TestAProbeTestFileIsRemovedWhenTheRunPanics` covers the case a removal written after the run cannot answer at all, asserting both that the file is gone and that the panic still propagates.
- `TestTheGapProbeFileIsRemovedAfterAFailingRun` covers removal after a failing run through the command: the record carries §5.4.3's `failed` rather than §5.1.7's override, and neither the file nor the directory the placement created is left in the sandbox.
- `TestTheGapProbeFileIsRemovedAfterATimeout` covers removal after a timeout with a one-second budget against a runner that sleeps for two minutes once the file is placed, so what is measured is the kill and the removal that follows it.
- `TestAKilledGapProbeLeavesAFileTheNextRunRecreates` asserts the case where the removal did not happen: a real SIGKILL to a real `cr probe run` leaves the probe file on disk, and the next invocation's §5.1.6 check finds it, names it in the §11.1 disclosure, and recreates the sandbox before measuring anything.

tasks.title: Decide gap result by rung ladder
tasks.acceptance:
- The result is determined by the first matching rung of §5.4.3's ladder, which is total over every run: killed for exceeding tests.timeout_seconds gives timeout; the runner could not be started gives error; a known executed count of zero gives no-tests-selected, since the filter excluded the supplied test or it failed to load; an undetermined executed or failed count gives inconclusive; a failed count of zero gives passed; otherwise failed.
- Rung 4 exists for the same reason as §5.3.4's: without it a profile that cannot report counts would drive every gap probe to failed, and §5.4.4 would raise it at severity high on no evidence at all.
- Round 9 finding probe-ladder-asymmetry: the error rung also fires on a runner that exited on a signal, matching §5.3.4's rung 3. Without it a gap probe whose runner is killed by OOM or SIGSEGV after emitting output that tests.count_pattern still matches falls through to failed, and §5.4.4 makes a supported failed gap probe carry severity at least high — a crashed process becoming high-severity evidence.
- A table-driven test exercises every rung including the signal case.
tasks.closed_reason:
- `probe.GapLadder` is §5.4.3 in the section's own order: a run killed for `tests.timeout_seconds` is `timeout`, a runner that could not be started is `error`, a known executed count of zero is `no-tests-selected`, an undetermined executed or failed count is `inconclusive`, a failed count of zero is `passed`, and anything else is `failed`.
- Its input is `probe.GapMeasured` rather than a list of arguments, and it is a type of its own rather than a reuse of the mutation ladder's `Measured`: §5.4.3 has no rung for a patch that did not apply, so a field the ladder never reads would be one a caller could fill in and be answered nothing about.
- Rung 4 is spelled and reasoned in the code: without it a profile that cannot report counts drives every gap probe to `failed`, and §5.4.4 raises that at severity `high` on no evidence at all.
- Round 9's probe-ladder-asymmetry is implemented: rung 2 fires on `Unstarted || ExitCode < 0`, so a runner killed by the out-of-memory killer or one that segmentation-faults after printing output `tests.count_pattern` still matches reaches `error` rather than `failed`, and a crashed process cannot become high-severity evidence. `internal/cli` hands the ladder the runner's own exit status, which `sandbox.Run` reports as a negative code for a process that died on a signal.
- `TestTheGapLadderAnswersEveryRunWithExactlyOneRung` restates every rung as a standalone predicate over the whole input and requires exactly one to match, which is the totality claim itself rather than a sample of its consequences — a table that compared six answers would see neither a second rung firing nor a run that fired none.
- Every rung is exercised, the signal case included: a crashed runner that printed counts rung 6 could read, a timeout that also died on a signal, an empty selection that reports zero failures, an undetermined count beside a zero failed count, and both terminal rungs.
- `TestEveryRunTheGapLadderCanSeeMatchesOneRung` drives every combination of the fields the ladder reads, with the counts spanning no count, a known zero and a known non-zero, so a rung widened by one boundary or an order swapped by one place has nowhere to hide.
- `TestNeitherLadderProducesTheOtherKindsResult` holds §5.5's per-kind vocabularies apart at the point a value is chosen: no gap run answers `no-test-failed` and no mutation run answers `passed`, which is the pair that sits on the same rung and means opposite things.
- The gate's mutation run found one real gap and it is closed: nothing constructed a `probe.IDTakenError`, so `TestAReservedProbeIdAnotherRunTookIsRefused` now spends the id under a first record and asserts the second is refused with exit 4 and writes nothing.
- `TestAGapProbeWhoseRunnerExitedOnASignalIsAnError` drives the signal case through the command against a runner that prints a matching recap and then segmentation-faults, asserting the record carries `error` beside the counts the rung overrode.

tasks.title: Support a finding only with baseline
tasks.acceptance:
- A failed gap probe means either the behaviour is wrong or the supplied test is wrong, and cr cannot distinguish the two. The result is recorded and the probe output offered as a reproduction, per §5.4.4.
- The probe is treated as supporting the finding only when its baseline passed per §5.2.5 and the finding's claim field names the claim the test asserts; otherwise it does not support a probed grade, which leaves the record argued under §6.2 and therefore a question under §6.3.
- A test asserts a failed gap probe with a mismatched claim field leaves the record argued.
- §5.4.4's condition is that the finding's claim field names a claim mapped to the finding's unit, checked mechanically against mapping.ndjson.
- Round 12 findings axis-availability-coupling and unearned-probed-grade, assigned here: when the intent axis is unavailable per §4.6.6 the mapping is empty, so no gap probe can reach probed in a repository that has tests but no tracker. The implementation reports that coupling through the §4.5.4 honesty channel rather than failing silently. Conversely, on a mapped unit the claim test is weak and target is the agent's --target, so the implementation must not present a gap probe as proving more than §5.4.4 states.
tasks.closed_reason:
- probe.Reproduces in internal/probe/support.go is §5.4.4's first half: a gap probe whose result is `failed` says the supplied test failed and nothing more, because cr cannot distinguish a wrong behaviour from a wrong test.
- The result is recorded exactly as the run produced it, the record keeps the runner's output_tail, and render.ProbeEvidence prints kind, target, filter, result and output_tail verbatim, so the output reaches the author as a reproduction rather than as a conclusion cr composed.
- probe.Supports is the whole of §5.4.4's condition and is one boolean expression: Reproduces(record) and baseline.Passed() and the mapping's own answer.
- The two facts an agent could otherwise talk cr into are types with one constructor each, the way probe.Proves already reads §5.3.5: a Baseline exists only where a stored run record §5.2.6 admits was resolved, and a ClaimMapping exists only where MapClaim asked §4.1.6's stored pairs.
- Record.ResolveBaseline resolves the run §5.5's baseline column names by id and still applies §5.2.6's fence, so a run carrying a probe, a contaminated one, or one at another head cannot become the verdict §5.4.4 reads.
- Otherwise the probe supports no probed grade, which leaves the record argued under §6.2 and a question under §6.3, and the reason printed says which of the two conditions decided.
- MapClaim is the mechanical check of §5.4.4's second condition against mapping.ndjson, scoped to the round because §3.4.6 makes a unit id round-scoped.
- TestAFailedGapProbeSupportsARecordOnlyOnABaselineAndAMappedClaim drives a mismatched claim field through cr record and asserts the probe supports nothing, alongside a red baseline, an absent claim field, and a probe from another head.
- TestAFailedGapProbeSupportsAFindingOnlyOnAPassingBaselineAndAMappedClaim drives the same six conditions at the probe package, including a pair belonging to an earlier round.
- Round 12's axis-availability-coupling is held by probe.GapUnmappable, which satisfies finding.HonestyDisclosure and reaches the reader through the channel §11.1 exempts from --quiet whenever the empty mapping of §4.6.6 is what decided a failed gap probe.
- Round 12's unearned-probed-grade is held in the opposite direction: the reported verb is supports rather than proves, the sentence says the probe establishes no more than that the supplied test failed and names target as the one the probe was given, and the tests assert the words prove, verif and confirm never appear.
- Dogfooded against deligoez/cr-qa PR 1 under an isolated CR_HOME: a failed gap probe p1 on a mapped claim reports supports true, the same probe on a record naming a claim mapped to another unit reports supports false, and a second CR_HOME whose key pattern matches nothing reports the coupling through honesty; the repository under review stayed clean, per invariant 2.

tasks.title: Deny probed grade to passed gaps
tasks.acceptance:
- A passed gap probe establishes that the behaviour is present, not that the suite lacks a test — only §5.3's no-test-failed establishes that, per §5.4.5.
- It does not support a probed grade, and neither may timeout, error, no-tests-selected, or inconclusive; a record resting on one falls to argued under §6.2 and is posted as a question.
- A test asserts each of the five results leaves the record argued.
tasks.closed_reason:
- probe.Present is §5.4.5's first sentence: a passed gap probe establishes that the behaviour the supplied test asserts is present.
- It is kept apart from the missing test only §5.3's no-test-failed establishes, in the type's own documentation and in every sentence cr prints about it.
- probe.Supports refuses a probed grade to passed, timeout, error, no-tests-selected and inconclusive by construction, because Reproduces names the one result that is not among them.
- A record resting on any of the five therefore falls to argued under §6.2 and is asked as a question under §6.3, and cr record says so in the reason it prints for that record.
- TestNoGapResultOtherThanFailedSupportsAFinding drives all five at the probe package with §5.4.4's two conditions met in full, so the result is the only thing refusing support.
- TestEachResultSection545NamesLeavesTheRecordArgued drives the same five through cr record and asserts each reason names §5.4.5 and says where the record lands.
- cr probe run no longer reports undecided for every gap probe: gapEstablishedBy leaves only failed undecided, answers passed with §5.4.5's own reading, and answers the other four with nothing.
- TestWhatEachGapResultIsReportedToEstablish covers all six values of §5.4.3's vocabulary and asserts every token carries a clause naming the section that decided.
- Dogfooded against deligoez/cr-qa PR 1: a supplied test asserting shipping is 0.0 at exactly 50.00 recorded passed and reported establishes behaviour, the same test under a filter matching nothing recorded inconclusive and reported establishes nothing, and cr record refused both a probed grade with a reason naming §5.4.5.

tasks.title: Enforce the gap probe severity bounds
tasks.acceptance:
- Severity is at least high only when the probe supports the finding per §5.4.4, and at most medium for a passed gap probe per §5.4.5.
- Round 8 finding unenforced-severity-bound: cr record is named as the enforcer and rejects with exit code 1 a gap-probe-backed record whose severity violates either bound, naming the record, the probe, and the result; cr post re-checks the bound after triage the way §7.2.2 re-checks the grade. Without a named enforcer both MUSTs bind nobody, since severity is agent-written and §6.1.3 checks presence alone.
- The cost of leaving it unenforced is a misdirected human: severity is what the reviewer triages on under the blocking cap of §1.6.2, so a probe that proved only a missing test could present its finding as the loudest item in the draft.
- A test asserts both bounds reject at record time and are re-checked at post time.
tasks.closed_reason:
- finding.GapAtLeastHigh is §5.4.4's floor: a record a failed gap probe supports carries severity high or critical, and the section's "only when" limits when the floor applies rather than which way it points.
- Nothing lowers it once it applies, and nothing raises a record that no probe supports, so a crashed runner cannot reach the floor at all: a signalled process is error on §5.4.3's second rung and never failed.
- finding.GapAtMostMedium is §5.4.5's ceiling: a record resting on a gap probe that supports no probed grade carries medium or low.
- The ceiling is read over all five results §5.4.5 names rather than passed alone, because the capping sentence has no subject of its own and the nearest one is the paragraph's, "a record resting on one" of the five; the task's acceptance names only the passed case, and the broader reading is the one implemented.
- finding.CheckGapSeverity is the single named enforcer both bounds bind through, and it takes the moment as an Actor argument so the record-time refusal and the post-time re-check cannot be two readings of §5.4 that disagree.
- cr record calls it before it writes anything and rejects with exit code 1, naming the record, the probe, the result, the bound's section and the severities the record must carry instead.
- internal/cli/exit.go maps finding.GapSeverityError onto §11.2's code 1, and gradingGap passes no probe when §5.5.3 keeps one from another head out of this round's grading, so a stale experiment refuses nothing.
- Without a named enforcer both MUSTs bind nobody, since severity is agent-written and §6.1.3 checks presence alone.
- The cost of leaving it unenforced is a misdirected human: severity is what the reviewer triages on under §1.6.2's blocking cap, so a probe that showed the behaviour working could present its record as the loudest item in the draft.
- TestBothGapSeverityBoundsAreEnforced drives every severity of §6.1 against every result of §5.4.3, including the unsupported failed probe that has no bound and the error result round 9's ladder finding is about.
- TestTheSameBoundIsCheckedAtRecordTimeAndAtPostTime asserts the same record and probe are refused for cr record, cr post --confirm and cr post --reconcile, each refusal naming the moment it came from; §7.2.2's re-check is therefore a call to this function, and wiring that call is the post command's own task, which v0.1 has not built yet.
- TestRecordRefusesASeverityEitherGapBoundForbids drives both bounds through the command, asserting exit code 1, the named record, probe and result, and that findings.ndjson is untouched.
- TestAnUnrecognisedSeverityMeetsNeitherBound holds the membership test open: a value §6.1 does not name satisfies neither bound, so it is refused wherever a bound applies rather than ranked into whichever half a comparison chose.
- gremlins over ./internal reported three surviving mutants in this cycle's code, all documented contracts with no boundary test, and all three are now killed: the coupling's len(unmapped) > 0, namedClaim's empty-claim branch, and the refusal's list of the severities the bound leaves.
- Each kill was verified by applying the mutation and reverting it, so the assertion is known to bite rather than assumed to.
- Dogfooded against deligoez/cr-qa PR 1: a record on the supported failed probe p1 at medium was refused with §5.4.4 named, a record on the passed probe p2 at critical was refused with §5.4.5 named, both exited 1, and nothing reached findings.ndjson.

tasks.title: Define the probe record fields
tasks.acceptance:
- The probe record carries every row of the §5.5 field table: id of the form p<n>, kind, head, input, filter, result, tests_run, tests_failed, baseline, target, duration_ms, output_tail.
- baseline is the id of the run record at the same head measuring the same tests on unmutated, un-probed code: for mutation, the run with this probe's filter; for gap, the unfiltered run.
- target is path:line, always side RIGHT since probes run against the sandbox at head; for mutation derived from the patch per §5.3.2, for gap supplied and validated as §6.2.3 validates a citation.
- A finding references at most one probe, by id, per §5.5.2.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/probe/record.go declares Record in §5.5's own table order and carries every row of it — id, kind, head, input, filter, result, tests_run, tests_failed, baseline, target, duration_ms, output_tail — with §2.3.3's round beside the head it travels with.
- The table is held as data in a fields list and checkRecordFields runs at package initialisation, so a field added to the struct without a row in the section, or a row the struct drops, panics the binary rather than reaching probes.ndjson unannounced.
- TestTheProbeFieldTableIsTheOneTheSpecWrites transcribes §5.5's rows from the spec and asserts the table equals them, so the table is checked against the section rather than against itself.
- TestEveryRowOfTheTableReachesTheWire marshals a filled record and asserts the key set is exactly the table's, then asserts a record with no counts and no filter omits exactly the three rows §5.5's Required column answers no.
- baseline is the id of the run record §5.2.6 admits at the same head on unmutated, un-probed code, and internal/probe/baseline.go's Referenced is the one place that answers which: Spec{Filter: filter} for a mutation probe and the unfiltered spec for a gap probe, whose test does not exist in the baseline.
- Spec.stands admits only a run at the head carrying the same filter, no probe id, and no contamination, and TestTheBaselineOfAKindIsTheRunTheSectionNames covers both kinds; nothing there was rebuilt for this task.
- target is a path:line, always side RIGHT because §5.1.6 admits the sandbox only at the round's head, and it is derived for a mutation probe by probe.Target from the patch per §5.3.2 while --target is refused for that kind.
- For a gap probe the target is supplied, and probe.CheckTarget now validates it as §6.2.3 validates a citation: ParseTarget holds the value to a path and a canonically spelled line, then the path is resolved against the head under review and a path the head does not hold as a file and a line past the file's end are both refused.
- The reader is git.FileAtRevision bound to the repository and the round's head, which is the same reader §6.2.3 resolves a citation through, so the two rules read one tree; internal/cli/exit.go maps InvalidTargetError onto ExitValidation, §11.2's code 1, which is the code §6.2.3 fixes.
- The check runs in runGapProbe before §5.2.6 performs a baseline suite and before §5.6.1's lock is taken, and gapInput asks the shape before any file is opened, so a target naming nowhere costs no run at all.
- TestAGapProbeTargetIsAPathAndALineNumber covers fifteen spellings including the last-colon separator, a padded line, a signed line and line zero; TestAGapProbeTargetIsResolvedAgainstTheHead covers both §6.2.3 refusals and both accepted boundaries; TestAnUnreadableHeadIsNotARejectedTarget asserts a reader failure is returned unchanged rather than reported as the agent's data.
- TestAGapProbeRefusesATargetTheHeadDoesNotHold drives six of those through the command and asserts exit code 1 and an absent runner log, so the refusal is proven to come before any suite ran.
- A finding references at most one probe and does so by id: internal/finding/finding.go declares Probe as a single optional string, and TestAFindingReferencesAtMostOneProbeByID asserts the field's kind is a string rather than a slice, asserts its wire name and omitempty, and asserts §6.1's table marks the row optional, which is §5.5.2's at most.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... && golangci-lint run && ./scripts/deadcode.sh, with gofmt -l internal empty.
Out of scope and left to the tasks that own them: §5.5's per-kind result vocabulary belongs to probe-result-vocabularies, §5.5.1's immutability and §5.5.3's grading fence to probe-record-invariants, and §6.2.2's containment of a probe target inside a record's anchor to probed-grade-validation.

tasks.title: Keep per-kind result vocabularies disjoint
tasks.acceptance:
- The result vocabulary is per kind and is not shared, per §5.5: mutation takes no-test-failed, failed, no-tests-selected, inconclusive, error, timeout; gap takes passed, failed, no-tests-selected, inconclusive, error, timeout.
- A record carrying a result outside its kind's vocabulary is rejected.
- A test asserts passed on a mutation probe and no-test-failed on a gap probe are both rejected.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/probe/vocabulary.go closes §5.5's second table per kind and shares neither row: a mutation probe carries one of no-test-failed, failed, no-tests-selected, inconclusive, error, timeout, and a gap probe one of passed, failed, no-tests-selected, inconclusive, error, timeout.
- The sets live in one place rather than beside each ladder, which is what §5.5's "MUST NOT be shared" asks for; mutation.go, gap.go and outcome.go each said the closing belonged in one place and now name that place, and nothing else in them changed.
- Results returns a kind's vocabulary in §5.5's order as a copy, and TestAKindsVocabularyCannotBeWidenedByItsReader writes through the returned slice and asserts the closed set is unchanged.
- A record carrying a result outside its kind's vocabulary is rejected: probe.CheckResult refuses it and internal/cli/probe.go calls that at the top of appendProbe, which is the one door onto probes.ndjson.
- The check sits ahead of the run record's own append, so a refused probe leaves neither a probe line nor the run line that would have named it, and §5.2.6 never has to read a run pointing at a probe that does not exist.
- It is asked of the record rather than of the ladder, because a ladder answers only for runs that went through it: §5.1.7's override replaces whatever it produced, a record can be assembled from fields, and a kind the command did not recognise reaches no ladder at all.
- A kind outside §5.5's two is refused on the same call, since its vocabulary is empty and the refusal says there is no third kind rather than showing an empty set.
- internal/cli/exit.go maps OutsideVocabularyError onto ExitValidation, §11.2's code 1, alongside the other records cr refuses to store.
- TestAResultOutsideItsKindsVocabularyIsRejected asserts passed on a mutation probe and no-test-failed on a gap probe are both rejected, and covers seven further spellings including the empty result, a capitalised one, a padded one, an unknown kind and the empty kind.
- TestAProbeResultOutsideItsKindsVocabularyIsNeverStored drives the same two crossings plus an unknown kind through recordProbe with a run record attached, and asserts exit code 1 with probes.ndjson and runs.ndjson both still empty.
- TestTheResultVocabularyIsTheOneTheSpecWritesPerKind transcribes §5.5's two rows as literal strings so a renamed constant both the ladder and the vocabulary followed would still fail.
- TestEveryResultItsKindAdmitsIsAccepted and TestEveryResultItsKindAdmitsIsStored walk all twelve admitted values through the check and through the write, so a check that refused everything would fail too.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... && golangci-lint run && ./scripts/deadcode.sh, with gofmt -l internal empty.
Out of scope: §5.5.1's immutability and §5.5.3's grading fence belong to probe-record-invariants, and §5.6.4's round cap to probe-round-cap.

tasks.title: Freeze probe records at their head
tasks.acceptance:
- Probe records are immutable once written, per §5.5.1.
- Probe records whose head differs from the current head are never used to grade a finding in the current round, per §5.5.3.
- A test asserts a write to an existing probe record is refused, and that a previous-head probe cannot grade.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Probe records are immutable once written, per §5.5.1: appendProbe refuses a record whose id one already on file carries, and internal/cli/noproberewrite_test.go proves from the abstract syntax tree that probes.ndjson has exactly one writer in the whole tree and that it is state.AppendStamped in appendProbe.
- AppendStamped is the only write that can satisfy §5.5.1, because it carries the bytes the file already holds through untouched; WriteStamped, the other door §2.3.3 opens onto a stamped file, restamps every record it is handed and would rewrite every earlier probe with the round now being written, so the guard fails any call naming the file that is neither the read nor that append.
- The guard was proven to bite: a scratch file calling state.WriteStamped with state.FileProbes made it fail naming the offending function, and was then removed.
- TestAStoredProbeRecordIsNeverRewritten stores a gap probe, attempts a second write under the id §5.4.2 fixed before the placement, and asserts the refusal plus probes.ndjson byte for byte unchanged; the assertion is on the bytes rather than the count, because a rewrite that replaced the line would satisfy a length check while repointing every finding that names the id.
