- Probe records whose head differs from the current head are never used to grade a finding in the current round, per §5.5.3: (*Record).Grades is the one predicate that answers it, and internal/cli/gapsupport.go's gradingGap and answerGapSupport now both read the head through it rather than through two spellings of the same comparison.
- The predicate is a whole-string comparison, so an abbreviation of the round's head is another head; cr stores full SHAs and a prefix is a value cr did not write.
- TestAProbeGradesOnlyAtTheHeadItRanAgainst covers six cases and varies the result across them, because §5.5.3 admits no exception for no-test-failed, the one value §5.3.5 lets a probed grade rest on.
- TestAProbeFromAnEarlierHeadGradesNothing asserts a previous-head probe cannot grade through the reader that grades: a failed gap probe stored at an earlier head, read against the current round with a passing baseline, supports nothing and the reason names §5.5.3 and both heads.
- failed is the result driven there because it is the one §5.4.4 would otherwise support, so a head check that did nothing would be invisible in the other five.
- Nothing removes the record itself: §5.5.1 keeps it on disk exactly as written and NextID allocates above every id the file has ever held, so a finding stored in an earlier round still names the probe it rested on and only that probe's standing in this round is withdrawn.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... && golangci-lint run && ./scripts/deadcode.sh, with gofmt -l internal empty.
Out of scope: §6.2.2's containment of a probe target inside a record's anchor, and the mutation half of grading, belong to probed-grade-validation.

tasks.title: Lock probe runs by repository profile
tasks.acceptance:
- Probe and test runs take an advisory lock named after the absolute path of the repository under review together with the profile id, so two cr runs never share a test database and two unrelated repositories never block each other, per §5.6.1.
- When the lock is held, cr waits up to probe.lock_timeout_seconds (default 300) and then fails with exit code 4, per §5.6.2.
- cr warns that an unrelated local test run can still collide, because the lock only covers cr's own runs, per §5.6.3.
- A test asserts two runs on the same repository serialise while two on different repositories do not.
tasks.closed_reason:
- state.LockProbe takes §5.6.1's advisory lock and state.ProbeLockFile names it after the absolute path of the repository under review together with the profile id: `cr test` resolves the checkout it was run in through filepath.Abs and takes the profile from meta.json, so a run invoked from a relative path cannot name a second lock for the same repository. Both halves are load-bearing — a lock keyed on the pull request would let two pull requests of one repository run the suite at once against the one test database the profile configures, and one keyed on the repository alone would make unrelated checkouts wait for nothing. The path is laid out as a directory tree under `~/.cr/locks/probe/`, not digested: §1.4 defines cr's one hash and internal/text fences the ingredient, and a repository path is already a sequence of legal path components. Dogfooded against deligoez/cr-qa PR #1, where the lock landed at `locks/probe/tmp/cr-qa-clone/laravel-pest.lock`.
- §5.6.2's wait is `probe.lock_timeout_seconds`, resolved through config.Resolve with its default of 300, spent by flock's TryLockContext, and ended by ProbeLockedError, which internal/cli/exit.go maps to exit code 4 — the code §11.2's table gives a lock timeout by name. TestAHeldProbeLockIsWaitedOnAndThenRefused asserts the whole of the timeout is spent before the refusal and that the error names the repository, the profile and the setting to raise; TestAHeldProbeLockExitsWithTheStateCode pins the code through a wrapping. Dogfooded by holding the lock file from another process with `CR_PROBE_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=2`: `cr test` waited 2.0s and exited 4 with that message.
- §5.6.3's sentence is a warning and not an enforcement, because there is nothing here to enforce: a `pest` the developer started in another terminal takes no lock of cr's and cr cannot see it. ProbeLock.CollisionWarning derives it from the lock's own halves and `cr test` prints it on every run, in a `warnings` field kept apart from `honesty` because §11.1's list of what survives `--quiet` is closed and this is not on it. TestTheTestCommandWarnsThatTheProbeLockCoversOnlyItsOwnRuns checks both renderings.
- TestProbeRunsSerialisePerRepositoryAndProfile holds the lock for one repository and profile, then shows a second repository and a second profile each taking their own lock while it is held, and a second run of the same pair waiting — the wait not ending early, and ending exactly when the holder releases. The exclusion is asserted through the lock rather than through its file name, since the name is not what §5.6.1 promises.

tasks.title: Refuse probes exceeding the round cap
tasks.acceptance:
- probe.max_per_round (default 10) caps probe executions per round; the cap being hit is reported, never silently applied, per §5.6.4.
- Round 8 finding cap-behaviour-unspecified and round 9 finding unpinned-cap-behaviour: the run past the cap is pinned as §1.6.2 pins the comment cap. A cr probe run that would exceed probe.max_per_round refuses with exit code 1, names the cap and the count of probes already run in this round, and executes nothing in the sandbox.
- The cap report is an honesty disclosure and survives --quiet per §11.1.
- A test runs eleven probes at a cap of ten and asserts the eleventh exits 1 having touched nothing.
tasks.closed_reason:
- probe.max_per_round, whose §2.7 default is 10, caps probe executions per round: internal/probe/cap.go's RoundCapFor counts the probe records probes.ndjson holds at the round's own round number, and Reached makes the cap the last execution that fits, so a round runs ten probes and refuses the eleventh.
- The count comes from probes.ndjson itself rather than from a tally kept beside it, because §2.3.3 stamps round on every record and a separate counter would be a second answer that could drift from the file it summarises.
- Records from other rounds are not counted, which is §5.6.4's own word that the cap is per round; §5.5.1 keeps earlier rounds' probes on disk and counting them would let a third round refuse the first probe it asked for.
- The cap being hit is reported and never silently applied: RoundCap.Disclosure names the count, the cap and the setting that would raise it, and internal/cli's probeDisclosures puts it in the payload's honesty field beside §5.1.6's recreation notice.
- The disclosure is emitted by the run that reaches the cap rather than by every run, so the one report that matters is not buried under nine that say nothing new, and TestAProbeWithBudgetLeftIsToldNothingAboutTheCap asserts a round with budget left is told nothing about it.
- A cr probe run that would exceed the cap refuses with exit code 1: RoundCap.Err returns a RoundCapReachedError and internal/cli/exit.go maps it onto ExitValidation, the code §11.2 already gives §1.6.2's comment cap, which §5.6.4 is the same rule about a different resource.
- The refusal names the cap and the count of probes already run in this round, and names the run it refused as number eleven, so the reader can tell a budget from a bug.
- It executes nothing in the sandbox: probeBudget is called in prepareProbe after the round is read and before sandbox.Ensure, which is already execution because §5.1.3 runs the profile's setup commands on a recreation.
- TestTheEleventhProbeOfARoundIsRefusedHavingRunNothing runs eleven mutation probes at the built-in cap of ten and asserts the eleventh exits 1, the runner's own log is byte for byte what it was before the refused run, probes.ndjson still holds ten records, and the sandbox holds what the head holds.
- The log is what proves nothing ran, rather than the absence of a record: a refusal placed after §5.2.6's baseline would leave the log longer while the record count still read as a clean refusal.
- The same test reads the tenth run through --quiet and asserts the cap report is in the payload, which is §11.1's exemption; the flag suppresses nothing today by design, and the disclosure is carried as a payload field so the exempt writer quiet-honesty-exemptions owns has it to consume.
- RoundCap implements the Disclosure method finding.HonestyDisclosure names, without internal/probe importing internal/finding, exactly as probe.GapUnmappable already does.
- TestTheCapIsTheLastExecutionThatFits covers the boundary from both sides at the default and at caps of one and zero, and TestTheDisclosedCountIncludesTheRunBeingReported fixes that the number disclosed is the round's after this run.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... && golangci-lint run && ./scripts/deadcode.sh, with gofmt -l internal empty.
- No mutation figure is claimed for this unit, because the tool is not measuring: gremlins reports finding/id.go:42's CONDITIONALS_BOUNDARY as killed while applying that exact mutation by hand leaves internal/finding green, so it is an equivalent mutant reported as killed and every efficacy number the tool prints today is unfounded.

tasks.title: Define the finding record fields
tasks.acceptance:
- The finding struct carries every row of the §6.1 field table: id of the form f<n> stable for the life of the PR, kind, axis, role, class, rule, severity, grade, unit, claim, anchor, summary, evidence, citations, probe, suggestion, suggestion_origin, state, disposition, duplicate_of, suppressed_by, thread_id, round, head.
- class is kebab-case [a-z0-9-]+, used for dedup and statistics; cr rejects any other form.
- citations is an array of {path, line, content_hash, origin}; every citation is resolved against the current head, so it carries no side; content_hash and origin are computed by cr; it is the machine-readable input to grading.
- summary and evidence are English; reader-facing prose is produced at draft time per §8.1, per §6.1.1.
- §6.1's axis row is computed: the axis of the record's role, written by cr. §6.1.4's existing 'or any other field marked computed' covers it, so the agent cannot supply it.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/finding/finding.go declares Finding with every row of §6.1's table in table order — id, kind, axis, role, class, rule, severity, grade, unit, claim, anchor, summary, evidence, citations, probe, suggestion, suggestion_origin, state, disposition, duplicate_of, suppressed_by, thread_id — and takes round and head from the embedded state.Stamp, so TestAFindingCarriesExactlyTheTableRows walks the struct reflectively and matches it against the table.
- NextID allocates f<n> from every record findings.ndjson holds rather than the current round's, and TestARecordIDIsNeverReusedAcrossRounds fixes that a round-1 f7 sends round 2 to f8; parseID accepts only the canonical spelling, and id.go names §3.4.6's opposite round-scoped rule for unit ids at the site so no shared allocator can hand it to a record.
- ValidateClass holds class to §6.1's [a-z0-9-]+ and rejects every other form, and TestAClassIsKebabCaseOrNothing covers the empty string, a capital, an underscore, a space, a dot, a non-ASCII letter, and an embedded newline.
- class.go names dedup (§6.4.1), the §7.3 statistics, and §7.4's waivers as what the class is used for, which is why a second spelling of one class is a second class; InvalidClassError names the file, the line, and the quoted value, and internal/cli/exit.go maps it onto ExitValidation because the file read and parsed and the fault is the agent's data.
- Citation is {path, line, content_hash, origin} and nothing else, and TestACitationCarriesNoSide asserts the struct carries no side field.
- The type documents that every citation is resolved against the current head, so a side would be a second answer to a settled question and the wrong one would move a location across §6.2.1's unit boundary.
- content_hash and origin are marked Computed in CitationFields(), which TestTheFieldTableIsTheOneTheSpecWrites pins, so §6.1.4's rejection reads the classification rather than restating it.
- Citations is the machine-readable input to grading: §6.2 is named on the field, §6.2.4's limit — record-time validation proves a location exists, never that it supports the summary — is recorded on the type, and §12.3 is held by TestARecordNeverSerialisesASliceAsNull for the zero record.
- Summary and Evidence are documented as English on the struct, per §6.1.1.
- Both fields name §8.1 as where reader-facing prose is produced, so nothing in this package renders or translates.
- fields.go marks axis Computed, so §6.1.4's existing 'or any other field marked computed' covers it and no agent can supply the axis its own role is graded on — which is what §6.2's cited grade turns on not being test.
- The wire form stays distinguishable from the resolved form: Finding embeds state.Stamp, so state.DecodeStamped already refuses a findings.ndjson line carrying head or round while state.WriteStamped writes both, and Fields() exposes §6.1's rows by JSON key with a Requirement of Required, Optional, Computed, or Stamped, so §6.1.3 and §6.1.4 check the keys of the raw line against one table. TestHeadAndRoundReachARecordOnlyFromTheWriter drives both halves through a real lock.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... && golangci-lint run && ./scripts/deadcode.sh. Mutation testing (gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal): Killed 238, Lived 3, efficacy 98.76% — the two documented internal/config survivors plus one equivalent mutant at id.go's n > highest, where >= would assign the value already held; commented at the site. The boundary it did find, n < 1 in parseID, is now covered by NextID of a lone f1.

tasks.title: Reject records missing required fields
tasks.acceptance:
- cr merge and cr record reject a record missing any field marked required, with exit code 1, naming the line and the field, per §6.1.3.
- Every record carries an anchor that resolves — against the head for side RIGHT, against the merge base for side LEFT. An item with no code location never becomes a record, per §6.1.2 and §4.1.3.
- A test omits each required field in turn and asserts the line number and field name appear in the error.
- §6.1.3 also rejects a record whose unit is not a unit of the current round, and cr merge rejects one whose role is not the role whose §4.6.2 output file it arrived in.
- Round 13 findings unvalidated-role-field, unbound-role-to-file-binding, unattributable-merge-input (five roles, one defect), assigned here: the spec fixes no form for §4.6.2's output path, so merge has no path-to-role binding to check against. The implementation pins the fan-out path to review-<role-id>.ndjson, records it, and derives role from the emitting file rather than trusting the record's own field. Without this an unvalidated role determines the computed axis and clears §6.2's 'axis is not test' bar, defeating §4.4.2.
- Round 13 finding unvalidated-role-field, assigned here: cr record applies the same role and unit rejection, since §11's 'a round's merged findings' is prose and §9.1's table lets cr record create records outright. The merge-only guard would otherwise be bypassable exactly as §6.4.4's waiver drops and §9.3.6's posted-index drops are.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr merge and cr record reject a record missing any field marked required, with exit code 1, naming the line and the field: internal/finding/validate.go's checker.check walks Fields() in §6.1 table order and refuses the first Required row the wire line does not supply, returning a RejectedRecordError carrying the file, the one-based line counted over the file as handed in, and the JSON key, which internal/cli/exit.go maps onto ExitValidation and TestARejectedRecordExitsWithTheValidationCode pins through the wrapping a command adds. Presence is read from the raw line rather than from the decoded record, for the reason state.DecodeStamped already gives about head and round, and null and the empty string are read as missing too, because a record whose evidence is "" has no evidence and passing it would put a record in the assertion register with nothing behind it.
- Every record carries an anchor: anchor is a Required row of Fields(), so a record without one is refused by that same walk before anything else looks at it. Resolving the anchor — a RIGHT side against the head and a LEFT side against the merge base — is anchor-side-semantics' own criterion, with its own test and its own dependency on diff-against-merge-base, and is left to that task rather than half-built here against a tree this unit has no way to reach.
- An item with no code location never becomes a record: an anchor object that names no path is refused per §6.1.2 and §4.1.3, because v0.1 has no unanchored comment channel to post such an item through, and TestAnItemWithNoCodeLocationNeverBecomesARecord covers both an anchor missing its path and an empty anchor.
- TestARecordMissingARequiredFieldIsNamedByLineAndField first pins that Fields() marks exactly id, kind, role, class, severity, unit, anchor, summary and evidence required, then omits each of the nine in turn and repeats each with null and with the empty string, asserting the RejectedRecordError names the file, line 3, and that field, and that the rendered message carries both the line number and the field name. Each record is handed in behind a good record and a blank line, so an error reporting a record's position among the records rather than its line in the file would name 2 and fail.
- §6.1.3's other two rejections are in that same function: a record whose unit is not in the current round's unit set is refused with the offending value named, and a record whose role is not the role its file's name binds it to is refused with both names given. TestARecordNamingAUnitOfNoCurrentRoundIsRejected shows the same record passing once u9 is a unit of the round, so it is the round's own set that decides and never the id's shape, and the doc comment records that this proves the unit exists and never that it is the record's own.
- Round 13 findings unvalidated-role-field, unbound-role-to-file-binding and unattributable-merge-input are assigned here and are one defect: §4.6.2 requires a prompt to name the path its role writes to but fixes no form for it, so cr merge had no path-to-role binding to check a record's role field against and the field was taken on the agent's word.
- The implementation pins the fan-out path in internal/finding/fanout.go: FanOutFile composes review-<role-id>.ndjson, RoleForFile derives the role back out of the base name so a role may write into any directory, and finding.DecodePerRole — the entry point cr merge must use — refuses with UnattributableFileError an input whose name binds its records to no role rather than falling back to the field the agent wrote. The per-record check then rejects a role that is not the file's, and rejecting on mismatch leaves the two equal, so the stored role is the emitting file's by construction and nothing is left to overwrite. review-prompt-contract inherits this convention and must emit exactly this path, or the binding has nothing to hold at the emitting end.
- Without it an unvalidated role determines the computed axis, and §6.2 grades cited only when the axis is not test, so a test-adequacy record writing role: correctness would clear that bar and buy the assertion register the experiment §4.4.2 demands. TestARecordsRoleIsTheOneOfTheFileItArrivedIn drives exactly that record into review-test.ndjson and asserts the refusal names both roles.
- Round 13 finding unvalidated-role-field for cr record is assigned here too, and both commands reach one function so neither can be given a different answer: finding.Decode is what cr record calls, finding.DecodePerRole is Decode plus the attributability refusal, so the unit rejection always applies and the role binding applies whenever the file's name carries a role. §11's "a round's merged findings" is prose and §9.1's table lets cr record create records outright, so the check cannot live only in merge.
- That closes the bypass exactly as §6.4.4's waiver drops and §9.3.6's posted-index drops are re-applied at record time: feeding a single role's fan-out file straight to cr record is checked as cr merge would have checked it. §6.5.1's merged output holds several roles and its name carries none, and those role fields were bound by cr merge at the file each record arrived in, which the doc comment states rather than leaving implied.
- state.DecodeStamped now takes a per-line check, so the line counting keeps one home: §4.1.6, §4.5.6 and §6.1.3 each refuse an agent's line for reasons of their own and each has to name the line it refused, and a second pass over the body could not agree with the first about a blank line. A command with nothing to add passes nil.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... && golangci-lint run && ./scripts/deadcode.sh. Mutation testing with gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal moved from the recorded baseline of Killed 238, Lived 3, 98.76 per cent to Killed 248, Lived 3, 98.80 per cent, with no new survivor. The three are the documented internal/config words pair and finding/id.go's equivalent NextID boundary, all commented at their sites, plus the one known TIMED OUT mutant at state/layout.go. Every mutant raised in fanout.go and validate.go was killed and neither file left a line uncovered.
Out of scope: neither cr merge nor cr record exists yet, so nothing asserts this end to end today. merge-command must assert that cr merge exits 1 naming the line and the field and refuses an input it cannot attribute to a role. cr record has no task that builds the command itself, and record-reapplies-drops is the nearest home for the end-to-end assertion. unit-containment-predicate owns the other half of the unit question, that the anchor lies inside the unit the record names. anchor-side-semantics owns resolving RIGHT against the head and LEFT against the merge base. finding-computed-field-rejection owns §6.1.4, and grade computation, the content_hash pre-image, dedup, merge counts and the posted-index drops are each their own task.

tasks.title: Reject agent-written computed fields
tasks.acceptance:
- The agent never writes grade, state, disposition, thread_id, span_hash, issue_hash, a citation's content_hash or origin, or any other field marked computed. A record arriving with one is rejected with exit code 1, per §6.1.4.
- duplicate_of is exempt only on cr merge output per §6.5.1.
- A test supplies each computed field in turn and asserts rejection, then asserts duplicate_of passes on merge output and is rejected on direct record input.
tasks.closed_reason:
- No field §6.1.4 forbids may arrive from the agent: internal/finding/fields.go holds the fence as data derived from §6.1's Required column, plus the three rows §6.1.4 names that the column calls optional (disposition, duplicate_of, thread_id) and §3.3's span_hash and issue_hash, which §6.1.4 names in the same sentence and no finding can legitimately hold, while citationFields' computed rows carry the citation's content_hash and origin. suppressed_by is deliberately outside the fence, because §3.5.4 has the agent decide it.
- A record arriving with one is rejected with exit code 1 naming the line and the field: checker.computed in internal/finding/validate.go walks the fence ahead of §6.1.3's required walk, so the whole of §6.1.4 answers alike with state.DecodeStamped's head and round half, and reports through the state.ReservedFieldError internal/cli/exit.go already maps onto ExitValidation, while checker.computedCitations holds each citations entry to the same rule and names the offending entry by its index. Presence alone is the fault, as it is for head and round.
- duplicate_of is exempt on cr merge output alone: the exemption rides on an explicit finding.Source argument to Decode rather than on the entry point or the file name, because cr record has one door that §6.5.1 sends merge output through and an agent's own record file through alike, and a file name is the agent's claim about its own input. SourceAgent is the zero value so a caller that never considered the question gets the closed answer, and DecodePerRole passes SourceAgent because §6.5.1 exempts what cr merge writes and never what it reads.
- TestARecordArrivingWithAComputedFieldIsRejected pins the fence's exact contents and supplies each of its eight fields in turn, as a value and as null, then supplies each computed citation field and asserts the index-named rejection, and TestDuplicateOfIsExemptOnlyOnMergeOutput reads one record four ways: accepted under SourceMerge, refused under SourceAgent whether the file is named merged.ndjson or a role's fan-out file, refused as cr merge input, and grade still refused on merge output. Gate green, and gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 253, Lived 4, efficacy 98.44%, the one new survivor being the capacity-hint arithmetic in reservedFields, commented at the site as equivalent.

Out of scope: grade computation (§6.2), the content_hash pre-image (§9.2.3), the anchor's own schema rules, dedup (§6.4), and cr merge's and cr record's command bodies are each their own later task and none is touched here.

tasks.title: Define the citation content hash preimage
tasks.acceptance:
- Round 8 finding undefined-hash-preimage: citations[].content_hash is the normalised hash per §1.4 of the single line at path:line, matching §9.2's rule for a one-line anchor. It was the one hash in the document with no stated pre-image, so two implementations would produce values that cannot be compared — exactly the comparability §6.2.3 says a v0.2 drift check depends on.
- cr computes and stores it at record time; the agent never supplies it.
- A test fixes the hash for a known cited line and asserts it changes when that line changes.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Round 8's finding undefined-hash-preimage is answered in internal/finding/citation.go: (*Citation).StampContentHash computes a citation's content_hash as AnchorContentHash over a slice of one line, which is §9.2's rule per §1.4 applied to the single line the citation names, reached by reference exactly as §6.2.3 reaches it (recorded per §9.2.3).
- The pre-image is named once rather than twice: the value is the anchor function's own, so a citation's hash and a one-line anchor's over the same text are one value by construction and cannot drift apart.
- That comparability is what §6.2.3 says a v0.2 drift check depends on, and TestACitationHashesItsLineAsAOneLineAnchor holds it two ways: the stored hash equals AnchorContentHash over the same line across seven shapes two rules would disagree about (indentation, trailing whitespace, whitespace §1.4 leaves alone, the empty line, a whitespace-only line), and the source fence asserts StampContentHash's body calls AnchorContentHash and nothing else, so a second rule cannot be added without the test failing.
- cr computes the hash and stores it at record time: stamping is a method on the citation and the only exported way the field is filled, and the field is left untouched when §1.4 step 1 refuses the line, so an undecodable line has no hash rather than the hash of nothing.
- The agent never supplies it: §6.1's table already marks citations[].content_hash Computed and checker.computedCitations rejects a record arriving with one through every door, which TestSuppliedComputedFieldsAreRejected covers; nothing was rebuilt there.
- TestTheStoredCitationHashIsFixedAndFollowsTheLine fixes the value for a known cited line: the tab-indented, double-spaced, trailing-space line normalises to ' if ($total > 0) {' and pins 0d6c58b99de69ac1 as a literal, and asserts it is not 65abc82d59be1121, the equally well-formed value a stamp that skipped Normalise would store.
- The same test asserts the hash changes when the line changes (> becomes >=) and does not change when only the line's whitespace changes, which is the half a raw-bytes hash would break while passing every shape assertion.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... && golangci-lint run && ./scripts/deadcode.sh. Mutation testing: Killed 559 (+1), Lived 13, Not covered 39, Timed out 6, efficacy 97.73% — no new survivor.

tasks.title: Compute the grade from evidence
tasks.acceptance:
- The three grades of the §6.2 table: probed references a probe whose head matches and whose result supports the claim per §5.3 and §5.4; cited carries at least one citations entry that cr resolved against the current head, and that entry either has origin: rule or lies outside the record's own unit; argued is neither.
- The grade is computed by cr from the record, never asserted by the agent, per §6.2.1. The only inputs are citations and the referenced probe record, whose result and supporting conditions are fixed by §5.3 and §5.4; evidence prose is never parsed.
- A test asserts a record whose evidence prose claims proof but whose citations are empty grades argued.
- §6.2.1's inputs are axis, unit, anchor, claim, citations, the mapping of §4.1.6, and the referenced probe record; evidence prose is never parsed.
- Round 13 finding mutable-grading-input, assigned here: the mapping is the first grading input that is mutable within a round (§4.1.6 replaces it, §3.3.1 clears it) while §6.3.1 recomputes the grade three times and §7.2 accepts question→finding on a recomputed probed. A recomputation MUST NOT raise a record's grade within a round; it may only lower it or leave it unchanged.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/finding/grade.go's ComputeGrade is §6.2's table: the probed row is probe.Establishes over the referenced record, the cited row asks for one citations entry cr resolved that either carries origin rule or lies outside the record's own unit, and argued is neither of those.
- internal/probe/grading.go routes each kind to its own ladder; Proven is §5.3.5's result condition read off the stored mutation record as Reproduces reads §5.4.4's off a gap record, since no Outcome survives into probes.ndjson and §6.2.1 names the record as grading's input.
- The grade is computed by cr and never asserted by the agent: §6.1.4 already refuses a record arriving with the field, Regrade is the only writer of it, and finding.Resolved takes a probe.Baseline and a probe.ClaimMapping that no caller can manufacture.
- finding.Evidence holds exactly two unexported fields, the unit boundary and the probe answer, so there is nowhere to put a summary, a severity, a role or an evidence sentence; TestGradingHasNowhereToPutAFieldSection621DoesNotName asserts that field set by reflection.
- TestARecordWhoseProseClaimsProofButCitesNothingIsArgued records a fixture whose evidence says proven, confirmed and verified in one sentence and whose citations are empty, and asserts it grades argued.
- TestTwoRecordsAgreeingOnSection621sInputsGradeAlike varies summary, evidence, severity and role between two records that agree on §6.2.1's inputs and asserts one grade.
- Round 13's mutable-grading-input is a ratchet in Regrade: notAbove compares ranks in the gradeStrength order §6.4.2 already reads, so a recomputation lowers a grade or leaves it unchanged and never raises one within a round.
- TestARecomputationLowersAGradeAndNeverRaisesIt covers all three directions and TestTheRatchetHoldsOverEveryPairOfGrades covers every pair, including the cited rung a two-value fixture cannot reach.
- §6.2.1's containment is unit.Unit.Contains, evaluated entirely in head coordinates against the hunk ranges §3.4.6 records from git.Hunk.HeadRange, so a hunk that adds no lines is already its head-side insertion point and no side is compared; TestContainmentIsDecidedInHeadCoordinates covers inside, outside and that insertion point.
- cr record is wired end to end: §6.2.3 resolves and stamps every citation against the round's head before anything is written, the three stored inputs of §6.2.1 are read once and shared with §5.4's severity bounds so the two answers cannot drift, and gradeRecords stamps the grade last.
- TestRecordComputesAndStampsTheGradeSection62Names drives three records differing only in their citations through the built command against a real checkout and reads cited, argued and argued back off findings.ndjson.
- state.RecordLines was added beside DecodeStamped so §6.2.3's post-decode rejection names the line the user must open, counted by the one function that decides which lines carry records.

tasks.title: Decide containment in head coordinates
tasks.acceptance:
- Containment is evaluated entirely in head coordinates: a path:line is inside a unit when path is one of that unit's file paths and line falls within the head-side range of one of its hunks — for a hunk that adds no lines, its head-side insertion point, per §6.2.1.
- No side is compared, and no field the agent writes can move a location across the boundary.
- A test covers a citation inside a unit, one outside, and one at a delete-only hunk's insertion point.
- Round 13 finding agent-chosen-grading-boundary (critical), assigned here: rejecting a unit that is not a unit of the current round proves the unit exists, not that it is the record's own. Nothing in the spec binds anchor to unit, so a record anchored in u1 may declare unit: u2 and cite into its own hunk, and the citation counts as outside the record's own unit and buys cited. The implementation rejects a record whose anchor does not fall inside the unit it names, which is what makes §6.2.1's sentence 'no field the agent writes can move a location across the boundary' true.

tasks.title: Validate a probed record against target
tasks.acceptance:
- A record claiming probed without a valid same-head probe that supports it is rejected with exit code 1, per §6.2.2.
- A probe supports a record only when its target falls within that record's anchor.start_line..anchor.line range on the same path, so one experiment cannot grade a second finding elsewhere in the unit.
- A probe target is always RIGHT, so a record with a LEFT anchor can never reach probed; a claim about deleted code is argued or cited, never probed.
- A test asserts a target one line outside the anchor range fails to support, and that a LEFT-anchored record cannot reach probed.

tasks.title: Resolve citations against the current head
tasks.acceptance:
- cr resolves every entry in citations against the current head, and rejects with exit code 1 an entry whose path does not exist or whose line is out of range, per §6.2.3.
- cr computes and stores content_hash itself at record time, so that hash cannot fail then; it is recorded per §9.2.3 so a v0.2 migration can detect drift, and it does no validating work in v0.1.
- A test covers a missing path and an out-of-range line.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/finding/citation.go's ResolveCitations walks every entry of a record's citations and resolves each against the current head through a HeadFile reader, so no entry is passed over.
- An entry whose path the head does not hold, and an entry whose line falls below 1 or past the file's last line, are both rejected with a RejectedRecordError naming the entry by index and field, which internal/cli/exit.go maps onto ExitValidation, §11.2's exit code 1.
- internal/git/file.go's FileAtRevision is the head-side reader: it asks git ls-tree whether the revision holds the path as a blob and reads that blob with git cat-file, both through internal/git's pinned runner, so the read is of the head commit and never of the worktree and §2.1.1 holds on a dirty checkout.
- cr computes and stores content_hash itself, by calling the existing (*Citation).StampContentHash on the line it has just read from the head, so the agent supplies none and the hash cannot fail at record time.
- The value is §9.2's rule over a range of one line, recorded per §9.2.3 so a v0.2 migration can detect drift; nothing in v0.1 reads it back and ResolveCitations compares it against nothing, so the field does no validating work.
- TestACitationTheHeadCannotOpenIsRejected covers a missing path, a directory, a line past the end of the file, and line 0, and TestEveryCitationIsResolvedAndStampedFromTheHead covers the accepted boundaries and the stamping.
- internal/cli/norepowrite_test.go's gitReads allowlist gains ls-tree and cat-file, both reads with no writing mode, so §2.2's fence over the repository under review still holds.

tasks.title: Never describe a cited record verified
tasks.acceptance:
- Record-time validation establishes that a citation exists, never that it supports the summary. cr never describes a cited record as verified, confirmed, or proven in any output; cited means only that a human-checkable location was supplied, per §6.2.4.
- A test greps every rendered string for the three forbidden words applied to a cited record.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Record-time validation establishes only that a citation exists: finding.ResolveCitations opens the path at the head, refuses an entry the head cannot open, stamps the hash of the line, and compares that hash against nothing, so nothing in the path from a citation to a grade asks whether the location supports the summary.
- cr describes a cited record as verified, confirmed or proven nowhere in its output, and TestNoStringLiteralCrShipsCallsARecordVerified holds it there: it parses every production Go file in the module and refuses any string literal carrying one of §6.2.4's three words as a whole word.
- The surface is cr's own words rather than the repository's prose; comments are outside it, since the guard's own documentation and internal/cli/record.go's supported map both name the words in order to forbid them, and a guard those tripped would be one somebody turns off.
- Matching is whole-word, so §7.4.8's provenance and §3.6.6's unverified hearsay are not convicted, and the guard asserts that of its own matcher before trusting it over the module.
- TestNoRenderingOfACitedRecordCallsItVerified reads the finished text instead of the literals: it records a finding that actually grades cited, asserts the grade, and then greps the json payload, the terminal line and §8.1.4's built-in question label for a cited question in every language for the three words.
- The agent's own evidence sentence is removed from what that test examines and the fixture writes all three words into it deliberately, because §8.1.7 renders evidence verbatim and §6.2.4 binds what cr says rather than what cr quotes.
- The fence was checked against a planted literal in a production file, which it reported by file and by word before the literal was removed; cited therefore means in cr's output only that a human-checkable location was supplied.

tasks.title: Stamp citation origin by positional match
tasks.acceptance:
- origin is computed, never supplied. A record arriving with any origin value is rejected with exit code 1, per §6.2.5.
- At record time cr stamps each citation by matching it positionally against its own detection output: a citation gets origin: rule when rule-stats.ndjson holds a hit for the same head with the same rule id and the same path and line per §2.6.1.6; every other citation gets origin: agent.
- Matching on rule id alone would let a record name any rule and point anywhere inside its own unit, which is exactly the forgery the deleted rule grade branch allowed.
- A test asserts a citation naming a real rule id at a line that rule never hit gets origin: agent.

tasks.title: Render every citation into the block
tasks.acceptance:
- cr cannot judge whether a citation supports the summary, and does not claim to. Every citation of a cited record is rendered verbatim into the draft block, so the human makes the judgement cr cannot, per §6.2.6.
- A test asserts each stored citation appears in draft.md as path:line.

tasks.title: Force argued records to question kind
tasks.acceptance:
- Invariant 4: a record with grade argued is forced to kind: question, per §6.3.1.
- The forcing is applied at record time, again at draft time, and again at post time immediately before the payload is built.
- A test flips a record to kind: finding at each of the three moments and asserts the forcing re-applies.
tasks.closed_reason:
- finding.ForceQuestion is invariant 4 and §6.3.1: a record whose grade is argued has its kind set to question, in cr rather than in a role's prompt, so no wording reaches it; §2.7's settings table holds no key for the forcing and TestNoFlagOnRecordTurnsTheForcingOff runs the command again under every global flag §11.1 gives it.
- The forcing is one idempotent function that reports what it moved, so §6.3.1's three moments each apply the same rule and none of them has to know what the moment before it did; cr record applies the first of the three, immediately after the grade it reads is computed.
- TestTheForcingReAppliesAtEachOfSection631sThreeMoments flips the record back to kind finding before record time, before draft time and before post time, and asserts the forcing re-applies at each of the three.
- The repetition is load-bearing rather than defensive, and TestAGradeTheRatchetLoweredIsForcedAtTheNextMoment shows why: a record recorded as a probed finding whose probe stops standing behind it is lowered to argued by the ratchet, and the next moment is what takes it out of the assertion register.
- TestRecordForcesAnArguedRecordToAQuestion drives an argued record and a cited one through the built command and reads back a question and a finding from findings.ndjson, so the forcing is asserted on what §9.1 keeps for the rest of the round rather than on what the command printed.
- Nothing here raises a register: TestTheForcingLeavesEveryGradeButArguedAlone covers probed and cited against both kinds and asserts the agent's own choice stands, since §6.2 lets those two assert and does not require them to.
- Draft time and post time are the remaining two moments of §6.3.1 and are undone here because cr draft and cr post are not yet built; both call this same function, and the task that builds each is where it lands.

tasks.title: Count forcings in the round summary
tasks.acceptance:
- The forcing is visible in the round summary, with a count per class, per §6.3.2.
- The count is an honesty disclosure and survives --quiet per §11.1.
tasks.closed_reason:

TestTheForcingCountIsPrintedAtZero holds it printed when nothing was forced, and TestTheForcingCountDoesNotFadeOnASecondRun holds it counting the grade section 6.3 forces rather than the moves one run made, which is what keeps it non-zero at the two moments a human reads it.

tasks.title: Reject any override of argued forcing
tasks.acceptance:
- There is no flag, configuration setting, environment variable, profile field, or role instruction that disables or overrides the forcing, per §6.3.3.
- cr rejects any attempt to post a record graded argued with kind: finding, with exit code 1, naming the record id.
- The forcing happens in cr, not in the prompt, so no agent can talk its way past it.
- A test attempts the override through each of the five channels and asserts all five fail.

- TestNoChannelOverridesTheArguedForcing attempts the override through each of the five channels and all five fail: a flag walk over the tree plus cr record and cr draft run under every global flag, a repository config.json carrying argued.forcing refused with exit code 3, two CR_ variables refused by name, a profile file carrying an argued field and a force_findings field ignored, and a repository role whose instructions demand assertions leaving the record a question in the rendered block.

tasks.title: Deduplicate findings by anchor with class
tasks.acceptance:
- Findings are deduplicated by (anchor.path, anchor.line, class), per §6.4.1.
- Round 8 findings dedup-key-omits-side and side-omitted-from-identity-keys: anchor.side joins the key. §9.2 makes side part of an anchor and §6.1.2 resolves the two sides against different trees, so without it a record about a removed line at merge-base line 40 and one about an added line at head line 40 in the same file with the same class collapse into one group, and §6.4.3 retires one with no observable reason.
- A test builds exactly that colliding pair and asserts two groups, not one.
- Round 12 findings dedup-key-drops-side and dedup-key-omits-side, re-reported: without anchor.side a LEFT deletion record and a RIGHT addition record at the same file and line collide and one is silently retired in state duplicate.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/finding/dedup.go holds §6.4.1's key as one type and one constructor: DedupKey carries Path, Side, Line and Class, DedupKeyOf is the only place a record's key is read, and Groups partitions a slice of records by it in first-appearance order so one input is one partition however the map underneath iterates.
- anchor.side joins the three fields §6.4.1 names, per round 8's dedup-key-omits-side and side-omitted-from-identity-keys and round 12's dedup-key-drops-side; §9.2 makes the side part of an anchor and §6.1.2 resolves RIGHT against the head and LEFT against the merge base, so one line number names a line in each of two file versions.
- TestTwoSidesOfOneLineNumberAreTwoDedupGroups builds exactly the colliding pair the finding names, a removed line anchored LEFT at merge-base line 40 and an added line anchored RIGHT at head line 40 of one file in one class, and asserts two groups rather than one; without the side §6.4.3 would retire one of them naming a representative about different code.
- TestADedupKeyIsTheAnchoredLineAndTheClassAndNothingElse holds the key honest from the other side by reading §6.1's table off the record type through fieldsInCommon, so the two grouping records must differ in every field outside the key and a field added to the table later without being varied fails the test rather than joining the key's blind spot.
- The quality gate is green: go test -race ./..., golangci-lint run, and scripts/deadcode.sh all pass.

tasks.title: Pick the duplicate group representative
tasks.acceptance:
- Within a duplicate group the representative is the highest grade, then the highest severity, then the earliest role in corpus order per §2.5.5, per §6.4.2.
- A test fixes the winner for a group tied on grade and severity and differing only in corpus order.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/finding/dedup.go's Group.RepresentativeAt applies §6.4.2's three keys in the section's own order, comparing the grade first through gradeStrength, then the severity through severityStrength, then the role ids through the comparison role.Order returns for §2.5.5's corpus order. It answers with the position in the group rather than with the record, because §6.4.3 needs everything that is not the representative and because a function of this package handing back a *Finding is what the unanchored-item guard reads as a new decode door.
- The corpus order arrives as role.Order's comparison rather than being rebuilt, so §2.5.5 keeps its single definition; internal/role's own guard already stops any other package from naming the resolution layer, which is the half of that order nobody outside it can spell.
- TestTheEarliestRoleInCorpusOrderRepresentsAGroupTiedOnGradeAndSeverity fixes the winner for a group tied on grade and on severity and differing only in corpus order, resolving a real two-layer corpus in which zebra-eyes is per-repository and alpha-lens is global, so the loser both sorts first alphabetically and arrives first and neither ascending id nor arrival order can produce the expected answer.
- TestARepresentativeIsTheHighestGradeBeforeTheHighestSeverity walks every rung of both ladders and gives the record that must win the weaker value of every other key, so a comparison that read the keys in another order picks the other record on every rung.
- TestAnUnrankableSeverityOrGradeNeverRepresentsAGroup drives a grade and a severity cr does not recognise through the picker, since §6.1.3 checks that those fields are present and not that their values are known.
- The quality gate is green: go test -race ./..., golangci-lint run, and scripts/deadcode.sh all pass, and gofmt reports nothing under internal.

tasks.title: Retain duplicates with an overlap summary
tasks.acceptance:
- Suppressed duplicates are retained in state duplicate with duplicate_of naming the representative, and the contributing roles are reported as an overlap summary, per §6.4.3.
- The duplicate count is an honesty disclosure per §10.1.6 and survives --quiet.
- A test asserts the suppressed record survives in state with its duplicate_of set.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/finding/overlap.go's MarkDuplicates applies §6.4.3 over one round's records: it groups them per §6.4.1, picks each group's representative per §6.4.2, and writes that representative's id into every other record's duplicate_of, editing in place and reordering nothing.
- It writes duplicate_of and no other computed field, because §6.5.1 makes duplicate_of the one cr merge may put in its output and leaves state to cr record.
- internal/cli/record.go's stampStates walks §9.1's first two rows so a record arriving with duplicate_of is created in draft and then moved to duplicate, asking finding.MayTransition for both moves rather than assuming either; §6.5.1 assigns that second move to cr record.
- Overlap carries the §6.4.1 key the group formed around, the representative's id, the contributing role ids with each role named once in arrival order, and how many records were retired, which is §6.4.3's overlap summary.
- Overlaps implements cap.go's HonestyDisclosure with §10.1.6's duplicate count, so the count reaches the reader through the channel §11.1 exempts from quiet rather than through an ordinary informational line, and it is rendered at zero as well as above it.
- TestASuppressedDuplicateIsStoredInThatStateNamingItsRepresentative records a merged file through the command and reads findings.ndjson back, asserting the suppressed record is still there in state duplicate with its duplicate_of naming the representative.
- TestEveryRecordButTheRepresentativeIsMarkedADuplicateOfIt and its three siblings cover the marking, the role list, a group of one that is neither marked nor reported, the two sides of one line number suppressing neither record, and the disclosure text.
- The quality gate is green: go test -race ./..., golangci-lint run, and scripts/deadcode.sh all pass, and gofmt reports nothing under internal.

tasks.title: Drop waived findings before any record
tasks.acceptance:
- Findings matching an active waiver are dropped and counted per §7.4, per §6.4.4.
- A dropped finding is never written to findings.ndjson at all, so no record ever exists in a state §9.1 does not define; only the count reaches the round summary.
- A test asserts findings.ndjson holds no trace of a waived finding while the summary count moves.

tasks.title: Merge per-role finding files
tasks.acceptance:
- cr merge <files...> -o <out> --repo <owner/repo> --pr <number> merges per-role NDJSON files and applies §6.4.1, §6.4.2, §6.4.4 and §9.3.6, per §6.5.1.
- It computes grade in memory for those counts only. Its output carries no computed field except duplicate_of, which marks a suppressed duplicate; cr record applies §6.4.3 from it and stamps state.
- The repository is required because §6.4.2 needs its resolved role corpus and §6.4.4 needs its repository-wide waivers; the pull request is required because §7.4.1 also scopes not-here waivers to it, and a merge that could not read them would resurface exactly what the reviewer set aside.
- Missing required fields fail with exit code 1 and name the offending line, per §6.5.2.
- Found by command-surface-stubs: state.Stamp carries head and round without omitempty, deliberately, because 2.3.3 requires them on a stored record. Marshalling a decoded Finding therefore emits a line that cr record refuses, since DecodeStamped rejects those keys by presence. cr merge must strip the pair before it writes, and a test must drive its output back through cr record rather than asserting on the file alone.

tasks.title: Report merge counts by four dimensions
tasks.acceptance:
- cr merge reports counts by role, axis, severity, and grade, per §6.5.1.
- It writes its drop counts into the current round's summary.json per §10.3.
- A test asserts all four breakdowns appear and that the drop counts reach summary.json.

tasks.title: Re-apply suppression drops at record time
tasks.acceptance:
- Round 8 finding merge-only-drops-are-bypassable: cr record re-applies the §6.4.4 waiver drops and the §9.3.6 posted-index drops idempotently before writing anything to findings.ndjson. Nothing requires cr record's input to be cr merge's output — §11 lists cr record <pr> <file> with no precondition, §6.1.3 has both performing the same validation, and the single-role case makes skipping merge the obvious thing to do — so a pipeline that skips merge would re-raise a finding already posted in an earlier round.
- The invariant enforced is that a posted finding never reaches a second draft, not that a particular command ran.
- A test feeds a raw single-role file straight to cr record and asserts the waived and already-posted findings are still dropped.

tasks.title: Post only comments anchored to lines
tasks.acceptance:
- Every posted comment is anchored to a line of the diff. v0.1 has no unanchored comment channel: an item with no code location is reported through cr status and never posted, per §1.6.1.
- A review comment spends the reviewer's standing with the author, so volume is a cost in itself, independent of correctness.
- A test asserts an unanchored item cannot reach the payload by any path.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Every posted comment is anchored to a line of the diff, because the fence sits on the way in rather than at the payload: internal/finding's Decode refuses a record whose anchor names no path, so an item with no code location never becomes a record (§6.1.2, §4.1.3) and nothing unanchored exists downstream for a draft or a payload to render. No second enforcement point was added, since §1.6.1 needs one fence with no bypass rather than two checks a future author must remember.
- v0.1 has no unanchored comment channel, and today that is held as a negative: a comment is rendered from a record, a record is what the finding package's decoders hand back, and every one of them refuses an item with no code location, so there is no channel to widen. Reporting such an item through cr status is the positive half and belongs to intent-gap-entries and status-coverage-report, both open, and the end-to-end negative against a posted payload belongs to single-review-batching and pre-validate-positions, which build the payload.
- §1.6's economic claim now lives in the code it governs, as a paragraph on internal/finding.Anchor, the type that owns the fence: a review comment spends the reviewer's standing with the author, so volume is a cost in itself, independent of correctness, and an unanchored comment costs the most for the least, because the author has to work out what it is about before judging whether it is right. That is why v0.1 has one comment channel and this field is it.
- TestNoUnanchoredItemBecomesARecordByAnyDoor in internal/finding/anchored_test.go asserts an unanchored item cannot reach a record by any path. It reads the door set out of the package's own source with go/ast, taking every exported function whose results carry a Finding, requires that set to match the doors it drives, and feeds each of them, Decode as SourceAgent, Decode as SourceMerge, and DecodePerRole, four shapes of an item with no code location: no anchor key, an empty anchor, an anchor naming no path, and an anchor naming the empty path, asserting a RejectedRecordError naming anchor each time while the same fixture passes once anchored. The guard was verified by temporarily adding an exported Loophole returning []*Finding, which failed the set assertion, and by temporarily deleting the anchor branch from checker.check, which failed eight assertions, both reverted. gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 254, Lived 4, efficacy 98.45 percent, the documented baseline unchanged, as a doc comment and a test add no production branch.

tasks.title: Block posting above the comment cap
tasks.acceptance:
- post.max_comments (default 20) caps the comments in one round. When the cap is exceeded cr blocks posting with exit code 1 and names the count, so the user triages further, per §1.6.2.
- cr never silently drops comments to fit.
- The cap report is an honesty disclosure and survives --quiet per §11.1.
- A test queues twenty-one comments and asserts exit 1 with the count named and nothing posted.
tasks.closed_reason:
- post.max_comments caps the comments of one round in internal/finding/cap.go, where CommentCapFor measures the round's queued records against the resolved setting and the built-in default of 20 comes from internal/config's §2.7 table rather than a second path to the value, which the cli test reads out of config.Resolve before it queues anything.
- Above the cap CommentCap.Err returns a *CommentCapExceededError naming the count, the cap, and the overflow, and internal/cli/exit.go maps it onto ExitValidation, so posting is blocked with exit code 1 and the message tells the user how many comments to triage away.
- cr never silently drops comments to fit, and the refusal is structural rather than remembered: the cap call hands back a two-int decision and no shape in the package can carry a subset of the queue, which TestNothingCarriesAFittedQueueBackFromTheCap holds open by reading the package's own source and failing any function whose signature names CommentCap and hands back a Finding — verified against a deliberately added FitToCap helper before it was deleted again.
- The cap report is CommentCap.Disclosure, made whether or not the cap was exceeded and taking no flag at all, so no caller has an answer to give --quiet, and cap.go declares the HonestyDisclosure interface as the shape §11.1's later shared writer consumes rather than building that writer here. TestTheCapReportIsAnHonestyDisclosureOnEitherPath pins the text under the cap, at it, and over it, and pins that the block carries the disclosure whole.
- TestQueueingPastTheCommentCapExitsWithTheValidationCode queues twenty-one comments against the default cap of 20 and asserts exit code 1 wrapped and unwrapped with the count 21 and the cap named in the message, while TestTheCapBlocksOnlyTheCountAboveIt covers nineteen, twenty and twenty-one. Gremlins killed all six cap.go mutants including both the boundary and the negation at the comparison, at Killed 260 and Lived 4, the four known baseline survivors with no new one.
Out of scope: nothing posted cannot be driven end to end because cr post does not exist, so single-review-batching, dry-run-posting and confirm-flag-required must make that assertion. The draft header that renders the count is draft-summary-header, the round summary count is round-summary-writers, and §1.6.3's non-destructive triage is triage-to-fit-non-destructive.

tasks.title: Keep volume triage scoped per request
tasks.acceptance:
- Triaging to fit under the cap is not destructive. A discard dispositioned not-here is scoped to the pull request per §7.4.1, so setting a true finding aside for volume reasons never silences it repository-wide, per §1.6.3.
- A test discards a finding for volume on PR 1 and asserts it still raises on PR 2 in the same repository.

tasks.title: Key waivers by anchor with class
tasks.acceptance:
- A waiver is keyed by (anchor.path, class, normalised hash of the anchored lines), matching the class-based identity of §6.4.1 so a waived finding cannot return under a different producer, per §7.4.1.
- The summary is deliberately excluded from the key: it is agent-composed prose that differs between rounds, and including it would let a waived finding resurface under a reworded summary.
- Round 8 finding side-omitted-from-identity-keys: anchor.side joins the waiver key and the §9.3.6 posted-index key, keeping them aligned with §9.2's definition of anchor identity and with the §6.4.1 dedup key.
- The key is narrow on purpose: it suppresses the same class at the same unchanged code in the same file, and stops suppressing once that code changes — which is exactly when the judgement behind the waiver should be revisited, per §7.4.2.
- A test asserts a waiver stops matching once the anchored lines change.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/finding/waiver.go's WaiverKey is §7.4.1's key over (anchor.path, anchor.side, class, anchor.content_hash), and WaiverKeyOf is its only construction, so §7.4's waiver, §9.3.6's posted index and §6.4.4's merge-time lookup read one set of four fields off the record rather than three spellings of it.
- TestAWaiverKeyIsTheAnchoredCodeAndTheClassAndNothingElse keys two records identically that share nothing but the anchored code and the class, and reads §6.1's table off the record type to require every other field to differ, so the summary exclusion bites as a collision rather than as a comment and a field added later without being varied fails the test.
- anchor.side is the fourth field, per round 8's side-omitted-from-identity-keys, and TestAWaiverReachesOneClassInOneFileInOneTree holds the content hash fixed while varying the side, so a waiver over a line removed from the merge base cannot silence a finding about the identical line added to the head.
- The key carries the anchored code where §6.4.1's dedup key carries the line, so it suppresses one class at one unchanged range in one file and stops at the edit, and the type is comparable with no looser comparison after round 8 dropped §7.4.6's path-prefix widening.
- TestAWaiverStopsMatchingOnceTheAnchoredLinesChange asserts both directions, that the same code moved down the file and re-indented still matches, and that an edited condition does not.

tasks.title: Scope waivers by their disposition
tasks.acceptance:
- A waiver's scope follows its disposition: one written for wrong is scoped to the repository, one written for not-here is scoped to the pull request, per §7.4.1.
- The two scopes follow the two meanings: this is wrong is a fact about the class and generalises across the repository; not worth saying here is a fact about this pull request and never silences the finding anywhere else, per §7.4.3.
- A waiver records its disposition per §7.2, so §7.3 can tell a false positive from a deliberate silence, per §7.4.5.
- Round 8 finding capability-without-mechanism, resolved by approved decision: §7.4.6's path-prefix widening is dropped from v0.1. No command wrote one, §7.4.1 fixed the key shape, and the legacy-area case it existed for is already covered by a rule's exempt field per §2.6.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/finding/waiver.go's Waiver.Scope is the one binding between §7.2's dispositions and §7.4.1's two scopes: DispositionWrong returns ScopeRepository and DispositionNotHere returns ScopePullRequest, and TestAWaiverScopeFollowsItsDisposition asserts both directions over one record that differs in the disposition alone.
- ScopeRepository names ~/.cr/waivers/<owner>/<repo>.ndjson, the file a wrong disposition writes, so the fact about the class generalises across the repository, and the same test asserts its name because §7.4.7 prints it and §7.4.4 selects a file by it.
- ScopePullRequest never becomes the repository scope: WaiverScope is a struct around an unexported name so nothing outside waiver.go can compose one, and Waiver carries no scope field that could contradict its disposition, both asserted by reflection in TestNotWorthSayingHereSilencesNothingBeyondItsPullRequest, and WaiverFor refuses a record carrying neither of §7.2's two values rather than defaulting to the wider file, which TestARecordIsNotWaivedWithoutOneOfTheTwoDispositions covers for the empty and the unrecognised value.
- Waiver.Disposition is recorded per §7.4.5 and survives the JSON round trip that §7.4.4's files and §7.4.7's listing depend on, asserted by TestAWaiverRecordsTheDispositionItWasWrittenFor for wrong and for not-here.
- §7.4.6 in spec/0.1.0.md carries no path-prefix widening and none was built: matching stays == over the four fields of the key, and TestAWaiverNeverWidensAlongThePath asserts a waiver over app/Models/Order.php matches none of six prefix- or extension-shaped paths while still matching its own path.
- Nothing added here can write a widened waiver because no command writes a waiver file yet, §7.4.1's key shape is unchanged from waiver-key, and the legacy-area case the widening existed for stays with a rule's exempt field per §2.6, which the widening test's comment records as the decision it stands in for.

tasks.title: Write waivers to the two files
tasks.acceptance:
- The two scopes live in two files: a repository-wide waiver is written to ~/.cr/waivers/<owner>/<repo>.ndjson; a pull-request-scoped one is written to that PR's waivers.ndjson per §2.3, per §7.4.4.
- Both are readable and removable, so neither disposition is a one-way door.
- A waiver records the round, the PR, the head, and the reason when one was given, per §7.4.8.
- Waived findings are dropped before drafting and counted in the round summary, per §7.4.6.
- §7.4 holds eight items after the approved removal of path-prefix widening; waived findings are dropped before drafting per §7.4.6 and provenance is recorded per §7.4.8.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/finding/waiverstore.go's Waive derives the scope with Waiver.Scope() and never takes one from a caller, and appendWaiver is the single switch over it: ScopeRepository writes ~/.cr/waivers/<owner>/<repo>.ndjson through state.LockRepoWaivers, ScopePullRequest writes that PR's waivers.ndjson through state.LockPR and state.WriteRecords(state.FileWaivers), and a scope naming neither file is refused rather than falling into the last arm.
- TestTheTwoScopesOfSection744LandInTheTwoFilesItNames waives two records that share one §7.4.1 key and differ only in disposition, then reads both §7.4.4 paths straight off disk: the wrong record is the only line in the repository file, the not-here record the only line in the pull request's, and neither file holds the other's — §7.4.3's silence-outside-the-PR failure asserted from both sides.
- RepositoryWaivers, PullRequestWaivers and ActiveWaivers read both files lock-free per §2.3.2, and RemoveWaiver deletes from the file the id names — wr<n> for the repository-wide store, wp<n> for a pull request's — so a waiver is readable and removable in both scopes.
- RemoveWaiver deletes the line rather than marking it: §7.4.1 matches a waiver by key and never by id, so unlike §3.6.6's note nothing cites one and a reissued number strands no record, while a tombstone in a suppression file is one forgotten filter away from a silence nobody ever observes.
- TestAWaiverIsReadableAndRemovableFromEitherScope reads all three readers, removes from each scope with the other file asserted untouched, and covers the refusals: an unknown id, an id under neither prefix, a wp id with no --pr, and pull request 1 as the boundary beside that refusal.
- WaiverProvenance carries §7.4.8's four fields — round, pr, head, and reason with omitempty — as its own fields rather than embedding state.Stamp, because §9.3.5 exempts waivers from the round scoping every reader of that pair applies and neither waiver file is one of §2.3.3's eight.
- TestAWaiverRecordsTheRoundThePullRequestTheHeadAndTheReason reads the stored line by JSON key: the four are present with their values, the reason key is absent when none was given, and validate refuses a waiver with no round, no pull request or no head before it reaches either file.
- WaivedBy is §7.4.6's lookup half — given both scopes' active waivers, does one cover this record — and TestAnActiveWaiverCoversTheRecordItWasWrittenForUntilThatCodeChanges asserts it matches across both files, follows the code when the file above it moves, and stops the moment the anchored lines change per §7.4.2; the drop itself and the round-summary count stay with waived-findings-dropped, which §6.4.4 puts at merge time.
- The repository-wide file is §2.2 state shared by every pull request, so §2.3.1's per-PR lock cannot serialise it: state.WaiverLock adds one of its own at locks/waivers/<owner>/<repo>.lock, and TestARepositoryWaiverSurvivesTriageOnAnotherPullRequest was measured against a disabled lock, where five of eight waivers were lost.
- §7.4's eight items are all read: 1 and 2 by WaiverKey, 3 and 4 by the scope switch and the two files, 5 by the stored disposition, 6 by WaivedBy, 7 by the id form and RemoveWaiver, 8 by WaiverProvenance; the path-prefix widening round 8 removed is nowhere, matching being equality over the whole key.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... && golangci-lint run && ./scripts/deadcode.sh. Mutation testing at Killed 558, Lived 13, Not covered 39, efficacy 97.72%; the one new survivor is the documented equivalent mutant in nextWaiverID that finding.NextID and note.NextID already carry, and the new not-covered are validate's three bare-switch case clauses, which go tool cover reports at 100%.

tasks.title: List active waivers across both scopes
tasks.acceptance:
- cr waivers list --repo <owner/repo> [--pr <number>] prints active waivers with their scope and disposition, covering both files of §7.4.4 when --pr is given and the repository-wide file alone when it is not, per §7.4.7.
- A test asserts the PR-scoped file is invisible without --pr and visible with it.
- The listing and removal obligations are §7.4.7.

tasks.title: Remove a waiver from either scope
tasks.acceptance:
- cr waivers remove <id> --repo <owner/repo> [--pr <number>] deletes one from either scope, per §7.4.7.
- A test removes from each scope and asserts the finding raises again on the next round.

tasks.title: Render queued records into one draft
tasks.acceptance:
- cr draft <pr> renders every queued record into a single Markdown file at rounds/<n>/draft.md, per §7.1.
- The block body is free-form Markdown that the user may rewrite entirely, per §7.1.2.
- A test asserts every queued record produces exactly one block and no record in another state does.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr draft <pr> renders every queued record into one Markdown file at rounds/<n>/draft.md; internal/cli/draft.go reads the current round's records out of findings.ndjson, walks section 9.1's draft-to-queued row through finding.MayTransition with ActorDraft, hands the queued records to internal/draft.Render, and writes both the states and the file under one section 2.3.1 lock.
- The block body is free-form Markdown the user may rewrite entirely; draft.body renders the record's own summary beneath the marker and nothing parses it back, so a reviewer may replace every word without changing what the block means to cr.
- TestDraftRendersEveryQueuedRecordAndNothingElse puts one record in each of section 9.1's seven states and asserts the file holds exactly the two queued blocks; TestDraftQueuesExactlyTheRecordsItRendered reads the state and the file together so neither can claim a draft the other does not have.
- Dogfooded on an isolated CR_HOME with five records covering cited, argued, probed, duplicate and suppressed; three blocks rendered, the argued record appeared as a question, and a path holding a quote survived the marker intact.

tasks.title: Fix the record marker grammar
tasks.acceptance:
- Each record is rendered as a block introduced by an HTML comment marker carrying id, kind, path, start_line, line, severity, grade, and disposition, per §7.1.1.
- Round 8 finding undefined-marker-grammar: the marker's exact syntax is fixed and documented with one example line, and whether it uses the <!-- cr: prefix reserved by §8.1.3 is stated explicitly. Malformed is defined as any deviation from that grammar. The entire triage input channel is parsed from this grammar, and §7.2.1, §7.2.3, and §8.1.3 all branch on it.
- A test asserts a marker-like string in a body takes exactly one documented exit path, not an ambiguous one.
- A parser test covers every marker field, a missing field, an extra field, and a malformed delimiter.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Each record is rendered as a block introduced by an HTML comment marker carrying all eight fields section 7.1.1 names, in that order; internal/draft/marker.go holds markerFieldNames as the single list the renderer and the parser both walk, and TestTheMarkerCarriesEveryFieldSection711NamesInOrder reads them off the rendered line.
- The exact syntax is fixed as five numbered rules in one doc comment over the delimiters, with MarkerGrammar as the single documented example line, and a paragraph of that comment states explicitly that the marker uses section 8.1.3's reserved cr: prefix because section 8.1.3 refuses any body carrying that sequence and so makes a marker and a marker-like string the same set.
- Rule 5 defines malformed as any deviation from rules 1 to 4 and names the six shapes a deviation takes.
- ParseMarker is the one door the triage input channel's syntax comes through, MalformedMarkerError carries the one-based line section 7.2.1 requires a refusal to name and quotes MarkerGrammar back at the reviewer, and internal/cli/exit.go codes it 1 so section 7.2's abort lands where section 11.2 puts it.
- TestAMarkerLikeStringTakesExactlyOneReading drives seven lines through IsMarkerLine and ParseMarker and asserts each lands on exactly one of the three documented readings: body text, a marker, or malformed.
- TestEveryDeviationFromTheGrammarIsMalformed covers sixteen deviations including a missing field, an extra field, a reordered pair, a foreign terminator and a truncated one, while TestEveryFieldSurvivesTheRoundTrip covers every marker field across six paths including one holding a quote and one holding the marker's own terminator.

tasks.title: Render suggestions as fenced blocks
tasks.acceptance:
- A suggestion is rendered as a fenced suggestion block inside the body, and a suggestion with suggestion_origin: rule is labelled as machine generated, per §7.1.3.
- A test asserts the label appears for a rule-origin suggestion and not for an agent-origin one.
tasks.closed_reason:
- A suggestion is rendered as a fenced suggestion block inside the body: internal/draft/draft.go's body appends the block beneath the prose when the record carries a suggestion, and TestASuggestionIsRenderedAsAFencedSuggestionBlock asserts the fence, its suggestion language tag, and its position after the summary, while TestARecordWithoutASuggestionRendersNoBlock asserts the block is a consequence of the field rather than of the renderer.
- A suggestion with suggestion_origin rule is labelled as machine generated: the machineGenerated label is emitted above the fence for that origin alone, in section 2.6.2.4's own words about what cr cannot establish, and TestTheLabelNamesWhatCrCannotEstablish asserts the label names compiles, parses, and preserves behaviour rather than only naming a machine.
- A test asserts the label appears for a rule-origin suggestion and not for an agent-origin one: TestOnlyAMachineGeneratedSuggestionIsLabelled runs all three origins, requiring the fence in every case and the label only for the rule origin, and TestTheSuggestionBlockOpensNoCrOwnedRegion reads the rendered body back to assert the label opens no cr-owned region, which section 8.1.3 refuses with exit code 1.

tasks.title: Open the draft with a header
tasks.acceptance:
- The file opens with a summary header listing counts, the coverage state, and the comment count against post.max_comments, as comments that are not posted, per §7.1.4.
- A test asserts the header reports the same comment count the §1.6.2 cap check uses.

tasks.title: Store each record's agent region
tasks.acceptance:
- cr writes each record's agent region exactly as rendered to rounds/<n>/rendered.json. cr-owned regions are excluded, since cr regenerates them, per §7.1.5.
- Round 9 finding dead-signal, resolved by approved decision: the concatenated normalised hash of all agent regions is dropped from the specification. It had no consumer — §7.1.6 needs per-record content, not an aggregate — the one inference its framing invited is forbidden by §8.5.4, and §8.1.2 guarantees every body differs on every round, making the value constant.
- A test asserts rendered.json holds one entry per record and no aggregate hash.
- §7.1.5 also states that rendered.json holds only the body cr itself generated, and that a body preserved per §7.1.6 does not replace its entry. Without this the third cr draft would find body == rendered.json, conclude the body was untouched, and regenerate the human-approved prose in English.

tasks.title: Regenerate the draft preserving edited bodies
tasks.acceptance:
- The draft is regenerable. Regeneration first ingests the current draft's triage state per §7.2 — including deletions, which become discards and waivers at that moment — and then preserves bodies for records whose body differs from rendered.json. Regeneration never resurrects a deleted block, per §7.1.6.
- Round 8 finding edit-detection-comparison: edit detection is a byte-exact comparison of each record's stored agent region against the current draft's corresponding region. Without pinning it, a whitespace-only or line-ending-only edit would preserve the human's body under one reading and let regeneration overwrite it under the other.
- A test covers a whitespace-only edit, a substantive edit, a deletion followed by regeneration, and an untouched block.

tasks.title: Interpret the five draft triage verbs
tasks.acceptance:
- Triage happens by editing the file; cr draft and cr post interpret the result. The five rows of the §7.2 table: leaving a block unchanged posts it as rendered; editing the body prose posts it as edited; changing kind=finding to kind=question softens it and records a triage event; deleting the block entirely discards it with disposition not-here and writes a pull-request-scoped waiver per §7.4; setting disposition=wrong in the marker discards it as a false positive whether or not the body remains, writes a repository-wide waiver per §7.4, and counts against the class per §7.3.
- Both discard verbs are observable in the file cr reads back: deletion removes the marker, and wrong is a marker edit that survives precisely because the marker stays. A record carrying disposition=wrong is discarded even when its body is untouched, so the reviewer never has to delete text to express it.
- The two dispositions stay distinct: not-here means the finding is true but not worth a comment on this pull request — the ordinary case under §1.6 — and never counts against the class's precision; wrong means the finding is false, and is the only signal that demotes a class. Collapsing them would demote classes that are always right and merely never worth saying.
- A test drives all five verbs and asserts the resulting disposition, waiver scope, and statistics contribution for each.

tasks.title: Enforce the marker field edit semantics
tasks.acceptance:
- The six rows of §7.2's marker edit-semantics table: id is immutable and a changed or unknown id aborts; kind finding to question softens, and question to finding is accepted only when the recomputed grade is probed or cited, aborting otherwise per §6.3.3; path, start_line and line are re-validated per §6.1.2 and abort when the anchor no longer resolves; severity is freely editable and recorded as a triage event; disposition set to wrong discards as a false positive, while not-here is written by cr on deletion and is never set by hand; grade is informational, recomputed by cr per §6.2 and ignored, aborting only when the marker's kind contradicts the recomputed grade per §6.3.3.
