- Any other marker edit aborts with exit code 1, naming the record id.
- cr post refuses to run when a marker is malformed, naming the line, per §7.2.1.
- A test exercises each row's accept path and each row's abort path.
- Round 12 finding anchor-hash-not-recomputed, assigned here: §7.2 re-validates path, start_line, and line after a marker edit but says nothing about the anchor's content hash, which §9.2 makes part of the anchor and §7.4.1 keys waivers on. The implementation recomputes it whenever the anchor lines change.

tasks.title: Recompute grades before building the payload
tasks.acceptance:
- cr post recomputes every record's grade and re-applies §6.3 before building the payload, so no draft edit can turn an argued record into a posted assertion, per §7.2.2.
- A test edits a marker to kind=finding on an argued record and asserts posting is refused.

tasks.title: Abort on an unknown marker id
tasks.acceptance:
- v0.1 has no manual-comment channel in the draft. A block whose id is unknown aborts with exit code 1 rather than being adopted as a new record, per §7.2.3.
- Every record in the corpus carries a role, an axis, and a grade cr computed, and a hand-written block can carry none of them. A comment the reviewer wants to make in their own name is written on GitHub directly, after posting.
- A test adds a hand-written block and asserts exit 1 naming the unknown id.

tasks.title: Write triage events idempotently per key
tasks.acceptance:
- Triage events are written idempotently: re-running a command overwrites the event for its key rather than appending a second one, so regenerating a draft per §7.1.6 or running cr post twice cannot inflate a count, per §7.3.1.
- cr draft writes one raised event per record it queues, and writes the outcome event directly for a record it discards at draft time. cr post --confirm writes exactly one outcome event per queued record, drawn from kept, softened, discarded-not-here, and discarded-wrong; cr post without --confirm writes none, since it changes nothing.
- Round 8 finding triage-event-key-permits-contradiction: outcome events key on (PR, round, record id) with the action as a value, so a later run replaces the earlier outcome; raised stays a separately keyed event. With action inside the key a record could carry both kept and discarded-wrong against a single raised — reachable through the ordinary retry after §8.4.2 — inflating §7.3.4's demotion rate on exactly the class the retry touched.
- Round 8 finding triage-event-key-permits-contradiction: cr post --confirm writes its outcome events after the network call, and a call rejected per §8.4.2 leaves no outcome event behind.
- A test drives a rejected post followed by a re-triage and asserts one outcome event survives.

tasks.title: Carry the full field set per event
tasks.acceptance:
- Every event carries class, axis, role, grade, rule id when present, the PR, the round, and the head, per §7.3.1.
- Round 8 finding unnameable-triage-event: a severity edit, which §7.2's marker table calls freely editable and recorded as a triage event, has a nameable representation. severity is added to the fields every event carries and a severity edit is recorded on the record's single outcome event rather than as an event of its own, so §7.3.1's closed five-name vocabulary and its exactly-one-outcome rule both hold.
- The five action names are the complete vocabulary the §7.3 statistics are computed from.
- A test edits only severity and asserts the change is observable in exactly one event.

tasks.title: Report triage statistics per class
tasks.acceptance:
- cr stats --repo <owner/repo> reports per class and per rule: raised, kept, softened, discarded as not-here, and discarded as wrong, per §7.3.2.
- The statistics are computed from the repository's triage.ndjson across pull requests.
- A test seeds events across two PRs and asserts the per-class and per-rule breakdowns.

tasks.title: Report every class first seen
tasks.acceptance:
- class is agent-composed, so a reworded slug would silently escape the waiver and posted-index keys of §7.4.1 and §9.3.6. cr reports every class first seen in a round as new, in the round summary and in cr stats, so drift is visible rather than silent, per §7.3.3.
- A test reruns a round with a reworded class slug and asserts the new-class report fires.

tasks.title: Compute the demotion rate as bound
tasks.acceptance:
- The demotion rate for a class is (discarded-wrong + softened) / raised over that class's events in the repository's triage.ndjson. Discards dispositioned not-here are excluded from the numerator, because they carry no evidence that the class is imprecise, per §7.3.4.
- A class whose rate exceeds stats.demote_threshold (default 0.6) over at least stats.min_samples (default 8) raised events is listed as a demotion candidate.
- Marking a false positive wrong costs the reviewer an extra edit while plain deletion is free, so discarded-wrong is systematically under-counted and the demotion rate is a lower bound on imprecision. cr reports it as a lower bound and never presents it as a measured precision, per §7.3.5.
- A test asserts the not-here exclusion and the lower-bound wording.

tasks.title: Report accurate classes rarely worth posting
tasks.acceptance:
- A class whose not-here rate exceeds stats.demote_threshold over the same sample is reported separately as a volume candidate: it is accurate but rarely worth posting, and the remedy is to stop raising it, not to soften it, per §7.3.6.
- Both candidacies are reports to the user, not automatic changes. cr never alters a rule's kind by itself, per §7.3.7.
- A test asserts a high not-here class appears as a volume candidate and not as a demotion candidate.

tasks.title: Define the anchor field set
tasks.acceptance:
- An anchor carries path, side, start_line, line, a normalised content hash, and up to three lines of context on each side, per §9.2.
- The content hash is the normalised hash per §1.4 of the lines from start_line to line inclusive, treated as one text — so a single-line anchor and a multi-line anchor hash by the same rule.
- Valid side values are RIGHT and LEFT.
- A test asserts a one-line and a three-line anchor hash by the same function.
- Round 12 finding unordered-range-fields, assigned here: nothing requires start_line <= line. The implementation rejects an anchor whose range is inverted or empty.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/finding/anchor.go holds §9.2 anchor rules beside the Anchor struct internal/finding/finding.go already carries, with path, side, start_line, line, content_hash and the two context windows, and ValidateAnchor bounds each window at contextWindow, three lines a side, with TestAnAnchorRecordsAtMostThreeLinesOfContextOnEachSide asserting that three passes and a fourth on either side does not.
- AnchorContentHash joins the anchored lines with a single LF and hands the whole text to text.NormalisedHash, so §1.4 runs once over the range and there is no branch on the line count at all — TestTheContentHashBranchesOnNothing reads that off anchor.go own source and proves the walker fires by asserting ValidateAnchor next door does branch.
- ValidateAnchor closes side against anchorSides, git.Right and git.Left, because git.Side is a defined string any untyped constant reaches, and TestAnAnchorNamesOneOfSection92sTwoSides accepts the two and refuses the empty value, right, Right, "RIGHT ", MIDDLE and BOTH with the offending value quoted back.
- TestAOneLineAndAThreeLineAnchorHashByTheSameFunction asserts the properties a special-cased one-line path would break rather than restating strings.Join — §1.4 normalisation reaches both sizes, a three-line anchor hashes as the one-line anchor carrying the same LFs, and neither the first line alone nor the reversed order reaches that digest.
- Round 12 unordered-range-fields is answered where §9.2 leaves the two numbers unordered, ValidateAnchor being the single place the pair is read as a range before §6.2.2 containment and §8.3.3 payload ordering rely on it, wired into checker.check in internal/finding/validate.go and proven on every door by TestAnAnchorRunningBackwardsNeverBecomesARecord.
- ValidateAnchor rejects line < start_line as inverted and start_line < 1 as the empty range that names no line of any file, an inclusive range making start_line == line a legal one-line anchor rather than an empty one and §9.2 required start_line ruling out GitHub optional one, with TestAnAnchorRangeRunsForwardsFromALineOfTheFile pinning both boundaries.

tasks.title: Resolve anchor sides against two trees
tasks.acceptance:
- RIGHT anchors a line in the head. LEFT anchors a removed line and is used only for records about deletions, per §9.2.1.
- Every record in findings.ndjson has an anchor; an item with no code location never becomes a record, per §4.1.3.
- A test resolves a RIGHT anchor against the head and a LEFT anchor against the merge base, and asserts a LEFT anchor pointing at a head-only line fails.
- Carried from anchor-schema: internal/gh/threads.go converts a GitHub diffSide with a raw git.Side(n.DiffSide) and validates nothing, so an unexpected value silently yields a thread anchor whose side matches no hunk in §3.5.3. The conversion is validated or the thread is refused.
tasks.closed_reason:
- §9.2.1's first half is where §6.1.2 puts it: internal/finding/anchor.go's ResolveAnchor sends a RIGHT anchor to the head and a LEFT one to the merge base, through a Trees pair of readers, so RIGHT anchors a line in the head and LEFT a line the head no longer has.
- The second half, that LEFT is used only for records about deletions, is documented rather than enforced, and ResolveAnchor says why: whether a record is about a deletion is a judgement about what it says, which §2.1 leaves to the agent and invariant 1 keeps cr out of. What cr establishes is the location, and a line the change added is not in the merge base to be anchored.
- Every record in findings.ndjson has an anchor already, and nothing was rebuilt: internal/finding/fields.go marks the anchor row Required, checker.check walks that table on every door and then hands the anchor to ValidateAnchor, which refuses one naming no path as an item with no code location per §6.1.2 and §4.1.3.
- The test that would catch the rule's removal already exists as well: TestNoUnanchoredItemBecomesARecordByAnyDoor in internal/finding/anchored_test.go reads the set of exported functions handing back a Finding out of the package's own source and drives all four shapes of an unanchored item through each, so a new door is a failing test rather than a reopened comment channel.
- TestARightAnchorResolvesAgainstTheHeadAndALeftOneAgainstTheMergeBase resolves a RIGHT anchor against the head and a LEFT anchor against the merge base over a real two-commit repository built by twoTrees, whose branch rewrites a line, adds a file and deletes one, so each side resolves the file only its own tree holds and is refused the other's by name. Swapping the two readers was verified to fail it in three places.
- TestALeftAnchorPointingAtAHeadOnlyLineIsRefused asserts the failure the two trees exist to produce: the head's lines 7 to 9 are four lines the change added, the merge base holds five, and the LEFT anchor is refused naming the tree and its length, with the boundary either side of line 5 pinned and the same ranges resolving on RIGHT.
- TestASideNamingNeitherTreeResolvesAgainstNothing drives six near-miss sides through readers that fail the test if they are opened at all, because refused and read-the-head-anyway are the same error to a caller and different faults.
- The carried finding is fixed at its root: §9.2's vocabulary is now closed once, by git.ParseSide beside the two constants, and both readers of an outside value go through it, ValidateAnchor for an agent's NDJSON side and internal/gh for GitHub's diffSide, so the set cannot be closed twice and drift.
- internal/gh/threads.go's raw git.Side(n.DiffSide) is gone: threadNode.anchor now returns an error, and an unknown value refuses the thread and aborts the ingest naming the thread id and quoting the value, rather than dropping it. Dropping is the quiet answer and it is the expensive one, because a thread with a side matching no hunk attaches to no unit under §3.5.3, suppresses nothing under §3.5.4, and cr repeats a concern a colleague already raised with nothing in the run reporting it; §3.5.1 admits no exception either.
- TestAThreadWhoseDiffSideNamesNeitherTreeIsRefused covers six unplaceable values, asserts no partial thread set is handed back, and asserts RIGHT and LEFT still ingest unchanged. One existing payload, TestOnlyGitHubsOwnBotTypeIsTaggedBot's, was completed with the diffSide GitHub declares non-null; no assertion of any existing test changed.
- gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 586, Lived 13, Not covered 39, Timed out 6, efficacy 97.83 percent: all eight new mutants killed, the thirteen commented equivalents unchanged, and the two ParseSide mutants gremlins first reported as not covered are killed by TestParseSideAdmitsRightAndLeftAndNothingElse in internal/git.

tasks.title: Record anchor context without migrating it
tasks.acceptance:
- An anchor is bound to the head it was produced against. cr never migrates an anchor across a head change in v0.1. Migration is the first thing v0.2 adds, and guessing at it silently is worse than declaring the round stale per §9.3, per §9.2.2.
- The context window and content hash are recorded even though v0.1 never migrates, so that a v0.2 migration has what it needs from rounds v0.1 produced, per §9.2.3.
- A test asserts a head change produces stale records and no migrated anchor, while the context window survives on disk.

tasks.title: Define the seven record states
tasks.acceptance:
- A record's life in v0.1 ends when it is posted. Everything after that — the author replying, pushing, and the reviewer verifying, resolving, or withdrawing — is the re-review half of the loop, and lands in v0.2 per §1.3.
- The seven states of the §9.1 table: draft (recorded, not yet queued), queued (rendered into the current draft), duplicate (§6.4.3), suppressed (§3.5.4), discarded (deleted during triage, waiver written, disposition set), posted (sent to GitHub, thread created), stale (abandoned unposted when the head moved, §9.3.4).
- Terminal states are posted, discarded, duplicate, suppressed, and stale. Every other state is open per §1.1, per §9.1.2.
tasks.closed_reason:
- A record's life ends at posting, and StatePosted is where internal/finding/state.go's vocabulary stops: nothing follows it, and the type's doc says so in the words §9's opening paragraph uses.
- The four states the re-review half would need — verified, resolved, accepted, withdrawn — are unrepresentable rather than merely absent, because State is a struct around an unexported name that nothing outside state.go can build and ParseState is the only door in from a string; TestTheSevenStatesAreTheOnesTheSpecWrites puts all four through it and reads the §1.3.6 pointer back out of the error, so a later contributor cannot widen the set by writing a literal anywhere in the tree.
- The seven of the §9.1 table are StateDraft, StateQueued, StateDuplicate, StateSuppressed, StateDiscarded, StatePosted and StateStale, each documented with the meaning and cross-reference the table gives it, held in table order by the states literal and handed out only as a copy by States(); ParseState round-trips every name, MarshalJSON and UnmarshalJSON carry them to and from findings.ndjson under the same check with §6.1's row switched to omitzero, and TestTheSevenStatesAreTheOnesTheSpecWrites and TestAStateOutsideTheTableNeverReachesARecord pin the exact set, the copy, and the refusal of an eighth on the wire.
- §9.1.2's five — posted, discarded, duplicate, suppressed, stale — are the one list written out, in the order that item writes them, and State.Terminal() reads only that literal.
- §1.1's open set is derived from the terminal list rather than restated, by State.Open() and by OpenStates(), so §10.2.4's "no record remains in draft or queued" cannot drift from it; TestOpenIsEveryStateThatIsNotTerminal asserts over the whole table that no state falls into both halves or neither, that the derived open set is exactly draft and queued, and that the zero State is neither open nor terminal.

tasks.title: Enforce the exhaustive transition table
tasks.acceptance:
- Transitions are exhaustive. The six rows of the §9.1 transition table: new record to draft by cr record; draft to duplicate or suppressed by cr record; draft to queued by cr draft; queued to discarded by cr draft or cr post --confirm; queued to posted by cr post --confirm or cr post --reconcile on adopt; draft or queued to stale by cr brief on a new head per §9.3.4.
- A transition not listed is rejected with exit code 4, naming the record and its current state.
- cr merge is not a producer: it runs on role output files before any record exists, and §6.4.3 marks duplicates as cr record writes them.
- A table-driven test asserts every listed transition succeeds and a representative sample of unlisted ones exits 4.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/finding/transition.go holds §9.1's transition table as six rows in the spec's own three columns, so a cell holding several values stays one row and the decision is a lookup into what those rows expand to, closed by default because §9.1 says a transition not listed MUST be rejected.
- Row one, creation to draft by cr record, is spelled with a From type rather than a State: Creation is a value no State can equal, and the zero From is Existing of the zero State, which no row names, so state.go's deliberate reading of the zero State as neither open nor terminal is left intact.
- Row two, draft to duplicate and draft to suppressed by cr record, puts §6.4.3's duplicate marking and §3.5.4's thread suppression at the command that writes the record.
- Row three, draft to queued by cr draft, and row four, queued to discarded by cr draft and by cr post --confirm, are listed with their actors, which is why the actor is part of the key rather than context around it.
- Row five, queued to posted by cr post --confirm and by cr post --reconcile, gives the reconcile the one move §9.1 allows it and refuses it the discard row four gives cr post --confirm, and the on-adopt qualifier stays a precondition cr post checks before it asks.
- Row six, draft to stale and queued to stale by cr brief, is §9.3.4's move, and the new-head qualifier is likewise a fact about the run that §9.1 gives no state to read from.
- MayTransition returns an IllegalTransitionError for every triple the six rows do not list, naming the record, the state it is in and the actor that asked, with a §12.4 hint listing what §9.1 does allow out of that state, and internal/cli/exit.go maps it onto ExitState, the first error to reach §11.2's code 4, asserted by TestAnUnlistedTransitionExitsWithTheStateCode over five ways the table can be misread.
- cr merge is left no way to be a producer: Actor's only field is unexported so no command outside internal/finding can be one, and TestCrMergeIsNoProducerOfRecordState reads every Actor composite literal out of the package's own non-test source and matches the set against §9.1's third column, then drives cr merge's own door, DecodePerRole, and finds its records in no §9.1 state and a supplied state refused by §6.1.4.
- TestEveryTransitionIsTheTableAndNothingElse is table-driven over §9.1 transcribed by hand rather than read from the implementation, and walks the whole cross product of nine From values, eight To values and six actors, asserting the ten listed cells pass and all 422 others are refused.
- TestARefusalNamesTheRecordAndItsCurrentState covers the queued, posted, creation and no-state renderings, the terminal case where §9.1 lists no move out, and the error's fields as fields rather than as text.
- Gate green and gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 466, Lived 10, efficacy 97.90 percent with the same three known TIMED OUT, and all ten survivors are the previously classified equivalents in cli/context.go, config/config.go, finding/fields.go, finding/id.go, finding/state.go, note/note.go and profile/none.go, none of them in transition.go.
Out of scope: §9.1.1's transitions.ndjson journal is transition-journal, §9.3.4's stale sweep is new-round-invalidation, and the six commands are their own tasks, so nothing here performs or records a transition. internal/finding/validate.go lines 100-103 carry the DocPerRole doc comment sentence twice, a stray duplication left by an earlier unit.

tasks.title: Journal every transition with its actor
tasks.acceptance:
- Transitions are recorded in transitions.ndjson with a timestamp, the head SHA, and the actor, per §9.1.1.
- A test asserts every transition of the §9.1 table leaves exactly one journal line.

tasks.title: Compare the current head every command
tasks.acceptance:
- cr compares the current head to meta.json's recorded head on every command that reads per-PR state, and reports both when they differ, per §9.3.1.
- The stale-round report is an honesty disclosure and survives --quiet per §11.1.
- A test asserts every state-reading command emits the comparison.
- Found by answer-command, assigned here: cr answer reads meta.json for the issue key, so §9.3.1 binds it even though it writes no per-PR state and §9.3.2's refusal therefore does not. The command set this task enumerates is derived from what actually reads per-PR state, not from a hand-kept list.

tasks.title: Refuse writes when the head moved
tasks.acceptance:
- When the heads differ, every command that writes per-PR state refuses with exit code 4, naming both heads; cr brief is the only way forward, per §9.3.2.
- cr post --reconcile is exempt: it anchors nothing and only matches the §8.4.3 payload hash against the PR's existing reviews.
- A test moves the head and asserts every writing command exits 4 while cr brief and cr post --reconcile proceed.

tasks.title: Increment the round on head change
tasks.acceptance:
- cr brief increments meta.json's round index if and only if the current head differs from the recorded head, and then stores the new head, per §9.3.3.
- A same-head cr brief is idempotent.
- A test asserts the index moves exactly once per distinct head.

tasks.title: Stale records before clearing the mapping
tasks.acceptance:
- On the increment every record still in draft or queued moves to stale, mapping.ndjson is cleared, and cr brief recomputes units and threads for the new head, per §9.3.4.
- Claims are carried forward unchanged; cr brief re-reads the issue text and re-runs the §3.3.3 drift comparison, and never re-extracts.
- A test asserts drafted records go stale, the mapping is empty, units are renumbered, and claims survive with a drift report.

tasks.title: Read only the current round records
tasks.acceptance:
- Every record carries round and head, and a command reads only the current round's records; earlier rounds are history, per §9.3.5.
- A command documented as replacing or clearing a file does so for the current round only and leaves earlier rounds intact.
- Waivers per §7.4, the context store per §3.6, and the posted index of §9.3.6 apply across rounds and are exempt from this scoping.
- A test asserts round 1 records are invisible to round 2 commands while the three exemptions still load.
- Round 12 finding closed-exemption-list-blocks-required-behaviour, assigned here: §9.3.5's exemption list is closed and does not cover the cross-round staling §9.3.4 requires, which would make the stale state unreachable. The implementation treats §9.3.4's transition as exempt.

tasks.title: Maintain the posted index at post
tasks.acceptance:
- cr maintains a posted index in posted-index.ndjson, keyed exactly as a §7.4.1 waiver is, holding one entry per record that reached posted, per §9.3.6.
- A finding matching an entry is dropped at merge and counted in the round summary, and is never written to findings.ndjson at all, exactly as §6.4.4 drops a waived finding.
- Round 8 finding unassigned-writer: cr post is named as the writer, appending one entry per record it moves to posted, on --confirm and on --reconcile adopt alike. The file is load-bearing — a missing entry silently re-raises a comment the author already received — and §10.3's writer list shows the document is otherwise explicit about ownership.
- A test posts a finding in round 1 and asserts the identical finding is dropped in round 2 with the drop counted.

tasks.title: Enumerate the render language domain
tasks.acceptance:
- Comment bodies are written in the language configured by render.lang, defaulting to tr, per §8.1.1.
- Round 8 finding render-lang-domain-unbounded: the valid v0.1 values are enumerated as tr and en, any other value aborts with exit code 3 naming the setting, and the built-in label text for each enumerated language is fixed in the implementation so it is testable rather than an implementation choice. §8.1.4 requires the question label to be built in per render.lang and explicitly non-configurable, which cannot hold for a free-form string — for an unknown language there is no built-in label and §6.3's forcing would reach the reader through nothing.
- Findings are stored in English; reader-facing prose is produced at draft time.
- A test asserts render.lang: de aborts with exit code 3 and that both enumerated languages carry a label.
- Round 12 finding unspecified-render-language, assigned here: §8.4.3's review-body disclosure never names a language. It is rendered in render.lang like every other author-facing body.
tasks.closed_reason:
- §8.1.1's language is the setting internal/config resolves as render.lang, defaulting to tr: the built-in table now takes both the key and the default from render.Setting and render.LangTR, so the table cannot drift from the domain, and TestRenderLangDefaultsToTurkishAndRejectsAnUnknownLanguage asserts the resolved default is tr.
- Round 8's render-lang-domain-unbounded: internal/render/lang.go enumerates exactly tr and en as Lang struct{code string} values, constructible nowhere outside the package and reachable from a string only through ParseLang — the same fence finding.State uses — and TestV01RendersInExactlyTurkishAndEnglish asserts the set whole and in order, so a third language cannot be added without the label table it then has to satisfy.
- Any other value aborts with exit code 3 naming the setting: config.Resolve parses render.lang once every layer has settled, internal/cli exitCodeFor maps a render.UnknownLangError onto ExitFile per §11.2's file-or-configuration row, and the freshly built binary exits 3 on CR_RENDER_LANG=de with a message naming render.lang, the rejected value, and the two it may hold.
- The built-in label text is fixed in the implementation rather than left to whatever renders it: internal/render/label.go writes out all six language-by-grade lines as literals, QuestionLabel is a lookup with no format string and nothing a profile, role, or rule can reach, and the exact Turkish and English lines are asserted rather than only their shape.
- Findings are stored in English: TestNoStoredRecordCarriesReaderFacingProse reads §6.1's field table out of finding.Fields and finding.CitationFields and shows no row could hold a body, a label, a language, or a translation — a record keeps summary and evidence, and the stored English grade word is what the Turkish line carries into the reader's view rather than the reverse.
- Reader-facing prose is produced at draft time: TestNoRenderingDecisionCanReachStoredState proves the separation structurally in both directions — no file of internal/render imports the filesystem, an encoder, or internal/state, and none of state, finding, note, intent, unit or testadequacy imports internal/render — so a rendering decision cannot reach disk and a stored value cannot be chosen by a language.
- A test asserts render.lang: de aborts with exit code 3 and that both enumerated languages carry a label: TestAnUnknownRenderLanguageExitsWithTheFileCode maps the error and runs cr config with CR_RENDER_LANG=de, asserting ExitFile, the setting named, the value quoted, and nothing printed; TestEveryLanguageCarriesABuiltInQuestionLabelForEveryGrade holds the table total over Langs times §6.2's three grades, with no line shared and none carrying a newline.
- Round 12's unspecified-render-language: §8.4.3's review body carries §4.5.4's disclosure to the author, so it is author-facing and is rendered in render.lang like the comment body of §8.1.1; internal/render/body.go makes that a closed set rather than a sentence — BodyComment and BodyReview — and TestTheReviewBodyIsAnAuthorFacingBodyLikeTheComment asserts it where the later review-body renderer will read it.
- Gate green: go test -race ./... and golangci-lint run and ./scripts/deadcode.sh all pass; gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 471, Lived 10, efficacy 97.92 percent against the 466/10/97.90 baseline, with the same three known TIMED OUT and no new survivor — all four mutants inside internal/render are killed.

tasks.title: Compose the initial body in English
tasks.acceptance:
- cr renders each block's initial body from the record's summary and evidence, in English, per §8.1.2.
- The agent then rewrites that body in render.lang by editing draft.md before the human reads it. Editing the draft is the only input path for reader-facing prose: cr never translates or composes, and never accepts a body through any other channel.
- A test asserts no command accepts a body argument or a body field.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr renders each block's initial body from the record's summary and evidence, in English, per §8.1.2: internal/draft/draft.go's body places the stored summary and the stored evidence verbatim as two paragraphs in that order, with no word of cr's between them, followed by §7.1.3's suggestion block when one exists; TestTheInitialBodyIsTheSummaryThenTheEvidenceVerbatim compares the whole body for equality, TestTheInitialBodyCarriesBothFieldsByteForByte carries Markdown through untouched, TestTheSuggestionFollowsTheInitialBody keeps the suggestion beneath, and TestAnEmptyFieldContributesNoParagraph leaves no blank paragraph for an empty field.
- The agent then rewrites that body in render.lang by editing draft.md before the human reads it: the block body stays the §7.1.2 free-form region the agent edits, and since §6.1.1 keeps both fields English the initial body is English without cr translating anything.
- Editing the draft is the only input path for reader-facing prose, cr never translates or composes, and never accepts a body through any other channel: body only concatenates two stored fields, and no command, flag, positional, or decoded record type carries a body.
- A test asserts no command accepts a body argument or a body field: internal/cli/bodychannel_test.go's TestNoCommandAcceptsABodyArgumentOrABodyField walks every flag and every Use line of the whole tree for "body", walks the JSON keys of finding.Finding, intent.Claim, mapping.Pair and coverage.Cell recursively, and runs cr record then cr draft over a record carrying a body key to show the key never reaches the block while the summary and evidence do.
- Existing tests TestABlockIsAMarkerAndABody and TestEveryRecordIsItsOwnBlockInTheOrderItArrived were updated for the second paragraph (5b090a1); no assertion was weakened.

tasks.title: Delimit each cr-owned comment region
tasks.acceptance:
- A body is non-empty and never contains the marker comment. A posted comment is a fixed sequence of regions: the §8.1.4 label, the §8.1.6 provenance block when one applies, the agent body, and the §8.1.7 evidence block when one applies, per §8.1.3.
- Each cr-owned region is delimited by its own named pair — <!-- cr:label -->…<!-- cr:/label -->, <!-- cr:provenance -->…<!-- cr:/provenance -->, <!-- cr:evidence -->…<!-- cr:/evidence --> — so recovery never depends on counting.
- A body containing any <!-- cr: sequence is rejected with exit code 1.
- cr regenerates every owned region and discards edits inside them; §8.1.5, §7.1.5, and §7.1.6 apply to the agent region alone.
- A test asserts an edit inside an owned region is discarded while the same edit in the agent region survives.
tasks.closed_reason:
- A body is non-empty and never contains the marker comment: internal/render/comment.go's ValidateBody refuses a body that is empty or whitespace only and one carrying the Reserved sequence `<!-- cr:`, which covers §7.1.1's record marker and every owned delimiter, naming the record in a BodyError; TestABodyIsNonEmptyAndCarriesNoReservedSequence covers seven refused and three accepted bodies.
- A posted comment is a fixed sequence of regions, the §8.1.4 label, the §8.1.6 provenance block when one applies, the agent body, and the §8.1.7 evidence block when one applies, per §8.1.3: Comment holds the four regions and Comment.String joins the ones present in that fixed order with one blank line between each two, so no caller can reorder them; TestACommentIsTheFixedSequenceOfRegions asserts the full order and that an absent region leaves no separator, and internal/draft's block now renders every body through Comment.
- Each cr-owned region is delimited by its own named pair, `<!-- cr:label -->`…`<!-- cr:/label -->`, `<!-- cr:provenance -->`…`<!-- cr:/provenance -->`, `<!-- cr:evidence -->`…`<!-- cr:/evidence -->`, so recovery never depends on counting: ownedRegions lists the three pairs, the evidence pair reusing evidence.go's constants, and AgentRegion finds each region by its pair wherever it sits; TestEveryOwnedRegionIsDelimitedByItsOwnNamedPair pins the six markers verbatim and TestRecoveryFindsARegionByItsPairNotItsPosition recovers the body from a rearranged comment.
- A body containing any <!-- cr: sequence is rejected with exit code 1: exitCodeFor maps render.BodyError to ExitValidation, and cr draft now refuses a record whose initial body carries the sequence before writing anything; TestAnInitialBodyThatSection813RefusesStopsTheDraft covers the summary, the evidence, a suggestion and an empty body, and TestDraftRejectsABodyCarryingTheReservedSequence asserts exit code 1, the record id in the error, no draft.md, and every record left in draft.
- cr regenerates every owned region and discards edits inside them: AgentRegion removes each complete owned region whole, whatever was typed inside it, so the caller rebuilds the Comment from the record with the recovered agent region; a marker left without its partner stays in the agent region and ValidateBody refuses it rather than cr guessing, per TestAHalfDeletedRegionIsRefusedRatherThanGuessed.
- §8.1.5, §7.1.5, and §7.1.6 apply to the agent region alone: AgentRegion returns exactly the Body a comment was built from when nobody edited it, for all eight combinations of owned regions (TestAnUneditedCommentRecoversItsBody), so rendered.json comparison and the question-mark check read the agent region only; the draft read-back that calls AgentRegion arrives with draft-rendered-regions and draft-regeneration, and until then AgentRegion is reached from tests only.
- A test asserts an edit inside an owned region is discarded while the same edit in the agent region survives: TestAnEditInsideAnOwnedRegionIsDiscardedWhileTheSameEditInTheAgentRegionSurvives writes one edit into all three owned regions and the agent region, regenerates, and asserts exactly one copy survives, in the agent region, with every owned region byte-identical to what cr generated.
- Render now returns an error, so the existing draft tests call it through a renderOf helper (bda98f3); that is a call-site change with no assertion weakened.

tasks.title: Prepend the fixed question label
tasks.acceptance:
- cr prepends a fixed, cr-owned label line to every kind=question comment, naming the register and the grade, per §8.1.4.
- The label text is built in per render.lang and is not configurable: §6.3's forcing reaches the reader through this line alone, so §2.7 protects it exactly as it protects the gate.
- A test asserts the label is unreachable from every configuration layer and appears on every question.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr prepends a fixed, cr-owned label line to every kind=question comment, naming the register and the grade, per §8.1.4: internal/draft/draft.go's commentOf sets Comment.Label to render.QuestionLabelRegion(lang, grade) for every record whose kind is question after §6.3's forcing, so the §8.1.4 row, which names the register and the grade, opens the comment between §8.1.3's label pair; a finding carries none; TestEveryQuestionOpensWithItsLabelAndNoFindingCarriesOne drafts a question and a finding for each of the two languages and three grades and asserts the whole marker, label, body sequence, and TestTheDraftedLabelIsNotPartOfTheAgentRegion shows AgentRegion strips it, so the label is regenerated and never read back.
- The label text is built in per render.lang and is not configurable: QuestionLabelRegion is a lookup into label.go's literal table and never a composition, and cr draft resolves only render.lang through §2.7 (renderLang), which picks a row; a pair with no row is refused with NoLabelError, coded 3, rather than rendered without a label, per TestAPairTheTableHasNoRowForIsRefused and TestAQuestionTheTableCannotLabelStopsTheDraft.
- §6.3's forcing reaches the reader through this line alone, so §2.7 protects it exactly as it protects the gate: config.Resolve's existing label token refuses every layer's name addressing it, and cr draft now runs that resolution, so a spoiled layer stops the draft with exit code 3 before anything is written.
- A test asserts the label is unreachable from every configuration layer and appears on every question: internal/cli/labelunreachable_test.go's TestTheQuestionLabelIsUnreachableFromEveryConfigurationLayer checks all five §2.7 layers through cr draft (no flag names the label and every global flag leaves the built-in line; CR_RENDER_LABEL, CR_QUESTION_LABEL and CR_POST_LABELS, a per-repository key and a nested global key each refuse with exit 3 and no draft.md; no built-in default holds a label key) and shows render.lang choosing the Turkish row by default and the English row when set, never supplying text.
- Render now takes the language, so the draft test helper and the reserved-sequence test pass render.LangEN (fe21c2c); a call-site change with no assertion weakened.

tasks.title: Refuse a question body without punctuation
tasks.acceptance:
- cr refuses to post a kind=question body containing no ? character, with exit code 1 naming the record id, per §8.1.5.
- The register of a question is not cosmetic: without it, §6.3's forcing changes only a field the reader never sees.
- A test asserts a declarative question body is refused.

tasks.title: Emit provenance for weak record origins
tasks.acceptance:
- Weak provenance is disclosed in the posted body, not only in the draft the author never sees. cr emits a cr-owned provenance region per §8.1.3 when the record carries suggestion_origin: rule, rests on a claim with source: note, or takes its grade from a citation with origin: rule — the last being the one that buys the assertion register mechanically, per §8.1.6.
- The region names the machine origin, or the note and its source per §3.6.3, or the rule id with its rationale per §2.6.4. Being cr-owned, it is generated and enforced rather than requested.
- Round 9 finding provenance-trigger-ambiguity: the third trigger is restated mechanically as any stored citation carrying origin: rule, regardless of what else qualifies the record for cited. When a record carries both a rule citation and an outside-unit agent citation either alone earns cited, so takes its grade from admits two defensible readings and two contradictory tests.
- A test covers all three triggers plus the both-citations case.
- Round 12 finding provenance-trigger-undecidable, assigned here: 'takes its grade from a citation with origin: rule' is undecidable against §6.2's disjunctive cited rule, and the or-list states no composition rule when triggers coincide. The implementation emits the region whenever any stored citation carries origin: rule, and emits every applicable trigger's content in the §8.1.6 order.

tasks.title: Append the evidence region per grade
tasks.acceptance:
- cr appends a cr-owned evidence region per §8.1.3 beneath the agent body of every record whose grade asserts. For cited it lists each stored citation as path:line; for probed it carries the probe's kind, target, filter, result, and output_tail, so the strongest register is the one the author can check rather than the one they must take on trust. It is generated by template substitution, regenerated at render and post time, and never editable, per §8.1.7.
- Round 9 finding unverifiable-evidence-region: the region also carries the probe's input for both kinds — the patch or test file cr actually executed. Without it a semantically inert mutation (a comment, a whitespace edit, a log string, dead code) produces a genuine no-test-failed against a passing baseline, grades probed, and posts as this line is untested with nothing the author can inspect; and for a gap probe §5.4.4 concedes cr cannot distinguish a wrong behaviour from a wrong test, leaving the author that distinction with no material to make it.
- The input is capped by post.max_probe_input_bytes and the region states when it was truncated.
- A test asserts the mutation patch and the gap test both reach the rendered region, and that truncation is announced.
- Round 11 finding undisclosed-evidence-limit, assigned here: §5.4.4 concedes cr cannot distinguish a wrong behaviour from a wrong test, but unlike §5.3.6's filter obligation that limit never reaches the reader. The evidence region states it for a gap probe.
- Carried from mutation-filter-scoping: internal/render/separation_test.go's recordKeepers list, which names the packages that must not import render, does not include probe, and this slice created the first render to probe edge. That direction is the one §8.1.2 wants; adding probe to the list closes the reverse for free.

tasks.title: Validate suggestion ranges within one hunk
tasks.acceptance:
- A suggestion maps to a contiguous line range that exists in the PR diff on the RIGHT side, per §8.2.1, and the range is within one hunk, per §8.2.2.
- A suggestion failing validation blocks posting with exit code 1 and names the record id, per §8.2.4.
- A test covers an out-of-diff range, a range spanning two hunks, and a LEFT-side range.
- Round 12 finding suggestion-range-unbound, assigned here: the implementation bounds the suggestion's line count against the hunk it sits in rather than accepting any contiguous range.

tasks.title: Warn on mismatched suggestion indentation
tasks.acceptance:
- cr never infers intent about indentation. When the leading whitespace of the suggestion's first line differs from that of the first replaced line, cr warns and shows both, and still posts when the user leaves the block in place, per §8.2.3.
- A test asserts the warning appears and the post proceeds.

tasks.title: Post every comment as one review
tasks.acceptance:
- All comments in a round are posted as one GitHub review, so the author receives a single notification, per §8.3.1.
- The review event is COMMENT in v0.1; cr never emits APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES, per §8.3.2.
- A test asserts one review-creation call for a multi-comment round and that no other event value is reachable.

tasks.title: Compute the payload hash over preimage
tasks.acceptance:
- The exact posted payload is written to rounds/<n>/posted.json before the network call, and updated with returned thread ids after it, per §8.3.3.
- The payload hash is computed over an explicit pre-image, never over a JSON serialisation whose field order or spacing is unspecified: each comment contributes its path, start_line, line, side, and body joined by LF, in that order; the comments are ordered by path ascending, then start_line, then line, then side with LEFT before RIGHT, then record id by numeric suffix; the per-comment texts are joined by LF; and the payload hash is the normalised hash per §1.4 of the result.
- The review body is excluded, so embedding the hash in it per §8.4.3 cannot change the value being embedded.
- A test fixes the hash for a known three-comment payload and asserts reordering the input does not change it.

tasks.title: Pre-validate every comment position before posting
tasks.acceptance:
- The GitHub review-creation call is atomic: it either creates the review with all its comments or creates nothing. cr therefore pre-validates every comment position per §8.2 before the call, per §8.4.1.
- A test asserts an invalid position is caught before any network call is attempted.

tasks.title: Report rejected positions with record ids
tasks.acceptance:
- If the call is rejected, no state is marked posted. cr reports every position GitHub named invalid, with the record id it belongs to, and exits 4, per §8.4.2.
- A test asserts findings.ndjson holds no posted state and no triage outcome event after a rejection.

tasks.title: Embed the hash beneath axis disclosure
tasks.acceptance:
- To make a round identifiable after the fact, cr embeds the payload hash as an HTML comment in the review's own body before posting, per §8.4.3.
- Above it the body carries the disclosure of §4.5.4 — the active axes, and the disabled and unavailable ones with their reasons — so the honesty obligation reaches the author and not only the reviewer's terminal.
- The review body is not a line comment and is unaffected by §1.6.1.
- A test asserts both the disclosure and the hash comment appear in the review body.
- §8.4.3's disclosure is every lens of §4.5.4 that did not run, with its reason — not only the disabled and unavailable axes. A skipped role and the unavailable reinvention half reach the author too.

tasks.title: Reconcile an unresolved post by hash
tasks.acceptance:
- If the outcome is unknown — a timeout, a dropped connection, or a response cr cannot parse — cr sets post_unresolved on meta.json and never retries automatically, per §8.4.4.
- cr post <pr> --reconcile lists the PR's reviews, matches the embedded payload hash of §8.4.3, and either adopts that review as posted or clears post_unresolved for a retry. Posting twice is a worse failure than posting late.
- A test simulates a timeout, then reconciles to an adopt and to a clear, asserting the posted index is written only on adopt.

tasks.title: Print the payload without any write
tasks.acceptance:
- cr post without --confirm validates, prints the full payload, reports "posted": false, and exits 0 without any network call, per §8.5.1.
- Validation runs before the confirmation gate. A cr post whose payload fails validation exits 1 whether or not --confirm was given; only a payload that passes validation reaches §8.5.1's exit 0, per §11.2.
- A test asserts a dry run makes no network call and that an invalid payload exits 1 under both flag settings.

tasks.title: Require confirm for every network write
tasks.acceptance:
- Invariant 3: --confirm is required for every network write, on every round, per §8.5.2.
- There is no configuration setting, environment variable, profile field, or alias that removes the gate or supplies --confirm implicitly, per §8.5.3.
- A test attempts to supply the gate through each of the four channels and asserts all four fail.

tasks.title: Report confirmation without claiming human reading
tasks.acceptance:
- cr never claims that a human read the draft. The only fact it can establish is that --confirm was given, and the round summary records exactly that and the payload hash, and nothing more, per §8.5.4.
- cr never reports whether draft.md changed as evidence of human involvement: §8.1.2 requires the agent to rewrite every body before the human sees it, so the file has always changed and the signal measures nothing.
- Any output describing the gate says that confirmation was given, never that the review was read.
- A test greps gate-related output for read-claiming wording and asserts none appears.

tasks.title: Report coverage units with claim mapping
tasks.acceptance:
- cr status <pr> reports units total, units with a complete row of cells, units with gaps, and units flagged oversized per §3.4.5, per §10.1.1.
- It reports claims total, claims mapped to units, and the unimplemented-claim entries of §4.1.3, which appear here and nowhere else because they are never posted, per §10.1.2. This includes the surviving set-aside stamp count required by the §4.1.7 carry-forward rule.
- It reports active axes, disabled and unavailable axes with reasons, and skipped roles with reasons per §4.5.4, per §10.1.3.
- A test asserts all three sections against a fixture holding an oversized unit, a gap entry, and a skipped role.
- §10.1.3 reports active axes and every lens of §4.5.4 that did not run, with its reason.
- Carried from oversized-unit-split: internal/unit records Cluster.Oversized per §3.4.5, but nothing renders it. The coverage report is where an oversized unit must appear as such, so a reader knows the cap did not bind there.

tasks.title: Report findings by state with probes
tasks.acceptance:
- cr status reports findings and questions by state, severity, and grade, per §10.1.4.
- It reports probes run, and probes that changed a finding's grade, per §10.1.5.
- It reports waivers applied and duplicates suppressed in the current round, per §10.1.6 — an honesty disclosure that survives --quiet per §11.1.
- It reports notes retracted in the current round per the §3.6.6 same-round rule.

tasks.title: Decide completeness from four conditions
tasks.acceptance:
- A round is complete when all four §10.2 conditions hold: the current head equals the head the round was recorded against per §9.3.1; every unit has a complete row of cells for every active role, and every one of those cells was filled for that unit's current unit hash per §3.4.6; every claim is mapped to at least one unit; and no record of the current round remains in draft or queued.
- A claim carrying an unimplemented-claim entry per §4.1.3 blocks completeness until it is either mapped, or set aside through cr claims set-aside per §4.1.8. The entry is not a record, so §10.2.4 never reaches it; this condition is the only thing that makes an unimplemented claim block, which is what §4.1.3 relies on.
- A test asserts each of the four conditions blocks independently.

tasks.title: Print the verdict beside missing lenses
tasks.acceptance:
- cr status prints the completeness verdict and, when it is false, the exact reason, per §10.2.
- A verdict of complete is printed together with every lens of §4.5.4 that did not run, because completeness across three axes is not completeness across four, and neither is completeness with a role that never looked.
- cr never approves the PR, and never describes a complete round as a settled review: v0.1 ends at posting, and whether the author addressed anything is outside what it can observe.
- A test asserts a complete verdict carries the missing-lens list and that no approval or settled wording is reachable.

tasks.title: Assign every summary count a writer
tasks.acceptance:
- cr merge, cr draft, and cr post each accumulate their own counts into rounds/<n>/summary.json, which is created by cr merge and finalised by cr post, per §10.3.
- Every round records counts for raised, deduplicated, suppressed by thread, waived, forced to question, drafted, posted, discarded as not-here, and discarded as wrong, plus the comment count against post.max_comments per §1.6.2, the probe cap state, and the payload hash of §8.3.3 — so the history of a review is reconstructable from state alone.
- Round 8 finding unassigned-writer: cr record is added to the writer list and assigned the deduplicated and thread-suppressed counts, since it is what stamps duplicate from duplicate_of per §6.4.3 and writes state suppressed per §3.5.4 — cr merge emits duplicate_of but never stamps state, and cr draft and cr post see only queued records.
- Round 8 finding missing-summary-count: the §9.3.6 already-posted drop count is a distinct key, kept separate from waived so the two suppression reasons stay distinguishable in the reconstructable history §10.3 promises.
- A test asserts every listed count has a named writer and that a shape assertion over summary.json passes.

tasks.title: Replace summary sections rather than accumulating
tasks.acceptance:
- Round 8 finding non-idempotent-accumulation: each writing command replaces its own section of summary.json on every invocation rather than adding to it, so the file is a function of current state and re-running a command is idempotent. Which keys belong to which writer is stated, mirroring §10.3's writer list.
- None of the writers is once-per-round: §7.1.6 contemplates regenerating the draft, §8.5.1 makes a dry run the normal precursor to cr post --confirm, and re-running cr merge after fixing one role's output is the obvious recovery path. Additive accumulation would inflate the waived, deduplicated, and drafted counts, making the round summary the one place where re-running a command silently changes the record.
- A test runs cr merge twice, cr draft twice, and cr post twice, and asserts every count is unchanged from the single-run case.

tasks.title: Record the payload hash once built
tasks.acceptance:
- Round 8 finding unpostable-round-summary: the payload hash is recorded only once cr post --confirm has built a payload and is absent otherwise, and an unfinalised summary is a valid terminal state for a round. A round that is drafted and never posted, or run only through §8.5.1's dry run, has no posted payload, and whether the key is absent, null, or holds the dry-run hash was undetermined.
- A test asserts an unposted round's summary omits the key entirely and still validates.

tasks.title: Document the full loop in skill
tasks.acceptance:
- skills/cr/SKILL.md ships with the release and documents the full loop: brief, review fan-out, merge, record, probe, draft, human read, post — and that v0.1 stops there, so a moved head means a new round per §9.3, per §13.1.
- It documents the argued rule, that it cannot be overridden, and when to escalate to a probe instead of asserting, per §13.2.
- It documents that every network write needs --confirm, that cr cannot prove the human read the draft, and that the human is therefore the one who must, per §13.4.
- It documents that citations is the machine-readable evidence field and evidence is prose, so a finding without citations is graded argued and posted as a question, per §13.7.
- It documents the comment economy of §1.6: fewer comments, each anchored to the line it concerns, per §13.8.

tasks.title: Document triage verbs with marker semantics
tasks.acceptance:
- SKILL.md documents the draft triage verbs, the marker edit semantics of §7.2, and the difference between discarding as wrong — a marker edit, repository-wide, counted against the class — and as not-here, which is plain deletion, scoped to the pull request, and counted separately, per §13.3.
- It documents the role, profile, and rule file formats, and how to add each, per §13.5.
- It documents that a comment written by hand more than twice belongs in the rule corpus, with a detect block when the violation is mechanically matchable, per §13.6.
- A test asserts SKILL.md names every command of §11.

tasks.title: Depend only on three external commands
tasks.acceptance:
- cr builds as a single binary whose only runtime dependencies are git, gh, and the configured tracker command, per §14.1.
- A test asserts the binary runs with no other executable on PATH beyond those three.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/cli/dependencies_test.go TestTheRunnersStartNothingButGitAndGh parses the two runner files that nowrite_test.go already confines os/exec to, and asserts each one names its program as a plain string literal, internal/git/run.go starting git and internal/gh/run.go starting gh, one invocation each. That closes what an import scan cannot see, because a call naming a variable reads the same to it as a call naming a literal, and a fourth dependency added inside a runner would therefore pass it untouched. crBinary makes the single-binary half a fact rather than a reading, one go build of ./cmd/cr producing one regular file, and that file is what the second criterion runs. The tracker is the third dependency and is treated differently on purpose, because §3.1.1 makes it argv the user configures and §3.1.4 lets --intent-file replace it outright.
- TestTheBinaryRunsWithNothingButGitAndGhOnPath runs that binary on a PATH of one directory holding a symlink to git, a symlink to gh and nothing else, with the directory listing asserted to be exactly those two names, and exercises --version, --help, every registered command with --help, cr init and cr config, in an environment carrying only PATH, HOME, TMPDIR and CR_HOME, the allowlist internal/git and internal/gh had already settled on. jira, the §3.1.2 default tracker, is installed on this machine and deliberately absent from that PATH, and cr config prints the default argv naming it while it stays unreachable, which is what makes the default a default rather than a dependency of every command. Run by hand, that PATH cannot resolve even sh, so the strip is total.

tasks.title: Release archives through GoReleaser on tags
tasks.acceptance:
- Releases are produced by GoReleaser on a v* tag via .github/workflows/release.yml, publishing archives for darwin and linux on both amd64 and arm64, per §14.2.
- go install github.com/deligoez/cr/cmd/cr@<tag> installs the same version as the tag, per §14.4.
- A dry-run GoReleaser build produces all four archives.
tasks.closed_reason:
- .github/workflows/release.yml fires on a push of a v* tag and nothing else, and its goreleaser-action step runs release --clean, so a tag is the only thing that publishes. .goreleaser.yml's one build matrix is now darwin and linux across amd64 and arm64 exactly, the windows entry the pre-spec scaffolding carried having gone with the zip format_overrides that existed only for it. TestAVersionTagIsWhatTriggersARelease pins the trigger and the release verb, and TestTheBuildMatrixIsExactlyTheFourTheSpecNames asserts both sets by ElementsMatch rather than by containment, so adding a platform fails as loudly as losing one, verified by putting windows back and watching it fail. The before-hooks were raised from go test ./... to the gate verbatim, with the release runner installing golangci-lint and deadcode, because a tag is the one moment a mistake cannot be taken back.
- Section 14.4's install path resolves to the module path plus the package directory, and TestTheReleaseBinaryIsTheOneGoInstallNames asserts every half of it, that go.mod declares module github.com/deligoez/cr, that the build's main is ./cmd/cr, and that its binary is cr, so the package go install fetches at a tag and the package GoReleaser builds at that tag are the same one. The version half is asserted where this task can reach it, that the ldflags carry -X github.com/deligoez/cr/internal/cli.version={{.Version}}, the variable root.go prints. go version -m on the archived darwin/arm64 binary confirms both, path github.com/deligoez/cr/cmd/cr and the -X flag applied, and the extracted binary printed cr version 0.0.0-SNAPSHOT-befaac8.
- goreleaser release --snapshot --clean --skip=publish --skip=announce produced exactly four archives and no others, macOS_x86_64.tar.gz, macOS_arm64.tar.gz, linux_x86_64.tar.gz and linux_arm64.tar.gz, down from the six the same command produced before the change. The strengthened before-hooks ran inside that run, all three gate steps passing, and TestEveryGateStepRunsInCIAndAtRelease now derives those steps from the tasks.json quality_gate string rather than restating them, so a future gate change fails until the hooks and the CI workflow both carry it. Mutation testing held at the baseline, Killed 305, Lived 5, efficacy 98.39 percent, unchanged because this unit adds no branching Go code.

Out of scope: section 14.3's Homebrew formula belongs to homebrew-formula, and goreleaser check reports the existing brews block as deprecated in favour of homebrew_casks, which that task should settle. Section 14.5's manifest belongs to skill-marketplace-manifest. Section 14.6 belongs to version-injection, which also owns a real gap this task could only measure, that go install applies no ldflags, so an installed binary prints cr version dev unless root.go falls back to runtime/debug.ReadBuildInfo, whose main module version does carry the tag.

tasks.title: Publish the Homebrew formula on release
tasks.acceptance:
- A release updates the Homebrew formula in the deligoez/homebrew-tap repository so that brew install deligoez/tap/cr installs the binary as cr, per §14.3.
- The formula is published by the release workflow, not by hand.
- Measured by goreleaser-release, assigned here: goreleaser check fails with "DEPRECATED: brews should not be used anymore", so .goreleaser.yml's brews block must migrate to homebrew_casks; goreleaser check exits 0 afterwards and a snapshot run still produces the four §14.2 archives.

tasks.title: Inject the tagged version at build
tasks.acceptance:
- cr --version prints the tagged version, injected at build time via -X github.com/deligoez/cr/internal/cli.version, per §14.6.
- A test asserts an unset version renders as a development marker rather than an empty string.
- Measured by goreleaser-release, assigned here: go install applies no ldflags, so go install github.com/deligoez/cr/cmd/cr@<tag> yields "cr version dev" and §14.4 is unmet by the -X path alone. The buildinfo mod line does carry the tag, so internal/cli reads runtime/debug.ReadBuildInfo() as a fallback when the injected version is unset, and a test drives a real go install to assert the tag reaches cr --version.

tasks.title: Expose the skill through the manifest
tasks.acceptance:
- The skill ships inside this repository at skills/cr/SKILL.md, and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json exposes it as an installable plugin, per §14.5.
- A test asserts the manifest's declared skill path exists.

tasks.title: Record a round's merged findings
tasks.acceptance:
- cr record <pr> <file> reads the merged NDJSON, validates every line through internal/finding's Decode, and appends the surviving records to findings.ndjson under the per-PR lock, per §11's command table and §9.1's new-record-to-draft transition.
- Validation is the existing one rather than a second copy: a missing required field, an unknown unit, or a borrowed role is refused with exit code 1 naming the file, the one-based line, and the field, and nothing is written when any line is refused.
- A test drives a good file and a file whose third line is bad, asserting the first writes every record and the second writes none and names line 3.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr record <pr> <file> is registered in internal/cli/record.go and root.go: it reads the NDJSON the agent names, hands every line to internal/finding's Decode with the current round's unit ids, stamps §9.1's draft state through MayTransition(Creation -> StateDraft, ActorRecord), and appends the survivors to findings.ndjson under layout.LockPR, per §11's command table and §9.1's first transition row.
- Validation is finding.Decode's and nothing else: TestRecordRefusesTheThreeFaultsSection613Names drives a missing required field, a unit belonging to the round before, and a role borrowed from another role's §4.6.2 output file, and asserts each arrives as the same finding.RejectedRecordError carrying the file, the one-based line and the field, mapped by internal/cli/exit.go onto exit code 1.
- Nothing is written when any line is refused, and that is atomicity by construction rather than rollback: Decode returns no records at all on the first fault, so the single state.AppendStamped publish never runs. TestARefusedLineLeavesFindingsExactlyAsItWas records a round first, then hands in a four-line file whose third line drops evidence, and asserts the error names line 3 and that findings.ndjson is byte-identical afterwards, so neither the two good lines above the fault nor the good line below it were stored.
- TestRecordStoresEveryRecordOfAnAcceptedFile drives the good file and asserts every record reached findings.ndjson in file order, each carrying the three fields the agent may not supply: state draft (§6.1.4), and the head and round of meta.json (§2.3.3).
- state.AppendStamped was added because WriteStamped restamps every record it is handed, which would rewrite earlier rounds' head and round on every append; TestAnAppendLeavesEarlierRoundsAsTheyWere holds the first round's stamp across a second append, per §9.3.5.
- The unit set is scoped to the round because §3.4.6 makes a unit id round-scoped, so roundUnitIDs filters units.ndjson by meta.json's round and a record naming the previous round's unit is refused.
- Dogfooded against a scratch CR_HOME with a hand-written merged.ndjson: two records stored with state, head and round written by cr; refusals for a bad third line, an out-of-round unit and a supplied grade all exit 1 leaving the file byte-identical.

tasks.title: Detect the repository from its remote
tasks.acceptance:
- cr derives owner/repo from the repository under review, so §11.1's --repo is an override rather than the only source, and every PR-scoped command works without it.
- The remote is read through internal/git's pinned runner, never a second exec path, and a repository with no remote, several remotes, or a non-GitHub remote is refused with a named next step rather than a guess.
- A test covers detection from an ssh remote and an https remote, the --repo override winning over both, and each refusal.

tasks.title: Reject a class that is not kebab-case
tasks.acceptance:
- Found by record-command's dogfood run: finding.ValidateClass exists but Decode never calls it, so cr record stores a class like "Not Kebab" without complaint.
- Every door that admits a record rejects a class outside [a-z0-9-]+ with exit code 1, naming the file, the one-based line and the field.
- §6.4's dedup key is built from the class, so a non-canonical class silently splits one group in two; the guard belongs at the door, not at the key.

tasks.title: Exit 3 on input a command cannot read
tasks.acceptance:
- Found by record-command's dogfood run: a missing input file, or a pull request with no state directory, exits 2 rather than §11.2's 3, because os.ReadFile and state.ReadPR return bare errors that exitCodeFor does not map.
- A shared unreadable-input error type carries the path and maps to ExitFile, so every command that reads a caller-named file answers the same way.
- Exit 2 stays what §11.2 says it is: the command line was wrong, not the file.

tasks.title: Refuse to blank a recorded issue key
tasks.acceptance:
- Found by brief-payload's dogfood run: a cr brief whose intent.key_pattern no longer matches silently rewrites meta.json's issue_key to empty, orphaning every claim already recorded under the old key, since §3.3 forms each claim id as <ISSUE-KEY>#c<n>.
- A brief that would replace a non-empty recorded issue key with a different one, or with none, refuses with exit code 4 and a hint, rather than writing.
- A test records claims under one key, then briefs again with a pattern that matches nothing, and asserts meta.json and claims.ndjson are both untouched.
- Also found by dogfooding: with a tracker-backed profile, cr brief runs the tracker command and fails on a 404 before --intent-file can help, and the error never says --issue is what would have avoided it. The message names it.

tasks.title: Destroy a sandbox whose registration is gone
tasks.acceptance:
- Found by baseline-resolution's dogfood run: when the repository under review has been re-cloned or force-pushed, git worktree remove fails with "is not a working tree" and cr sandbox create then refuses because the directory exists, leaving no way out of cr but rm -rf under ~/.cr by hand.
- cr sandbox destroy falls back to removing the sandbox directory when the registration is already gone, so §5.1.5 has no state it cannot clear.
- A test registers a worktree, removes the registration behind cr's back, and asserts destroy still leaves nothing and that create afterwards succeeds.

tasks.title: Test the mapping package where its mutants can die
tasks.acceptance: internal/mapping carries its own test file; today it has none, and gremlins reports all five of its mutants NOT COVERED because default-mode gremlins runs only the mutated package own tests, so nothing in that package can ever be killed. The package is load-bearing: 4.1.1, 4.1.2, 4.1.3 and 4.2.1 all read this one join, and 4.1.6 forbids any second opinion about which claim covers which unit. The tests drive its decode and its refusals directly rather than through internal/cli, so a defect is named at the file that holds it. A gremlins run scoped to ./internal/mapping reports zero NOT COVERED mutants, and every surviving mutant is classified in the closure reason.

tasks.title: Refuse a force-named setting the way argued and forcing are refused
tasks.acceptance: config.protectedTokens holds argued and forcing but not force, so a name like CR_POST_FORCE_FINDINGS is not refused by name even though the deny-list comment claims a setting that would override 6.3 cannot be addressed. It is inert today because fromEnv maps only known keys, so it overrides nothing; the gap is that the list is one synonym short of what it says about itself, and the next reader tests the claim rather than the list. Adding force needs carriers entries for enforce, reinforce and workforce, so the change is not a one-line addition and a test drives each carrier through unrefused. Found by argued-forcing-unoverridable, whose unit left it rather than editing a closed task with that blast radius.

tasks.title: Hand the head symbol index to hunk clustering
tasks.acceptance: brief/brief.go calls unit.Clusters with a nil SymbolIndex on every run, so the symbol branch of hunk clustering never runs outside tests and every pull request clusters by adjacency alone. The nil was deliberate while no index existed; internal/unit/symbols.go says so, calling a nil index every run until the head symbol index exists. symbol-index-build has since built that index, and nothing handed it over. It does not satisfy unit.SymbolIndex yet: Indexed can be answered, but Enclosing needs the span each symbol covers, and the index records only the line a symbol is declared on. The index gains the spans or an adapter derives them, cr brief passes the built index where it now passes nil, and a file the index cannot serve still falls through to adjacency without an error. A test drives cr brief over a diff whose hunks sit inside one function and asserts they form one unit by symbol, where adjacency alone would split them.
